human-capital-social-development-officer.explanation: The National ECD Policy objectives cover school readiness, positive parenting, reduced malnutrition and stunting, reduced under-5 and maternal mortality, child protection and inclusion of children with special needs; the other options are partial or false (diseases 'cannot' affect them, pre-primary 'not necessary').

human-capital-social-development-officer.section: Early Childhood Development and school feeding
human-capital-social-development-officer.stem: Early Childhood Development (ECD) targets children aged:
human-capital-social-development-officer.explanation: Rwanda's ECD policy and the National Early Childhood Development Programme target children aged 0 to 6 years.

human-capital-social-development-officer.section: Early Childhood Development and school feeding
human-capital-social-development-officer.stem: Stunting is:
options: Low height-for-age caused by long-term malnutrition
human-capital-social-development-officer.explanation: Stunting is low height-for-age resulting from chronic malnutrition.

human-capital-social-development-officer.section: Early Childhood Development and school feeding
human-capital-social-development-officer.stem: ECD centres (Ingo Mbonezamikurire) aim to:
options: Care for young children and prepare them for school
human-capital-social-development-officer.explanation: Rwanda's ECD policy provides care and early learning for children from conception to age 6 and aims to increase children's preparedness for primary school.

human-capital-social-development-officer.section: Early Childhood Development and school feeding
human-capital-social-development-officer.stem: Stunting in children means low:
human-capital-social-development-officer.explanation: Stunting is low height-for-age; wasting is low weight-for-height.

human-capital-social-development-officer.section: Early Childhood Development and school feeding
human-capital-social-development-officer.stem: Which is a component of nurturing care in ECD?
human-capital-social-development-officer.explanation: The Nurturing Care Framework has five components: good health, adequate nutrition, responsive caregiving, safety and security, and opportunities for early learning.

human-capital-social-development-officer.section: Early Childhood Development and school feeding
human-capital-social-development-officer.stem: The Rwanda Demographic and Health Survey 2019-20 has shown that children under age 5 are stunted at:
human-capital-social-development-officer.explanation: The RDHS 2019-20 found that 33 percent of Rwandan children under five are stunted (9 percent severely), so none of 28, 31 or 32 percent is right.

human-capital-social-development-officer.topic: Early Childhood Development and school feeding
human-capital-social-development-officer.section: Early Childhood Development and school feeding
human-capital-social-development-officer.stem: What is the area of Rwanda?
human-capital-social-development-officer.explanation: NISR gives Rwanda's surface area as 26,338 square kilometres (24,210 km2 land plus 2,120 km2 water and swamps).

human-capital-social-development-officer.section: Early Childhood Development and school feeding
human-capital-social-development-officer.stem: Rwanda joined the African Union on ......
human-capital-social-development-officer.explanation: Rwanda is listed by the African Union as a member since 25 May 1963, the founding date of the OAU that became the AU in 2002.

human-capital-social-development-officer.section: Data collection, reporting and information management
human-capital-social-development-officer.stem: According to the fifth Rwanda Population and Housing Census (RPHC5), the life expectancy at birth in Rwanda in 2022 was:
human-capital-social-development-officer.explanation: RPHC5 gives life expectancy at birth of 69.6 years in 2022 (67.7 for males, 71.2 for females, 64 in 2012). 64, 67.7 and 71.2 are not the national 2022 figure, so "None is correct" is right.

human-capital-social-development-officer.section: Data collection, reporting and information management
human-capital-social-development-officer.stem: According to the multidimensional child poverty report (EICV5), child poverty is:
human-capital-social-development-officer.explanation: The EICV5 Multidimensional Child Poverty (MODA) report finds that 32.7% of children under 18 in Rwanda are multidimensionally poor, deprived in at least three dimensions at once.

human-capital-social-development-officer.section: Data collection, reporting and information management
human-capital-social-development-officer.stem: According to the EICV5 multidimensional child poverty report, the percentage of children who are multidimensionally poor (child poverty) is:
human-capital-social-development-officer.explanation: NISR EICV5 Multidimensional Child Poverty Report (MODA) finds that 32.7% of children under 18 are multidimensionally poor (deprived in at least three dimensions).

human-capital-social-development-officer.section: Data collection, reporting and information management
human-capital-social-development-officer.stem: According to the 2023/24 Integrated Household Living Conditions Survey (EICV7), the total poverty line per adult per year in Rwanda is set at:
human-capital-social-development-officer.explanation: NISR EICV7 sets the total poverty line at RWF 560,127 per adult per year (Jan 2024 prices); 356,432 is the extreme (food) line and 159,375 was the 2014 total line.

human-capital-social-development-officer.section: Data collection, reporting and information management
human-capital-social-development-officer.stem: According to the 2023/24 Integrated Household Living Conditions Survey (EICV7), the national literacy rate among young adults (aged 15-24) in Rwanda is ....; the national net attendance rate in primary is ....; the net attendance rate in secondary is ....; and the Province with the highest net attendance rate in primary is:
human-capital-social-development-officer.explanation: EICV7: literacy 15-24 is 87.7%, primary NAR 92.8%, secondary NAR 33.7%, and the highest provincial primary NAR is Northern Province (96.1%), not City of Kigali (95.2%).

human-capital-social-development-officer.topic: Community mobilisation on education and literacy
human-capital-social-development-officer.section: Community mobilisation on education and literacy
human-capital-social-development-officer.stem: The community development policy builds on which among the following specific opportunities?
options: Declining capacity at the grass-roots level
human-capital-social-development-officer.explanation: The policy lists 'Emerging community-based development initiatives' as one of its specific opportunities. The first option is a truncated version of 'Increasing capacity at the grass-roots level', which is also listed, and the community is established at Umudugudu (Village) level, not Cell level.

human-capital-social-development-officer.topic: Community mobilisation on education and literacy
human-capital-social-development-officer.section: Community mobilisation on education and literacy
human-capital-social-development-officer.stem: What are the three broad community development objectives at the core community level?
options: Economic Development, social welfare and Security
Economic Development, Social development and political development
Economic Development, good health and good governance
Economic Development, Social development and good governance
human-capital-social-development-officer.explanation: The Community Development Policy defines objectives across three inter-linked spheres: economic development, social development and good governance.

human-capital-social-development-officer.topic: Community mobilisation on education and literacy
human-capital-social-development-officer.section: Community mobilisation on education and literacy
human-capital-social-development-officer.stem: Umugoroba w'Ababyeyi (Parents' Evening Forum) is used to:
options: Address family issues, child upbringing and village solidarity
human-capital-social-development-officer.explanation: Umugoroba w'Ababyeyi is a village-level forum where parents discuss and resolve family conflicts, gender-based violence, children's schooling and upbringing, and build community togetherness.

human-capital-social-development-officer.topic: Community mobilisation on education and literacy
human-capital-social-development-officer.section: Community mobilisation on education and literacy
human-capital-social-development-officer.stem: Which of the following contribute to reducing infectious diseases in the community?
options: Hand and personal hygiene, food hygiene and safe disposal of faeces
human-capital-social-development-officer.explanation: Hand and personal hygiene, food hygiene and safe disposal of faeces all reduce transmission of infectious diseases.

human-capital-social-development-officer.section: Data collection, reporting and information management
human-capital-social-development-officer.stem: According to the fifth Rwanda Population and Housing Census, what was the adult literacy rate in Rwanda in 2022?
human-capital-social-development-officer.explanation: RPHC5 found that 79% of the resident population aged 15 and above can read and write with understanding in any language. 89.3% is the primary net attendance rate.

human-capital-social-development-officer.section: Data collection, reporting and information management
human-capital-social-development-officer.stem: The Rwanda Governance Scorecard (RGS) 9th edition is built on how many pillars, indicators and variables?
human-capital-social-development-officer.explanation: RGB states that the eight pillars and 35 indicators were kept in the 10th edition while variables rose from 144 (9th edition) to 151.

human-capital-social-development-officer.topic: Community mobilisation on education and literacy
human-capital-social-development-officer.section: Community mobilisation on education and literacy
human-capital-social-development-officer.stem: ...... is responsible for putting in place strategies to mobilize the citizens on their participation in interventions meant for them and accountability in respect thereof.
options: Office of the President of the Republic
human-capital-social-development-officer.explanation: This is item 9 of the Rwanda Governance Board's core mandate, under its establishing law.

human-capital-social-development-officer.section: Community mobilisation on education and literacy
human-capital-social-development-officer.stem: The EAC comprises ... Partner States.
human-capital-social-development-officer.explanation: Somalia became the 8th Partner State on 4 March 2024, joining Burundi, DRC, Kenya, Rwanda, South Sudan, Tanzania and Uganda.

human-capital-social-development-officer.topic: Community mobilisation on education and literacy
human-capital-social-development-officer.section: Community mobilisation on education and literacy
human-capital-social-development-officer.stem: What are the last three countries to join the Commonwealth?
human-capital-social-development-officer.explanation: Rwanda joined in 2009, then Gabon and Togo in June 2022; no later member is listed.

human-capital-social-development-officer.section: Community mobilisation on education and literacy
human-capital-social-development-officer.stem: The NST1 targets are ambitious but achievable. Realising these targets requires some conditions:
options: Strengthening partnership among key stakeholders and enhancing accountability at all levels
Strengthening collaboration and partnership among all stakeholders and enhancing ownership at all levels
Building strong partnership and collaboration among key stakeholders and accountability at all levels
human-capital-social-development-officer.explanation: The Prime Minister's foreword says the targets are ambitious but achievable and realizing them requires strengthening collaboration and partnership among all stakeholders and enhancing ownership at all levels.

human-capital-social-development-officer.section: Community mobilisation on education and literacy
human-capital-social-development-officer.stem: Rwanda's ambition to become a developed country hinges on its ability to enhance competitiveness at macro and micro levels. Rwanda is targeting to:
options: Belong to the top 20 countries in doing business in 2035 and maintain the status; rank among the top 20 economies in competitiveness by 2035 and top 10 in 2050
Belong to the top 10 countries in doing business in 2035 and maintain the status; rank among the top 20 economies in competitiveness by 2035 and top 10 in 2050
Belong to the top 5 countries in doing business in 2035 and maintain the status; rank among the top 20 economies in competitiveness by 2035 and top 10 in 2050
Belong to the top 3 countries in doing business in 2035 and maintain the status; rank among the top 20 economies in competitiveness by 2035 and top 10 in 2050
human-capital-social-development-officer.explanation: Under the Competitiveness and Integration pillar, Vision 2050 targets a place among the top 10 countries in doing business in 2035, top 20 economies in competitiveness by 2035 and top 10 in 2050.

human-capital-social-development-officer.stem: What makes you an effective problem solver?
human-capital-social-development-officer.explanation: Effective problem solvers are systematic and logical in how they analyse a problem; presentation, speaking and proposal writing are communication skills, not problem-solving ones.

human-capital-social-development-officer.stem: The macroeconomic framework for NST1 requires an average GDP growth over the NST1 period for the country to remain on its path of economic transformation. What is that average?
human-capital-social-development-officer.explanation: NST1 states an average GDP growth of 9.1% is needed over 2017-2024.

human-capital-social-development-officer.stem: After the 1994 Genocide against the Tutsi, Rwanda made a choice of three things. What are the three choices that Rwanda adopted?
options: Staying together, being accountable and thinking big
Education for all, Ndi Umunyarwanda and agriculture
human-capital-social-development-officer.explanation: Vision 2050 describes Rwanda's post-genocide 'triple choice': staying together, being accountable and thinking big.

human-capital-social-development-officer.stem: NST1 considered seven (7) cross-cutting areas to attain inclusive and sustainable development. Which of the following is among the seven cross-cutting areas?
human-capital-social-development-officer.explanation: The NST cross-cutting areas are capacity development, HIV/AIDS and NCDs, disability and social inclusion, environment and climate change, regional integration and international positioning, gender and family promotion, and disaster management.

human-capital-social-development-officer.section: Early Childhood Development and school feeding
human-capital-social-development-officer.stem: NST1 covered a seven-year period, namely:
human-capital-social-development-officer.explanation: The National Strategy for Transformation (NST1) was the 7 Years Government Programme for 2017-2024.

human-capital-social-development-officer.section: Early Childhood Development and school feeding
human-capital-social-development-officer.stem: The NST1 macroeconomic framework requires an average GDP growth over the NST1 period of:
human-capital-social-development-officer.explanation: NST1 states an average GDP growth of 9.1% is needed over 2017-2024.

human-capital-social-development-officer.section: Early Childhood Development and school feeding
human-capital-social-development-officer.stem: Results-based performance management respects phases. How many?
human-capital-social-development-officer.explanation: Art 4 of Law 18/2017: results-based performance management respects five (5) phases (planning, budgeting, implementation, monitoring, evaluation). Five is not Six, Seven or Eight, so "None of the mentioned" is correct.

human-capital-social-development-officer.section: Early Childhood Development and school feeding
human-capital-social-development-officer.stem: When was the Imihigo performance contract started in local government?
human-capital-social-development-officer.explanation: Imihigo started in 2006 with district performance contracts.

human-capital-social-development-officer.section: Early Childhood Development and school feeding
human-capital-social-development-officer.stem: When were the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) adopted?
human-capital-social-development-officer.explanation: The 2030 Agenda with its Sustainable Development Goals was adopted by world leaders at the UN in September 2015.

human-capital-social-development-officer.section: Data collection, reporting and information management
human-capital-social-development-officer.stem: According to the previous (latest) census, the population of Rwanda is:
human-capital-social-development-officer.explanation: The 5th Population and Housing Census (August 2022) enumerated 13,246,394 residents.

human-capital-social-development-officer.section: Data collection, reporting and information management
human-capital-social-development-officer.stem: Which of the following is an example of an output indicator?
options: Number of households that received cows under Girinka
human-capital-social-development-officer.explanation: An output indicator counts direct deliverables of an activity, such as households that received cows; the others are outcome or impact-level.

human-capital-social-development-officer.section: Community mobilisation on education and literacy
human-capital-social-development-officer.stem: According to the 5th Rwanda Population and Housing Census (RPHC5), what is the adult (15 years and above) literacy rate in 2022?
human-capital-social-development-officer.explanation: About 79% (6.5 million) of the 8.2 million adults aged 15+ can read and write with understanding in any language.

human-capital-social-development-officer.section: Community mobilisation on education and literacy
human-capital-social-development-officer.stem: Which of these is a pillar of NST1?
human-capital-social-development-officer.explanation: NST1 (2017-2024) had three pillars: Economic Transformation, Social Transformation and Transformational Governance.

human-capital-social-development-officer.stem: How many categories of social health insurance exist?
human-capital-social-development-officer.explanation: Article 7 of Law 48/2015 says social health insurance consists of three categories: insurance provided by public entities, community-based health insurance schemes, and insurance provided by health insurance associations. 4, 6 and 5 are all wrong.

human-capital-social-development-officer.stem: From the experience of COVID-19, all Rwandans are well versed in good handwashing practice. What are the benefits of this practice?
options: Prevent the spread of infectious diseases, save lives, save money, prepare the future
To be able to shake the hands of the people you meet
To be able to eat with your hands safely
human-capital-social-development-officer.explanation: Handwashing with soap prevents infections and so saves lives and health costs; the other options are not the public-health purpose.

human-capital-social-development-officer.stem: The "First 1,000 Days" covers the period:
options: From conception until the child is 2 years old
human-capital-social-development-officer.explanation: The first 1,000 days run from conception until the child's second birthday.

human-capital-social-development-officer.stem: How many Community Health Workers (CHWs) serve each village?
human-capital-social-development-officer.explanation: Each Rwandan village has three CHWs: a male-female pair (binome) and a maternal health worker (ASM).

human-capital-social-development-officer.stem: The Rwanda Demographic and Health Survey (RDHS) 2019-20 showed that children under age 5 are stunted at:
human-capital-social-development-officer.explanation: RDHS 2019-20 final report: 33% of children under 5 are stunted (9% severely). 33% is not 28%, 32% or 31%.

human-capital-social-development-officer.stem: The Economic and Human Capital Development Officer is responsible for monitoring the implementation of interventions related to health, hygiene and sanitation at Cell level. Concerning the validity of contribution to the Community-Based Health Insurance scheme (CBHI) and the categories of its members, which statement is correct?
options: A member who joins for the first time the Community-Based Health Insurance scheme starts benefiting from medical services immediately if he/she has paid for the whole household before 30th September; Ordinary Members & Honorary Members

A member who joins for the first time the Community-Based Health Insurance scheme and who has paid for the whole household shall wait for one month after payment of his/her subscription fees before benefiting from medical services; Ordinary Members & Honorary Members
The member who renews his/her insurance continues to receive medical care services for thirty days upon expiry of the insurance; Ordinary Members
The member who renews his/her insurance continues to receive medical care services for three months upon expiry of the insurance; Honorary Members
human-capital-social-development-officer.explanation: Under Law 03/2015 as amended by Law 70/2018, households that pay the whole contribution by 30 September benefit directly, and the member categories are ordinary and honorary members. Option C gives only one category and D has a wrong period.

human-capital-social-development-officer.stem: Choose the false response: The Economic and Human Capital Development Officer is responsible for monitoring the implementation of interventions related to health, hygiene and sanitation at Cell level. The improved sanitation consists of:
options: A pit latrine without a slab
A pit latrine with a constructed floor slab
human-capital-social-development-officer.explanation: A pit latrine without a slab is classified as unimproved sanitation; flush toilets, VIP latrines and pit latrines with a slab are improved.

human-capital-social-development-officer.stem: Early initiation of breastfeeding means breastfeeding:
options: within the first hour after birth
human-capital-social-development-officer.explanation: WHO and UNICEF recommend that infants initiate breastfeeding within one hour of birth.

human-capital-social-development-officer.stem: Which of the following is a benefit of breastfeeding?
options: It replaces the need for all vaccination
human-capital-social-development-officer.explanation: Breast milk gives antibodies (immunity) and nutrition for growth, and strengthens the mother-child bond, so all three listed items are benefits.

human-capital-social-development-officer.section: Youth, gender, disability and inclusion programmes
human-capital-social-development-officer.stem: Fill in the missing: The ......... monitors how the national gender policy is implemented in all spheres of national development.
human-capital-social-development-officer.explanation: The Gender Monitoring Office is the national "watchdog" that evaluates compliance with gender indicators on a permanent basis across national development.

human-capital-social-development-officer.section: Youth, gender, disability and inclusion programmes
human-capital-social-development-officer.stem: The Government of Rwanda's commitment to gender and to combating gender-based violence is also manifested through the establishment of the following "Gender machineries":
human-capital-social-development-officer.explanation: The National Gender Machinery is made up of institutions such as the Ministry of Gender and Family Promotion, the Gender Monitoring Office and the National Women Council. District councils, courts and security organs are not gender machineries.

human-capital-social-development-officer.section: Youth, gender, disability and inclusion programmes
human-capital-social-development-officer.stem: What does GBV mean in full words?
human-capital-social-development-officer.explanation: GBV stands for gender-based violence, the term used throughout the National Policy against GBV.

human-capital-social-development-officer.section: Youth, gender, disability and inclusion programmes
human-capital-social-development-officer.stem: Most of the delinquent behaviours are never deliberately committed by sober minded individuals of the Rwandan society; rather, there are historical and environmental factors behind the said incidences. The following are major causes of delinquency:
options: Poverty, unemployment and low level of education
human-capital-social-development-officer.explanation: The National Rehabilitation Service names family breakdown/dysfunctional parenting, violence (victimisation), drug and substance abuse, poverty, unemployment and low education/skills as major causes of delinquency, so all three listed groups are causes and "All are correct" is right.

human-capital-social-development-officer.section: Youth, gender, disability and inclusion programmes
human-capital-social-development-officer.stem: Isange One Stop Centres help:
options: Victims of gender-based violence (GBV) access all services in one place
human-capital-social-development-officer.explanation: Isange One Stop Centres provide medical, psychosocial, police and legal services for GBV and child abuse victims in one place, free of charge.

human-capital-social-development-officer.section: Youth, gender, disability and inclusion programmes
human-capital-social-development-officer.stem: GBV stands for:
human-capital-social-development-officer.explanation: GBV is Gender-Based Violence, defined in Law 59/2008 on prevention and punishment of gender-based violence.

human-capital-social-development-officer.section: Youth, gender, disability and inclusion programmes
human-capital-social-development-officer.stem: The Constitution requires at least what percentage of women in decision-making organs?
human-capital-social-development-officer.explanation: The Constitution of Rwanda provides that women must occupy at least 30% of posts in decision-making organs.

human-capital-social-development-officer.section: Youth, gender, disability and inclusion programmes
human-capital-social-development-officer.stem: In Rwanda, "youth" are persons aged:
human-capital-social-development-officer.explanation: The National Youth Policy defines youth as persons aged 16 to 30 years.

human-capital-social-development-officer.section: Sports, innovation, talent detection and delinquency prevention
human-capital-social-development-officer.stem: Which option lists the major causes of delinquency most completely?
options: Poverty, unemployment and low level of education only
Dysfunctional families, violence, drug and substance abuse, poverty, unemployment and low level of education
human-capital-social-development-officer.explanation: The National Rehabilitation Service lists drug and substance abuse, poverty, unemployment, low education, dysfunctional families and violence (plus peer influence) as major causes of delinquency, so all the listed groups are causes.

human-capital-social-development-officer.topic: Sports, innovation, talent detection and delinquency prevention
human-capital-social-development-officer.section: Sports, innovation, talent detection and delinquency prevention
human-capital-social-development-officer.stem: Our national flag has three colours: blue, yellow and green. What does the light blue represent?
human-capital-social-development-officer.explanation: Blue stands for happiness and peace; yellow for economic development; green for hope of prosperity.

human-capital-social-development-officer.topic: Sports, innovation, talent detection and delinquency prevention
human-capital-social-development-officer.section: Sports, innovation, talent detection and delinquency prevention
human-capital-social-development-officer.stem: The deepest lake in East Africa is ...
human-capital-social-development-officer.explanation: Lake Tanganyika (about 1,470 m deep) is the deepest lake in Africa; Lake Victoria is very shallow (under 100 m).

human-capital-social-development-officer.section: Sports, innovation, talent detection and delinquency prevention
human-capital-social-development-officer.stem: How many countries belong to the African Union?
human-capital-social-development-officer.explanation: The African Union has 55 Member States, covering all the countries on the African continent.

human-capital-social-development-officer.topic: Sports, innovation, talent detection and delinquency prevention
human-capital-social-development-officer.section: Sports, innovation, talent detection and delinquency prevention
human-capital-social-development-officer.stem: Who is the Minister in charge of Emergency Management?
human-capital-social-development-officer.explanation: Albert Murasira is the Minister in charge of Emergency Management (MINEMA).

human-capital-social-development-officer.section: Sports, innovation, talent detection and delinquency prevention
human-capital-social-development-officer.stem: Fill in the missing: The aspirations of the government of Rwanda to become ....................
options: the Upper Middle Income country by 2035 and High Income country by 2050
the Upper Middle Income country by 2035 and High Income country by 2060
the Upper Middle Income country by 2045 and High Income country by 2065
the Upper Middle Income country by 2025 and High Income country by 2060
human-capital-social-development-officer.explanation: Vision 2050 aims for Rwanda to be an upper-middle income country by 2035 and a high-income country by 2050.

human-capital-social-development-officer.stem: Early child development is very key especially in the first 1,000 days because it facilitates the:
options: Both healthy growth of the child and cognitive child development
human-capital-social-development-officer.explanation: The first 1,000 days are critical for long-term cognitive and physical development and health. Family planning is not what early child development facilitates.

human-capital-social-development-officer.stem: How can access to Social Care Services be improved for all vulnerable groups?
options: Promote positive values for intergeneration relationship
To create awareness among the community members as to ensure physical, economical and psychological preparedness for elderly persons
Strengthen interventions that prevent delinquency while also strengthening capacity for delivery of rehabilitation and reintegration services for delinquent children and youth
human-capital-social-development-officer.explanation: Under the policy action "To improve access to Social Care Services for all vulnerable groups" the listed measures include strengthening interventions that prevent delinquency and strengthening rehabilitation and reintegration services. The other two options belong to the separate action for elderly persons.

human-capital-social-development-officer.stem: Which ministry is NCDA affiliated to?
human-capital-social-development-officer.explanation: NCDA is supervised by the ministry in charge of children, the Ministry of Gender and Family Promotion (MIGEPROF), which lists NCDA and the National Women's Council as its affiliated institutions.

human-capital-social-development-officer.stem: According to the National Social Protection Policy of June 2020, what is the key factor contributing to malnutrition among children?
options: Lack of time of parents to take care of children
human-capital-social-development-officer.explanation: The National Social Protection Policy states that although many factors contribute to malnutrition, low incomes remain a key contributory factor, with malnutrition strongly correlated with consumption/income.

human-capital-social-development-officer.stem: Which of the following is a component of social protection in Rwanda?
human-capital-social-development-officer.explanation: Rwanda National Social Protection Policy (2020) covers social security (contributory social insurance and income support), social care services, short-term social assistance and livelihood/employment support (labour market access).

human-capital-social-development-officer.stem: A protective factor against delinquency is:
human-capital-social-development-officer.explanation: Strong family bonds and school/education engagement are recognised protective factors; neglect, substance abuse and negative peer pressure are risk factors.

human-capital-social-development-officer.stem: What does NCDA stand for?
human-capital-social-development-officer.explanation: NCDA is the National Child Development Agency, under MIGEPROF.

human-capital-social-development-officer.stem: The ECD Scorecard, 2nd edition 2022, ranked districts on breastfeeding children up to 24 months. Which district had the highest score?
human-capital-social-development-officer.explanation: In the ECD Scorecard (2nd edition) the overall score for breastfeeding children up to 24 months is 88.2%, with Rulindo highest at 95.6%; Nyamasheke and Karongi scored below 80%.

human-capital-social-development-officer.stem: The ECD Scorecard, 2nd edition 2022, demonstrated that the first cause of not breastfeeding children up to 24 months was:
human-capital-social-development-officer.explanation: About 11% of parents breastfeed for less than 24 months; the two main reasons are inadequate birth spacing (52.7%) and low breast milk supply (20.5%).

human-capital-social-development-officer.stem: In order to foster the development of a child, the promotion and the protection of his or her rights, the NCDA was established. As an Economy and Human Capital Officer you must monitor the implementation of interventions related to ECD programs. When was NCDA established?
human-capital-social-development-officer.explanation: The National Child Development Agency was established by Presidential Order No 083/01 of 28/08/2020, published in the Official Gazette on 4 September 2020, replacing the National Commission for Children and the NECDP.

human-capital-social-development-officer.stem: Community Health Workers (CHWs) were introduced in Rwanda in:
human-capital-social-development-officer.explanation: Vision 2050 states that Community Health Workers were introduced in Rwanda in 2005.

human-capital-social-development-officer.stem: The following are considered as cross cutting areas as they have been raised in the National Strategy for Transformation (NST 1). Which of the following answers is false?
human-capital-social-development-officer.explanation: NST1 lists seven cross-cutting areas: capacity development, HIV/AIDS and NCDs, disability and social inclusion, gender and family promotion, regional integration and international positioning, disaster management, and environment and climate change. Security maintenance is not one of them.

human-capital-social-development-officer.stem: Why is there a direct link between local planning and national planning in Rwanda?
options: National plans take local priorities into account, local plans and Imihigo align with national priorities, and national programmes are implemented through local government
Local governments prepare their plans independently and national government does not use them
National planning is done only by MINECOFIN and Districts only spend the budget they receive
Local Imihigo are prepared without reference to the National Strategy for Transformation
human-capital-social-development-officer.explanation: National plans take local priorities into account, local plans and Imihigo align with the NST and national priorities, and Districts implement national programmes.

human-capital-social-development-officer.stem: Rwanda has developed the necessary policies and tools for attaining Vision 2020 as well as Vision 2050. By this, the term vision means:
options: A short term aspiration of what a country wants to achieve in specific period of time
A long term aspiration of what a country wants to achieve in specific period of time
A medium period plan that includes what a country wants to achieve
human-capital-social-development-officer.explanation: Vision 2020 and Vision 2050 are Rwanda's long-term national frameworks (Vision 2050 sets the framework for 2020-2050), so a vision is a long-term aspiration of what a country wants to achieve in a specific period.

human-capital-social-development-officer.stem: Rwanda's Imihigo performance contracts started in 2006. By 2024, for how many years had they been operational?
human-capital-social-development-officer.explanation: Imihigo were introduced in 2006, so by 2024 they had been in place for 2024 - 2006 = 18 years.

human-capital-social-development-officer.stem: Imihigo performance contracts were introduced in Rwanda in:
human-capital-social-development-officer.explanation: The first Imihigo were signed in 2006 between the President and district mayors, at the start of the second phase of decentralisation.

human-capital-social-development-officer.section: Youth, gender, disability and inclusion programmes
human-capital-social-development-officer.stem: NST2 covers a five-year period, namely:
human-capital-social-development-officer.explanation: The Second National Strategy for Transformation (NST2) is the Five Years Government Programme 2024-2029.

human-capital-social-development-officer.section: Youth, gender, disability and inclusion programmes
human-capital-social-development-officer.stem: A "baseline" is:
options: Initial data showing the situation before an intervention begins
human-capital-social-development-officer.explanation: A baseline is the initial data describing the situation before an intervention begins, used to measure change later.

human-capital-social-development-officer.topic: Youth, gender, disability and inclusion programmes
human-capital-social-development-officer.section: Youth, gender, disability and inclusion programmes
human-capital-social-development-officer.stem: When did the United Nations Millennium Development Goals (MDGs) start?
human-capital-social-development-officer.explanation: The Millennium Declaration containing the MDGs came from the UN Millennium Summit of 6-8 September 2000, so November, June and December 2000 are all wrong.

human-capital-social-development-officer.section: Youth, gender, disability and inclusion programmes
human-capital-social-development-officer.stem: Who has the responsibility to prepare the reference documents related to the monitoring of the implementation of performance contracts of the state organs?
options: The head of the state organ
human-capital-social-development-officer.explanation: Art 15 of Law 18/2017: the Office of the Prime Minister prepares reference documents related to the monitoring of the implementation of performance contracts of the organs. None of the options (head of the organ, MINALOC, MINECOFIN) names the OPM.

human-capital-social-development-officer.section: Sports, innovation, talent detection and delinquency prevention
human-capital-social-development-officer.stem: Rwanda recognises the importance of culture and values in providing a platform for sustained socio-economic transformation and prosperity. Which of the following sets of values is reflected among the values of Rwanda in Vision 2050?
options: Justice, Kindness, Knowledge, Leadership, Loyalty, Work, Openness, Optimism, Peace
Self-determination, Solidarity and Dignity, Unity and Reconciliation, Identity
Respect, Responsibility, Security, Self-Respect, Service, Stability, Success
Authenticity, Achievement, Authority, Autonomy, Balance of gender, Compassion, Citizenship, Community
human-capital-social-development-officer.explanation: Vision 2050 (Positive Values supporting Societal Transformation) names self-determination (Kwigira), solidarity and dignity (Agaciro), unity and Rwandan identity/culture, with unity and reconciliation as a key value, plus equity and inclusiveness.

human-capital-social-development-officer.section: Sports, innovation, talent detection and delinquency prevention
human-capital-social-development-officer.stem: By the term "vision" (Vision 2020 / Vision 2050) we mean:
options: A short term aspiration of what a country wants to achieve
A long term aspiration of what a country wants to achieve in a specific period of time
A medium period plan that includes what a country wants to achieve
human-capital-social-development-officer.explanation: Vision 2050 sets out the long-term strategic direction (30 years) of the country; the medium-term plans are the NSTs, so a vision is a long-term aspiration.

human-capital-social-development-officer.stem: When was NCDA established?
human-capital-social-development-officer.explanation: The National Child Development Agency (NCDA) was established by Presidential Order 083/01 of 28/08/2020 (published 04/09/2020), merging the NCC and the NECDP.

human-capital-social-development-officer.stem: The Economic and Human Capital Development Officer is responsible for monitoring the implementation of interventions related to eradicating delinquency in the Cell. What do "Children on the streets" mean?
options: Children spending their time on the streets begging
Children living on the street full time, and have no contact with their families
Children spending most of their day time on the streets but returning home at night
Children living on the street full time but having contact with their families
human-capital-social-development-officer.explanation: The National Commission for Children distinguishes "children of the street" (full time, no family contact) from "children on the streets" who spend most of the day on the street but return home at night.

human-capital-social-development-officer.stem: According to the 5th Rwanda Population and Housing Census (RPHC5), youth (16-30 years) constitute ... of the Rwandan population.
human-capital-social-development-officer.explanation: Youth aged 16-30 are 27.1% (3.6 million) of the population.

human-capital-social-development-officer.stem: Vision 2050 aims to make Rwanda a:
human-capital-social-development-officer.explanation: Vision 2050 targets upper-middle-income status by 2035 and high-income status by 2050.

human-capital-social-development-officer.stem: Which is NOT a pillar of Vision 2050?
human-capital-social-development-officer.explanation: Vision 2050's five pillars are Human Development, Competitiveness and Integration, Agriculture for Wealth Creation, Urbanisation and Agglomeration, and Accountable and Capable State Institutions; Mining for Export is not one.

human-capital-social-development-officer.stem: In order for the Gender-Based Violence policy to be successfully implemented, the Government of Rwanda as a whole will have to:
options: Ensure access to services is free for victims
Ensure adequate financial resources are allocated to support services
Ensure that the Law on Prevention and Punishment of Gender-Based Violence is sufficiently disseminated to the people of Rwanda and that it is well understood and respected
human-capital-social-development-officer.explanation: The policy's institutional framework section says that for successful implementation Government as a whole must empower public institutions, ensure the GBV law is sufficiently disseminated, understood and respected, and put coordination and M&E mechanisms in place.

human-capital-social-development-officer.stem: When was MINUBUMWE established?
human-capital-social-development-officer.explanation: Cabinet approved the creation of the Ministry of National Unity and Civic Engagement at its meeting of 14 July 2021.

human-capital-social-development-officer.stem: What are the age categories composing the Itorero at village level?
options: It is composed of 6 categories, namely: Ibirezi (0-5), Imbuto (6-12), Indirira (13-18), Indahangarwa (19-35), Ingobokarugamba (36-55) and Inararibonye (55 and above)
It is composed of 6 categories, namely: Ibirezi (5-10), Imbuto (11-18), Indirira (19-30), Indahangarwa (31-45), Ingobokarugamba (45-50) and Inararibonye (55 and above)
It is composed of 6 categories, namely: Ibirezi (0-8), Imbuto (8-19), Indirira (20-30), Indahangarwa (31-45), Ingobokarugamba (46-55) and Inararibonye (55 and above)
It is composed of 6 categories, namely: Ibirezi (0-5), Imbuto (6-18), Indirira (18-25), Indahangarwa (25-35), Ingobokarugamba (36-55) and Inararibonye (55 and above)
human-capital-social-development-officer.explanation: The National Itorero Commission structure at village level groups members as Ibirezi (under 5/0-5), Imbuto (6-12), Indirira (13-18), Indahangarwa (19-35), Ingobokarugamba (36-55) and Inararibonye (older).

human-capital-social-development-officer.stem: Which of the following is NOT an achievement of URUGERERO?
options: Educating the population on personal hygiene and cleanliness of their environment
Sensitizing the community in general and the youth in particular to fight against drug abuse
Sensitizing Rwandans on the eradication of genocide and its ideology
human-capital-social-development-officer.explanation: The first Urugerero group's achievements were sensitisation drives (genocide ideology, drug abuse, hygiene and others); public lighting is not among them.

human-capital-social-development-officer.stem: What are the major factors contributing to teenage pregnancies?
options: Poverty, lack of information on reproductive health, lack of parental attachment and guidance on children's moral, psychological, emotional and financial support
Lack of contraceptives in surrounding shops
The Rwandan culture which says that reproductive health is a taboo that no one should talk about
Lack of follow-up from schools where adolescents spend more time
human-capital-social-development-officer.explanation: Studies in Rwanda identify poverty, lack of knowledge of sexual and reproductive health and weak parental guidance as the leading drivers of adolescent pregnancy.

human-capital-social-development-officer.stem: "Human capital" refers to:
options: The knowledge, skills and health of people that enable them to be productive
human-capital-social-development-officer.explanation: Human capital is the knowledge, skills and health of people that make them productive; it underpins Rwanda's human capital development agenda.

human-capital-social-development-officer.stem: TVET stands for:
options: Technical and Vocational Education and Training
human-capital-social-development-officer.explanation: TVET is the standard term (Rwanda TVET Board, national TVET policy) for Technical and Vocational Education and Training.

human-capital-social-development-officer.stem: NCPD is the national council responsible for:
human-capital-social-development-officer.explanation: NCPD is the National Council of Persons with Disabilities, created by Law 03/2011 as a forum for advocacy and social mobilisation for persons with disabilities.

human-capital-social-development-officer.stem: Which of the following was NOT a responsibility of the National Unity and Reconciliation Commission (NURC)?
options: To educate, sensitize and mobilize the population in areas of national unity and reconciliation
To establish and promote mechanisms for restoring and strengthening the Unity and Reconciliation of Rwandans
To prepare and coordinate the national programs aimed at promoting national unity and reconciliation
To act as a link between the citizen and public and private institutions
human-capital-social-development-officer.explanation: The NURC law (Law 35/2008) lists preparing and coordinating national programmes, establishing mechanisms for unity, and educating/sensitising/mobilising the population as NURC duties; acting as a link between citizens and institutions is not among them.

human-capital-social-development-officer.stem: The Economic and Human Capital Development Officer monitors the implementation of interventions related to the ECD programme. According to the Ministerial Order of 2023 relating to child well-being, which ECD programme is the Cell authority competent to register and accredit, and what is a minimum requirement for it to be accredited?
options: ECD centers; to be established in a building constructed by the local population
Model ECD centers; to present a detailed project containing the real challenges that need to be addressed
Community-based ECD centers; to have a caregiver trained on ECD services
Home-based ECD services; to have clean water, toilet and kitchen
human-capital-social-development-officer.explanation: Under Ministerial Order No 001/MIGEPROF/2023 relating to child well-being, the Cell authority registers and accredits home-based ECD services, whose host home must have clean water, a clean toilet and a clean kitchen (among other requirements).

human-capital-social-development-officer.stem: Choose the false response: The Economic and Human Capital Development Officer is responsible for monitoring the implementation of interventions related to education. According to the Law determining the organisation of education in Rwanda of 2021, the responsibilities of a parent or a person with parental authority in the development of quality of education consist of:
options: Ensuring that the child starts school at the required age
Ensuring the discipline and learning of the child
Providing the child with quality education and ensuring his or her development
Training the learner to work, to love the work, to take their work seriously and to be punctual
human-capital-social-development-officer.explanation: Article 6 of Law 010/2021 lists parents' duties (quality education, school-start age, discipline and learning, means, choice of school, school feeding); training the learner to work and be punctual is not among them.

human-capital-social-development-officer.stem: Which programmes help prevent child stunting at village and cell levels?
options: One cow per poor family only
One cup of milk per child only
Kitchen garden, one cow per poor family and one cup of milk per child
human-capital-social-development-officer.explanation: The National Food and Nutrition Policy lists Girinka (one cow per poor family), One Cup of Milk per child and kitchen gardens among the interventions against malnutrition and stunting.

human-capital-social-development-officer.stem: The Chancellery for Heroes, National Orders and Decorations of Honour is responsible for:
options: awarding national honours and recognising heroes
human-capital-social-development-officer.explanation: CHENO recognises National Heroes and awards National Orders and decorations of honour.

human-capital-social-development-officer.stem: Under Law No 05/2015 governing the organisation of pension schemes, to access the monthly old-age pension a member must be at least ... years old (or the age provided for by a legally recognised special statute), have contributed for at least 15 years and have stopped paid work.
human-capital-social-development-officer.explanation: Original stem is ambiguous ("retirement age of a member of RSSB": the pension law fixes the minimum age to claim a monthly old-age pension at 60 or the age in a legally recognised special statute, while some public-service statutes set 65). Rewritten to the exact rule: Article 18(1) of Law 05/2015 requires at least sixty (60) years (or the age provided by a special statute), 15 years of contributions and cessation of paid work.

human-capital-social-development-officer.section: District plans, reporting and performance monitoring
human-capital-social-development-officer.stem: NST1 and the National Social Protection Policy envision the reduction of chronic malnutrition to ... by 2024.
human-capital-social-development-officer.explanation: NST1's results matrix targets prevalence of chronic malnutrition (stunting) among children under 5 at 19% by 2024.

human-capital-social-development-officer.section: District plans, reporting and performance monitoring
human-capital-social-development-officer.stem: Which one of the following is not included in the National Policy against Gender-Based Violence?
options: The Government of Rwanda strongly believes in, and promotes gender equality, equity and empowerment of women as a crucial human resource for social and economic development
The Government of Rwanda condones any acts of gender-based violence

The Government of Rwanda is committed to using its fullest powers to fight, prevent and provide response to all forms of gender-based violence in society; and GBV interventions and responses must be conducted in all social, economic and political sectors
The Government of Rwanda recognizes gender-based violence as a violation of human rights
human-capital-social-development-officer.explanation: The policy states that the Government of Rwanda does not condone any acts of gender-based violence, so a statement that it condones them is not in the policy.

human-capital-social-development-officer.section: District plans, reporting and performance monitoring
human-capital-social-development-officer.stem: Fill in the missing: The National Policy against GBV was developed by a Technical Team led by ..........................
human-capital-social-development-officer.explanation: The policy was developed by a Technical Team led by MIGEPROF (Ministry of Gender and Family Promotion) with MINICAAF, MINECOFIN, MINISANTE, MINIJUST, MINALOC, Police, RDF and others.

human-capital-social-development-officer.section: District plans, reporting and performance monitoring
human-capital-social-development-officer.stem: Fill in the blanks: The Economic and Human Capital Development Officer is responsible for monitoring the implementation of interventions related to education. ...... aims to train a child to socialise with others, to do physical, rhythmic and arms exercises.
human-capital-social-development-officer.explanation: The 2021 education law says pre-primary education aims to train a child to socialise, play and do physical, rhythmic and arms exercises.

human-capital-social-development-officer.section: District plans, reporting and performance monitoring
human-capital-social-development-officer.stem: The Vision 2020 Umurenge Programme (VUP) started in:
human-capital-social-development-officer.explanation: The Government of Rwanda launched the VUP in 2008 with three components: Direct Support, Public Works and Financial Services.

human-capital-social-development-officer.section: District plans, reporting and performance monitoring
human-capital-social-development-officer.stem: As per the fifth Rwanda Population and Housing Census (RPHC5), youth constitute what share of the Rwandan population?
human-capital-social-development-officer.explanation: RPHC5 reports that youth (aged 16-30) constitute 27.1% (3.6 million) of the total population.

human-capital-social-development-officer.section: District plans, reporting and performance monitoring
human-capital-social-development-officer.stem: As per the fifth Rwanda Population and Housing Census, youth constitute ...... of the Rwandan population.
human-capital-social-development-officer.explanation: In the 2022 census youth (aged 16-30) are 27.1% of the population (3.6 million).

human-capital-social-development-officer.section: District plans, reporting and performance monitoring
human-capital-social-development-officer.stem: Which ministry oversees gender and family promotion?
human-capital-social-development-officer.explanation: MIGEPROF, the Ministry of Gender and Family Promotion, is responsible for gender and family promotion.

human-capital-social-development-officer.section: District plans, reporting and performance monitoring
human-capital-social-development-officer.stem: Choose the false response: What are the key interventions, among the following, implemented by the Government and its stakeholders to fight against malnutrition in Rwanda?
options: One cup of milk per child
human-capital-social-development-officer.explanation: The National Food and Nutrition Policy lists Girinka, One Cup of Milk per child, school gardens, and promotion of kitchen gardens and small livestock as nutrition interventions; community-based health insurance is a health-financing scheme not listed among them.

human-capital-social-development-officer.stem: Choose the false response: Students' parents or their representatives participate in school management and activities through:
human-capital-social-development-officer.explanation: Under Law 10/2021 on the organisation of education, parents sit in the General Assembly, the Executive Committee (5 elected parents) and the Audit Committee (chair and deputy elected from parents); the management of a school is the head teacher and deputy heads only.

human-capital-social-development-officer.stem: In which city is the African Union Headquarters located?
human-capital-social-development-officer.explanation: The African Union headquarters is in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia.

human-capital-social-development-officer.stem: What are outcome indicators of Enhanced citizen participation, empowerment and inclusiveness?
options: % of citizen satisfaction with the performance of local government councils
% of citizens satisfaction in their participation in planning disaggregated by gender and age
Proportion of seats held by women in Local governments at district, sector and cell level
To ensure that service delivery to the citizens meet the highest quality standards
human-capital-social-development-officer.explanation: Under Outcome 1 "Enhanced citizen participation, empowerment and inclusiveness", the outcome indicators are citizen satisfaction in participation in planning, budgeting and decision making, and gender parity in leadership. Satisfaction with councils and seats held by women are output 1.1 indicators.

human-capital-social-development-officer.stem: Which one of the following is not a guiding principle of decentralization?
options: National unity, indivisibility and equitable development
Establish Community data center at cell level
human-capital-social-development-officer.explanation: The guiding principles include subsidiarity, national unity, indivisibility and equitable development, and demarcation of roles and responsibilities. Establishing a community data centre at Cell level is a policy action under data and information systems, not a principle.

human-capital-social-development-officer.stem: What are the three forms of decentralisation?
human-capital-social-development-officer.explanation: Rwanda's decentralisation policy names three forms: deconcentration, devolution and delegation.

human-capital-social-development-officer.stem: The most populated district in Rwanda is located in which province?
human-capital-social-development-officer.explanation: Gasabo, in the City of Kigali, is the most populated district (879,505 residents in the 2022 census).

human-capital-social-development-officer.stem: Decentralization is a sensitive governance reform process that is often politically unpopular. It can only succeed with ...... from top leadership.
human-capital-social-development-officer.explanation: The National Decentralization Policy (October 2021) states decentralization can only succeed with immense political will from top leadership.

human-capital-social-development-officer.stem: According to NST1, the target for citizens satisfied by service delivery by 2024 is:
human-capital-social-development-officer.explanation: NST1 says the percentage of citizens satisfied with service delivery will rise from 67.7% (2016 RGS) to 90% by 2024.

human-capital-social-development-officer.stem: The sectoral decentralization and service delivery have different issues. Which one is it?
options: The capacity gap in the matter related to Public Financial Management is still critical at decentralized entities
Limited availability and use of data and information management systems at Local Government level
Decentralized tax revenue sources are limited
human-capital-social-development-officer.explanation: Limited availability and use of data and information management systems at Local Government level is a policy issue listed under Pillar 1, sectoral decentralization and service delivery. The public financial management and tax revenue issues belong to Pillar 2, fiscal and financial decentralization, and capacity development is Pillar 3.

human-capital-social-development-officer.stem: Which form of decentralisation matches this definition: the transfer of functions and resources to lower-level units of the same administrative system while authority over decision-making and use of such resources remains with the centre?
human-capital-social-development-officer.explanation: This is the policy definition of deconcentration: functions move to lower units but power and authority stay with the centre.

human-capital-social-development-officer.stem: The District Development Plan (DDP), now the District Development Strategy, is aligned with:
human-capital-social-development-officer.explanation: District development plans (now District Development Strategies) are aligned with the National Strategy for Transformation (NST) and Vision 2050.

human-capital-social-development-officer.stem: The role of the Cell SEDO is to:
options: Plan, monitor and report on economic development activities in the Cell
human-capital-social-development-officer.explanation: The Cell Socio-Economic Development Officer coordinates planning, monitoring and reporting of socio-economic activities in the Cell under the Cell Executive Secretary.

human-capital-social-development-officer.stem: How many priority areas are in the Transformational Governance pillar of NST1?
human-capital-social-development-officer.explanation: NST1 (2017-2024) says the Transformational Governance pillar is achieved through 6 priority areas.

human-capital-social-development-officer.stem: According to the 5th Rwanda Population and Housing Census (RPHC5), which is the most densely populated District?
human-capital-social-development-officer.explanation: Kicukiro is the most densely populated District (about 2,944 inhabitants per sq km), ahead of Nyarugenge and Gasabo.

human-capital-social-development-officer.stem: According to the 5th Rwanda Population and Housing Census (RPHC5), which is the least populated District?
human-capital-social-development-officer.explanation: Nyaruguru has the lowest population of all Districts (about 318,900 residents).

human-capital-social-development-officer.section: District plans, reporting and performance monitoring
human-capital-social-development-officer.stem: How many national symbols does Rwanda have?
human-capital-social-development-officer.explanation: Article 9(1) of the Constitution lists four national symbols: the National Flag, the Motto of the Republic, the Seal of the Republic and the National Anthem. None of 2, 5 or 3 is right.

human-capital-social-development-officer.section: District plans, reporting and performance monitoring
human-capital-social-development-officer.stem: The State of Rwanda, through its Constitution, commits itself to upholding the fundamental principles and ensuring their respect. How many are they?
human-capital-social-development-officer.explanation: Article 10 of the Constitution as amended in 2015 lists six fundamental principles (earlier version had eight).

human-capital-social-development-officer.section: District plans, reporting and performance monitoring
human-capital-social-development-officer.stem: The overall NST1 M&E Framework is grounded on key guiding principles. How many are they?
human-capital-social-development-officer.explanation: NST1 lists five guiding principles: comprehensiveness; participation and inclusiveness; leverage of ICT tools and dashboards; consistency and harmonization between sector and district strategies; flexibility.

human-capital-social-development-officer.section: District plans, reporting and performance monitoring
human-capital-social-development-officer.stem: What is NST1 in full?
human-capital-social-development-officer.explanation: NST1 is the National Strategy for Transformation (2017-2024), the 7 Years Government Programme. The other expansions are invented.

human-capital-social-development-officer.section: District plans, reporting and performance monitoring
human-capital-social-development-officer.stem: What are the pillars of NST1?
options: Economic transformation, social transformation, transformational governance
Economic transformation, social transformation, transformational leadership, transformational governance and cross-cutting
Economic transformation, project management, social transformation, transformational leadership, transformational governance and cross-cutting
human-capital-social-development-officer.explanation: NST1 rests on three pillars: Economic Transformation, Social Transformation and Transformational Governance. Cross-cutting areas are treated separately and are not pillars.

human-capital-social-development-officer.section: District plans, reporting and performance monitoring
human-capital-social-development-officer.stem: According to NST1, online service delivery will be at which percentage in 2024?
human-capital-social-development-officer.explanation: NST1 sets the target that 100% of Government services are delivered online by 2024 (from 40%).

human-capital-social-development-officer.section: District plans, reporting and performance monitoring
human-capital-social-development-officer.stem: What are the pillars of the National Strategy for Transformation (NST1) 2017-2024?
options: Good governance and capable State; Human resource development and a knowledge-based economy; Private sector-led development; Infrastructure development; Productive, high-value and market-oriented agriculture; Regional and international integration
Human development; Agriculture for wealth creation; Competitiveness and integration; Urbanisation and agglomeration; Accountable and capable State institutions
Economic Transformation; Social Transformation; Transformational Governance
human-capital-social-development-officer.explanation: NST1 (2017-2024) is built on three pillars: Economic Transformation, Social Transformation and Transformational Governance.

human-capital-social-development-officer.section: District plans, reporting and performance monitoring
human-capital-social-development-officer.stem: Which statement is true among the following? By Vision 2050,
options: Rwanda is on a transformation path from a middle-income to a high-income country
Rwanda is on a transformation path from a low-income to a high-income country
Rwanda is on a transformation path from a low-income to a middle-income country
human-capital-social-development-officer.explanation: Vision 2050 starts from a 2019 GDP per capita of USD 837 (low income) and aims for upper-middle income by 2035 and high income by 2050, so the end-point is high income.

human-capital-social-development-officer.section: District plans, reporting and performance monitoring
human-capital-social-development-officer.stem: Which option lists the pillars of Vision 2050?
options: Human Development; Competitiveness and Integration; Agriculture for Wealth Creation; Urbanization and Agglomeration; Accountable and Capable State Institutions
Development of human resource, financial development, industry development
Good governance, economic development, social development
human-capital-social-development-officer.explanation: Rwanda Vision 2050 is built on five pillars: Human Development, Competitiveness and Integration, Agriculture for Wealth Creation, Urbanization and Agglomeration, and Accountable and Capable State Institutions.

human-capital-social-development-officer.section: District plans, reporting and performance monitoring
human-capital-social-development-officer.stem: How many are the guiding principles adopted for the RBM-based performance management system in the Public Service in Rwanda?
human-capital-social-development-officer.explanation: Section 6 of the RBM Policy lists seven principles: accountability, ownership, inclusiveness, alignment of operations to RBM, evidence-based learning, transparency, and a culture of results.

human-capital-social-development-officer.section: District plans, reporting and performance monitoring
human-capital-social-development-officer.stem: Fill the missing: Performance contracts (Imihigo) program has been launched in ......
human-capital-social-development-officer.explanation: Imihigo performance contracts were launched in 2006 (first signed by district mayors with the President).

human-capital-social-development-officer.section: District plans, reporting and performance monitoring
human-capital-social-development-officer.stem: When did the Imihigo performance contracts start in Rwanda?
human-capital-social-development-officer.explanation: Imihigo was reintroduced in 2006; the first contracts were signed between the President and mayors on 4 April 2006.

human-capital-social-development-officer.section: Professional competencies and ethics in practice
human-capital-social-development-officer.stem: The journey of reconciliation in Rwanda continues to achieve tangible progress. Findings of the Rwanda Reconciliation Barometer 2020 show that the current state of reconciliation in Rwanda stands at:
human-capital-social-development-officer.explanation: The Rwanda Reconciliation Barometer 2020 puts the status of reconciliation at 94.7%, up from 92.5% in 2015.

human-capital-social-development-officer.topic: Professional competencies and ethics in practice
human-capital-social-development-officer.section: Professional competencies and ethics in practice
human-capital-social-development-officer.stem: Choose the false response: "Human capital" encompasses:
human-capital-social-development-officer.explanation: Human capital is the knowledge, skills and health that people accumulate; income is not a component.

human-capital-social-development-officer.topic: Professional competencies and ethics in practice
human-capital-social-development-officer.section: Professional competencies and ethics in practice
human-capital-social-development-officer.stem: What do basic needs comprise?
options: Food, clothing, basic education, money, livestock
Food, clothing, shelter, basic education, basic health care
human-capital-social-development-officer.explanation: Basic needs are food, clothing and shelter plus essential services such as basic education and health care; land, livestock and money are not basic needs.

human-capital-social-development-officer.topic: Professional competencies and ethics in practice
human-capital-social-development-officer.section: Professional competencies and ethics in practice
human-capital-social-development-officer.stem: According to the Human Capital Index published by the World Bank in 2018 and 2020, which statement is true?
options: Rwanda's performance was below the region in both Health components and Education indicators
Rwanda's performance was above the region in Health components; but lagged behind on Education indicators
Rwanda's performance was above the region in both Health components and Education indicators
Rwanda's performance was above the region in Education indicators; but lagged behind on Health components
human-capital-social-development-officer.explanation: MINEDUC's HCI policy brief states Rwanda performed above the region in Survival and Health components but lagged behind on Education (and stunting) indicators.

human-capital-social-development-officer.stem: When was the Ndi Umunyarwanda programme started by the Government of Rwanda?
human-capital-social-development-officer.explanation: Ndi Umunyarwanda grew out of 2013 youth dialogues led with NURC and was launched in 2013.

human-capital-social-development-officer.stem: When did the Government of Rwanda start the "one cow per poor family" programme?
human-capital-social-development-officer.explanation: Girinka (One Cow per Poor Family) was launched in 2006 (implementation start November 2006).

human-capital-social-development-officer.stem: After restructuring, Itorero was placed in MINUBUMWE. What does MINUBUMWE mean in full?
options: Ministry of National Unity and Reconciliation for Civic Education
Ministry of National Unity and Civic Education
Ministry of National Unity and Civic Engagement
human-capital-social-development-officer.explanation: MINUBUMWE is the Ministry of National Unity and Civic Engagement; the National Itorero Commission was wound down and its functions moved to it.

human-capital-social-development-officer.stem: The criteria considered in the selection of Girinka beneficiaries were:
options: The beneficiary must be considered by his/her cell executive secretary as poor
The selected beneficiary must construct a cowshed before he/she receives the cow
The beneficiary must be the poorest in the village
The beneficiary must have at least 1-2 hectares
human-capital-social-development-officer.explanation: RAB's Girinka criteria require no current cattle, enough land or common grazing area, prepared pasture, and a simple structure to house the cow. Beneficiaries are chosen by the community from poor households; they are not named by the Executive Secretary and do not need 1-2 hectares.

human-capital-social-development-officer.stem: Choose among the following, a false guiding principle for the Community Development Policy.
human-capital-social-development-officer.explanation: The policy lists community participation, common benefit and collaboration between sectors and partners; the principle is promotion of commerce, not "promotion of economy".

human-capital-social-development-officer.stem: In the National Social Protection Policy, equity means:
options: All interventions address specific needs and vulnerabilities of both girls and boys, women and men
All eligible citizens are guaranteed a minimum package of services within Government means
Fairness and openness in provision; duty bearers are accountable
Fairness and justice across demographic categories and geographical locations
human-capital-social-development-officer.explanation: The National Social Protection Policy (June 2020), section 3.5 Guiding principles: "Equity: Fairness and justice shall underpin the provision of social protection services across different demographic categories and geographical locations." Option A is Gender Responsiveness, B is Universalism and inclusiveness, C is Transparency and accountability.

human-capital-social-development-officer.stem: One of the principles that guide the National Social Protection Policy is Equity. In this context, equity means:
options: All social protection interventions shall address specific needs and vulnerabilities for both girls and boys, women and men

All eligible citizens shall be guaranteed a minimum package of social protection services within the limits of Government means with a view to ensuring that all Rwandan citizens achieve a dignified standard of living

Fairness and openness shall be emphasized in the provision of social protection services. Duty bearers and institutions implementing social protection interventions be accountable for their performance
Fairness and justice shall underpin the provision of social protection services across different demographic categories and geographical locations
human-capital-social-development-officer.explanation: The policy defines Equity as fairness and justice underpinning social protection services across demographic categories and geographical locations. The other options define gender responsiveness, universalism and inclusiveness, and transparency and accountability.

human-capital-social-development-officer.stem: Ndi Umunyarwanda is a home-grown solution launched on 15 November 2013. What is the overall objective of Ndi Umunyarwanda?
options: To strengthen unity and reconciliation among Rwandans after the 1994 Genocide against the Tutsi
To bring together Rwandans who live outside the country and those who live in the country to discuss the development of the country
To raise funds that will be used to build houses for the vulnerable
To encourage people to love their country and therefore love each other
human-capital-social-development-officer.explanation: Ndi Umunyarwanda is a home-grown programme aimed at strengthening unity and reconciliation among Rwandans, building national identity and solidarity and tackling genocide ideology.

human-capital-social-development-officer.stem: Which of the following does NOT reflect the benefits of ITORERO in general and Urugerero in particular?
options: Increased solidarity, strengthened national identity and reduced stereotypic thinking by interfacing with the realities of the communities and the country in general
Increased number of women participating in the economy of the country
Increased patriotism and civic participation, especially among the young generation
human-capital-social-development-officer.explanation: Itorero and Urugerero aim at unity, social cohesion, national identity, patriotism and civic participation; raising women's economic participation is not one of their stated aims.

human-capital-social-development-officer.stem: The Government of Rwanda has put in place many programmes that aim to sustain social development. Which of the following is NOT among the social development programmes?
options: One cow for one poor family (Girinka)
human-capital-social-development-officer.explanation: Agaciro Development Fund is Rwanda's sovereign wealth fund for public savings and self-reliance, not a social development programme; Girinka, Ejo Heza and VUP are social protection / poverty-reduction programmes.

human-capital-social-development-officer.stem: Ubudehe is a programme based on:
human-capital-social-development-officer.explanation: Ubudehe is a home-grown approach based on collective action and mutual support to solve community problems; it is also used for household categorisation.

human-capital-social-development-officer.stem: The purpose of Itorero ry'Igihugu is to:
options: Instil civic education, values and commitment to serve the nation
human-capital-social-development-officer.explanation: Itorero ry'Igihugu (National Itorero Commission) is Rwanda's civic education programme promoting patriotic values and producing active citizens committed to national development.

human-capital-social-development-officer.stem: The School Feeding programme aims to:
options: Reduce dropout, improve attendance and support nutrition
human-capital-social-development-officer.explanation: Under the National Comprehensive School Feeding Policy (2019), school meals aim to improve nutrition, enrolment, attendance, retention and learning.

human-capital-social-development-officer.stem: The guiding principles for the community development policy include:
options: Monitoring the implementation of the poverty reduction programs
Determination of household poverty profile as they themselves perceive it
human-capital-social-development-officer.explanation: Collaboration between sectors and partners is one of the guiding principles in section 3.1 of the Community Development Policy; the other options are not listed principles (the poverty-profile item is a step of the Ubudehe process in 3.2.2).

human-capital-social-development-officer.stem: Responsibilities of CHWs in the stunting programme include all EXCEPT:
options: Education on kitchen gardens, hygiene, food preparation
Diagnosis of non-communicable diseases for under-fives
