human-capital-social-development-officer.explanation: The National Food and Nutrition Policy has communities/CHWs do monthly growth monitoring and teach kitchen gardens, hygiene and food preparation; diagnosing NCDs in under-fives is not a CHW task.

human-capital-social-development-officer.stem: According to the school feeding policy, a benefit of school feeding is:
options: Better attendance, improved concentration and support to local farmers
human-capital-social-development-officer.explanation: The National School Feeding Policy lists better attendance, improved concentration and support to local farmers among its benefits.

human-capital-social-development-officer.stem: In which year was the first National Social Protection Policy adopted in Rwanda?
human-capital-social-development-officer.explanation: The first National Social Protection Policy was adopted in 2005, moving from humanitarian assistance to social assistance. A revised policy followed in 2020.

human-capital-social-development-officer.stem: Which one of the following is the key Community Development objective?
options: Community participation in accountability and justice systems
Community engagement in ecosystem rehabilitation and conservation
human-capital-social-development-officer.explanation: The Community Development Policy defines its objectives across three spheres: economic development, social development and good governance. The other options are only examples of activities listed under those objectives.

human-capital-social-development-officer.stem: The following are considered as principles guiding the implementation of the Community Development Policy:
options: Autonomous management at local government level
Political will and strong support by stakeholders
human-capital-social-development-officer.explanation: The guiding principles include community participation, common benefit, exploitation of local potential, transparency and accountability, autonomous management at local government level, promotion of commerce, and collaboration. Political will is an opportunity and a rapidly changing environment is a challenge.

human-capital-social-development-officer.stem: The selection of social protection programme beneficiaries is currently done using:
human-capital-social-development-officer.explanation: Since 29 Feb 2024 MINALOC's Imibereho Dynamic Social Registry replaced Ubudehe categorisation for targeting social protection beneficiaries; IremboGov is a service portal.

human-capital-social-development-officer.stem: What is the Rwanda national motto?
human-capital-social-development-officer.explanation: The Constitution states the motto of the Republic is Unity, Work, Patriotism (Ubumwe, Umurimo, Gukunda Igihugu).

human-capital-social-development-officer.stem: From when has Rwanda been a full member of the Commonwealth?
human-capital-social-development-officer.explanation: Rwanda joined the Commonwealth in 2009 as its 54th member.

human-capital-social-development-officer.topic: Professional competencies and ethics in practice
human-capital-social-development-officer.section: Professional competencies and ethics in practice
human-capital-social-development-officer.stem: When was the ICTR established?
human-capital-social-development-officer.explanation: The UN Security Council established the International Criminal Tribunal for Rwanda by resolution 955 on 8 November 1994.

human-capital-social-development-officer.topic: Professional competencies and ethics in practice
human-capital-social-development-officer.section: Professional competencies and ethics in practice
human-capital-social-development-officer.stem: Which of the following is not a tip for building an effective brand awareness campaign?
options: Spreading your energy across multiple social media platforms
Focus on the platforms your audience uses most
human-capital-social-development-officer.explanation: Brand awareness guidance advises understanding your target audience, partnering with brands that share your audience and focusing on the channels your audience uses most. Spreading effort thinly across many platforms is the opposite of that advice.

human-capital-social-development-officer.section: Professional competencies and ethics in practice
human-capital-social-development-officer.stem: When did Rwanda join the EAC?
human-capital-social-development-officer.explanation: Rwanda (with Burundi) joined the East African Community in July 2007.

human-capital-social-development-officer.stem: By definition Home grown solutions are:
options: innovations that have proved to be the solutions to a particular problem;
Rwanda's 'trade mark' solutions developed by Rwandans based on local opportunities, cultural values and history to fast track their development.
innovations that address a challenge in a new and different way often through simpler and more effective approaches
innovations or initiatives rooted in the Rwandan cultural heritage and values
human-capital-social-development-officer.explanation: The Rwanda Governance Board defines Home Grown Solutions as Rwanda's 'trade mark' solutions developed by Rwandans based on local opportunities, cultural values and history to fast track their development. The other options describe only parts of the criteria.

human-capital-social-development-officer.stem: Fill in the missing: ............ the Ministry of Local Government, in collaboration with the National Itorero Commission and Local Administrative Entities Development Agency, launched Itorero at village level across the country.
human-capital-social-development-officer.explanation: MINALOC, with the National Itorero Commission and LODA, launched Itorero at village level on 11 December 2018 (national event in Nyagatare).

human-capital-social-development-officer.stem: What is the vision of the revised National Decentralisation Policy of 2021?
options: A self-reliant, secure, politically mature and informed society for sustainable national transformation
To build a highly effective and accountable Local Government driven by citizen-centred governance for local socio-economic transformation
A fully mobilised, empowered, engaged and proud citizen for sustainable socio-economic transformation
human-capital-social-development-officer.explanation: The 2021 National Decentralisation Policy states its Vision as "A self-reliant, secure, politically mature and informed society for sustainable national transformation"; option B is its Mission.

human-capital-social-development-officer.stem: Rwanda's Decentralization Policy was inspired by ...... fundamental principles which had been violated until 1994.
human-capital-social-development-officer.explanation: The policy was inspired by four fundamental principles: human rights, dignity, freedom and development.

human-capital-social-development-officer.stem: When did Rwanda join the Organisation internationale de la Francophonie (OIF)?
human-capital-social-development-officer.explanation: Rwanda has been a member of the Organisation internationale de la Francophonie since 1970 (a founding member of the original agency, ACCT, created in 1970).

human-capital-social-development-officer.stem: On 1st July every year, Rwanda celebrates:
human-capital-social-development-officer.explanation: 1 July is Independence Day; Liberation Day is 4 July.

human-capital-social-development-officer.stem: Home Grown Solutions (HGS) are Rwanda's 'trade mark' solutions developed by Rwandans based on ... key points.
human-capital-social-development-officer.explanation: RGB lists five criteria that an innovation must meet to qualify as a Home Grown Solution.

human-capital-social-development-officer.stem: The home grown solution that enables citizens to keep their leaders accountable and accelerate socio-economic development is:
human-capital-social-development-officer.explanation: Imihigo are the performance contracts through which local leaders commit to targets and are held to account, introduced to speed up development and strengthen accountability.

human-capital-social-development-officer.stem: Civil Society Organizations and media have key roles in decentralization dynamism in Rwanda. Which one of the following is part of them?
options: Approving indicators to monitor decentralization implementation
Advising on harmonization of legislation on decentralization and harmonize sector policies to reflect devolution
Participation in policy and program development
Facilitating cross sectorial implementation of the decentralization policy and accelerating the envisaged process
human-capital-social-development-officer.explanation: The policy gives civil society organisations and media three roles: sensitising citizens and helping them hold service providers to account, participating in policy and programme development, and advocacy. The other three options are tasks of the Ministry in charge of Local Governance and Decentralization.

human-capital-social-development-officer.stem: Which one of the following is not a commendable achievement of the implementation of the decentralization policy?
human-capital-social-development-officer.explanation: The policy describes commendable achievements in political, administrative, financial and fiscal decentralization and in local economic development. Social decentralization is not listed.

human-capital-social-development-officer.stem: Girinka or One Cow per family programme is an important Home Grown Solution (HGS) with an intrinsic connection to the Rwandan culture. It was introduced in ..... by the Government of Rwanda (GoR) with the purpose to reduce child malnutrition and improve health and wellbeing of vulnerable citizens.
human-capital-social-development-officer.explanation: The Government launched the Girinka programme in 2006, following the 2005-2006 rural household survey that showed high rural poverty and malnutrition.

human-capital-social-development-officer.stem: Which one of the following is a home-grown solution?
human-capital-social-development-officer.explanation: Gacaca is one of Rwanda's recognised home-grown solutions; vaccination, 12YBE and hybrid plants are not.

human-capital-social-development-officer.stem: Rwanda Vision 2020 was launched in:
human-capital-social-development-officer.explanation: The Rwanda Vision 2020 document was issued by the Ministry of Finance and Economic Planning in Kigali in July 2000.

human-capital-social-development-officer.stem: Which development strategy preceded NST1?
human-capital-social-development-officer.explanation: NST1 (2017-2024) followed the Economic Development and Poverty Reduction Strategy II (EDPRS 2, 2013-2018) as Rwanda's medium-term plan; Agaciro, Ubudehe and Imihigo are home-grown solutions, not national development strategies.

human-capital-social-development-officer.stem: Which of the following is NOT a Rwandan Home-Grown Solution?
human-capital-social-development-officer.explanation: Gacaca, Girinka and Imihigo are home-grown solutions; the East African Community is a regional organisation, not a home-grown solution.

human-capital-social-development-officer.stem: What do you understand by "medium term" in planning?
options: A period longer than one (1) year but not exceeding three (3) years
A period longer than one (1) year but not exceeding five (5) years
A period of one (1) year but not exceeding three (3) years
human-capital-social-development-officer.explanation: Art 2(4) of Law 18/2017: medium term is a period longer than one year but not exceeding five years.

human-capital-social-development-officer.stem: Each State organ must monitor the implementation of individual performance contracts for its staff on the basis of indicators determined by ...
options: The head of the state organ
human-capital-social-development-officer.explanation: Art 16 of Law 18/2017: each State organ monitors individual staff performance contracts on the basis of indicators determined by the Ministry in charge of public service (MIFOTRA), by a Ministerial Order. None of the options names it (the head of the organ, MINALOC, MINECOFIN).

human-capital-social-development-officer.stem: HGS (as in Girinka, Umuganda, Gacaca) stands for:
human-capital-social-development-officer.explanation: Rwanda Governance Board is custodian of the Home Grown Solutions (HGS), which include Girinka, Umuganda and Gacaca.

human-capital-social-development-officer.stem: By 2050, Rwanda aspires to become a:
human-capital-social-development-officer.explanation: Vision 2050 targets upper-middle-income status by 2035 and high-income status by 2050.

human-capital-social-development-officer.stem: Imihigo are best described as:
human-capital-social-development-officer.explanation: Imihigo are performance contracts with targets that central and local institutions set and are evaluated on each year.

human-capital-social-development-officer.stem: Agenda 2063 of the AU is:
human-capital-social-development-officer.explanation: Agenda 2063 is the AU's blueprint and master plan for transforming Africa.

extras.title: Executive Secretary — Mock Exam 6
extras.summary: Practice for Executive Secretary recruitment: governance concepts and the law, plus administrative practice and service delivery.

questions.stem: The sectoral decentralization and service delivery have different issues. Which one is it?
options: The capacity gap in the matter related to Public Financial Management is still critical at decentralized entities
Limited availability and use of data and information management systems at Local Government level
Decentralized tax revenue sources are limited
questions.explanation: Limited availability and use of data and information management systems at Local Government level is a policy issue listed under Pillar 1, sectoral decentralization and service delivery. The public financial management and tax revenue issues belong to Pillar 2, fiscal and financial decentralization, and capacity development is Pillar 3.

questions.stem: The following are considered as cross cutting areas as they have been raised in the National Strategy for Transformation (NST 1). Which of the following answers is false?
questions.explanation: NST1 lists seven cross-cutting areas: capacity development, HIV/AIDS and NCDs, disability and social inclusion, gender and family promotion, regional integration and international positioning, disaster management, and environment and climate change. Security maintenance is not one of them.

questions.stem: Why is customer service so important to any institution?
options: It is required by law in order for the company to operate
Customer service is merely an illusion
Makes the line ups go faster
Gives a company a competitive advantage
questions.explanation: Good customer service builds loyalty, reputation and retention, which gives an institution a competitive advantage. The other options are false or irrelevant.

questions.stem: What makes you an effective problem solver?
questions.explanation: Effective problem solvers are systematic and logical in how they analyse a problem; presentation, speaking and proposal writing are communication skills, not problem-solving ones.

questions.stem: Why is there a direct link between local planning and national planning in Rwanda?
options: National plans take local priorities into account, local plans and Imihigo align with national priorities, and national programmes are implemented through local government
Local governments prepare their plans independently and national government does not use them
National planning is done only by MINECOFIN and Districts only spend the budget they receive
Local Imihigo are prepared without reference to the National Strategy for Transformation
questions.explanation: National plans take local priorities into account, local plans and Imihigo align with the NST and national priorities, and Districts implement national programmes.

questions.stem: Which form of decentralisation matches this definition: the transfer of functions and resources to lower-level units of the same administrative system while authority over decision-making and use of such resources remains with the centre?
questions.explanation: This is the policy definition of deconcentration: functions move to lower units but power and authority stay with the centre.

questions.stem: One of the specific priorities in the Human Development pillar of Vision 2050 is:
options: A diversified economy built upon future industries
A transformed workforce for higher productivity
Ease of mobility and efficient transport
questions.explanation: Vision 2050 Human Development pillar priorities are universal access to quality health care, universal access to quality education and a transformed workforce for higher productivity.

questions.stem: According to the previous (latest) census, the population of Rwanda is:
questions.explanation: The 5th Population and Housing Census (August 2022) enumerated 13,246,394 residents.

questions.stem: Girinka or One Cow per family programme is an important Home Grown Solution (HGS) with an intrinsic connection to the Rwandan culture. It was introduced in ..... by the Government of Rwanda (GoR) with the purpose to reduce child malnutrition and improve health and wellbeing of vulnerable citizens.
questions.explanation: The Government launched the Girinka programme in 2006, following the 2005-2006 rural household survey that showed high rural poverty and malnutrition.

questions.stem: Rwanda has developed the necessary policies and tools for attaining Vision 2020 as well as Vision 2050. By this, the term vision means:
options: A short term aspiration of what a country wants to achieve in specific period of time
A long term aspiration of what a country wants to achieve in specific period of time
A medium period plan that includes what a country wants to achieve
questions.explanation: Vision 2020 and Vision 2050 are Rwanda's long-term national frameworks (Vision 2050 sets the framework for 2020-2050), so a vision is a long-term aspiration of what a country wants to achieve in a specific period.

questions.stem: How many Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) are there?
questions.explanation: The 2030 Agenda has 17 Sustainable Development Goals.

questions.stem: The macroeconomic framework for NST1 requires an average GDP growth over the NST1 period for the country to remain on its path of economic transformation. What is that average?
questions.explanation: NST1 states an average GDP growth of 9.1% is needed over 2017-2024.

questions.stem: Rwanda's Imihigo performance contracts started in 2006. By 2024, for how many years had they been operational?
questions.explanation: Imihigo were introduced in 2006, so by 2024 they had been in place for 2024 - 2006 = 18 years.

questions.stem: Which one of the following is a home-grown solution?
questions.explanation: Gacaca is one of Rwanda's recognised home-grown solutions; vaccination, 12YBE and hybrid plants are not.

questions.stem: The quality of being able to deal with people, having human-relation skills and being friendly is called:
questions.explanation: Sociability is the quality of being sociable, i.e. friendly and good at relating to other people; integrity is honesty/moral soundness, self-confidence is trust in oneself.

questions.stem: Rwanda recognises the importance of culture and values in providing a platform for sustained socio-economic transformation and prosperity. Which of the following sets of values is reflected among the values of Rwanda in Vision 2050?
options: Justice, Kindness, Knowledge, Leadership, Loyalty, Work, Openness, Optimism, Peace
Self-determination, Solidarity and Dignity, Unity and Reconciliation, Identity
Respect, Responsibility, Security, Self-Respect, Service, Stability, Success
Authenticity, Achievement, Authority, Autonomy, Balance of gender, Compassion, Citizenship, Community
questions.explanation: Vision 2050 (Positive Values supporting Societal Transformation) names self-determination (Kwigira), solidarity and dignity (Agaciro), unity and Rwandan identity/culture, with unity and reconciliation as a key value, plus equity and inclusiveness.

questions.stem: After the 1994 Genocide against the Tutsi, Rwanda made a choice of three things. What are the three choices that Rwanda adopted?
options: Staying together, being accountable and thinking big
Education for all, Ndi Umunyarwanda and agriculture
questions.explanation: Vision 2050 describes Rwanda's post-genocide 'triple choice': staying together, being accountable and thinking big.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT among the five broad priorities (pillars) of Vision 2050?
options: High quality and standards of life
One cow for one poor family
questions.explanation: Vision 2050 is built on five pillars (e.g. quality of life, modern infrastructure and livelihoods, transformation for prosperity, values, international cooperation); 'One cow per poor family' (Girinka) is a home-grown programme, not a Vision 2050 priority.

questions.stem: NST1 considered seven (7) cross-cutting areas to attain inclusive and sustainable development. Which of the following is among the seven cross-cutting areas?
questions.explanation: The NST cross-cutting areas are capacity development, HIV/AIDS and NCDs, disability and social inclusion, environment and climate change, regional integration and international positioning, gender and family promotion, and disaster management.

questions.stem: Imihigo performance contracts were introduced in Rwanda in:
questions.explanation: The first Imihigo were signed in 2006 between the President and district mayors, at the start of the second phase of decentralisation.

questions.stem: Rwanda Vision 2020 was launched in:
questions.explanation: The Rwanda Vision 2020 document was issued by the Ministry of Finance and Economic Planning in Kigali in July 2000.

questions.stem: Vision 2050 aims for Rwanda to reach which income status by 2050?
questions.explanation: Vision 2050 sets Rwanda on a path to upper-middle-income status by 2035 and high-income status by 2050.

questions.stem: NST1 covered a seven-year period, namely:
questions.explanation: The National Strategy for Transformation (NST1) was the 7 Years Government Programme for 2017-2024.

questions.stem: NST2 covers a five-year period, namely:
questions.explanation: The Second National Strategy for Transformation (NST2) is the Five Years Government Programme 2024-2029.

questions.stem: Which development strategy preceded NST1?
questions.explanation: NST1 (2017-2024) followed the Economic Development and Poverty Reduction Strategy II (EDPRS 2, 2013-2018) as Rwanda's medium-term plan; Agaciro, Ubudehe and Imihigo are home-grown solutions, not national development strategies.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT a Rwandan Home-Grown Solution?
questions.explanation: Gacaca, Girinka and Imihigo are home-grown solutions; the East African Community is a regional organisation, not a home-grown solution.

questions.stem: In SMART objectives, the letter "M" stands for:
questions.explanation: In SMART objectives (Specific, Measurable, Achievable, Realistic, Time-bound), M stands for Measurable.

questions.stem: Which of the following is an example of an output indicator?
options: Number of households that received cows under Girinka
questions.explanation: An output indicator counts direct deliverables of an activity, such as households that received cows; the others are outcome or impact-level.

questions.stem: The District Development Plan (DDP), now the District Development Strategy, is aligned with:
questions.explanation: District development plans (now District Development Strategies) are aligned with the National Strategy for Transformation (NST) and Vision 2050.

questions.stem: The role of the Cell SEDO is to:
options: Plan, monitor and report on economic development activities in the Cell
questions.explanation: The Cell Socio-Economic Development Officer coordinates planning, monitoring and reporting of socio-economic activities in the Cell under the Cell Executive Secretary.

questions.stem: A "baseline" is:
options: Initial data showing the situation before an intervention begins
questions.explanation: A baseline is the initial data describing the situation before an intervention begins, used to measure change later.

questions.stem: M&E stands for:
questions.explanation: M&E stands for Monitoring and Evaluation.

questions.stem: How many priority areas are in the Transformational Governance pillar of NST1?
questions.explanation: NST1 (2017-2024) says the Transformational Governance pillar is achieved through 6 priority areas.

questions.stem: The NST1 macroeconomic framework requires an average GDP growth over the NST1 period of:
questions.explanation: NST1 states an average GDP growth of 9.1% is needed over 2017-2024.

questions.stem: When did the United Nations Millennium Development Goals (MDGs) start?
questions.explanation: The Millennium Declaration containing the MDGs came from the UN Millennium Summit of 6-8 September 2000, so November, June and December 2000 are all wrong.

questions.stem: What do you understand by "medium term" in planning?
options: A period longer than one (1) year but not exceeding three (3) years
A period longer than one (1) year but not exceeding five (5) years
A period of one (1) year but not exceeding three (3) years
questions.explanation: Art 2(4) of Law 18/2017: medium term is a period longer than one year but not exceeding five years.

questions.stem: The United Nations Millennium Development Goals (MDGs) are the eight goals set by the ..... UN member states.
questions.explanation: The Millennium Declaration setting out the MDGs was adopted by 189 UN Member States, so 179, 184 and 186 are all wrong.

questions.stem: Results-based performance management respects phases. How many?
questions.explanation: Art 4 of Law 18/2017: results-based performance management respects five (5) phases (planning, budgeting, implementation, monitoring, evaluation). Five is not Six, Seven or Eight, so "None of the mentioned" is correct.

questions.stem: Who has the responsibility to prepare the reference documents related to the monitoring of the implementation of performance contracts of the state organs?
options: The head of the state organ
questions.explanation: Art 15 of Law 18/2017: the Office of the Prime Minister prepares reference documents related to the monitoring of the implementation of performance contracts of the organs. None of the options (head of the organ, MINALOC, MINECOFIN) names the OPM.

questions.stem: Each State organ must monitor the implementation of individual performance contracts for its staff on the basis of indicators determined by ...
options: The head of the state organ
questions.explanation: Art 16 of Law 18/2017: each State organ monitors individual staff performance contracts on the basis of indicators determined by the Ministry in charge of public service (MIFOTRA), by a Ministerial Order. None of the options names it (the head of the organ, MINALOC, MINECOFIN).

questions.stem: Performance contracts of an organ and individual staff performance contracts are evaluated on the basis of ...
options: Criteria fixed by the Prime Minister's Office
Criteria fixed by the Presidential Office
questions.explanation: Art 19(1) of Law 18/2017: organ and individual staff performance contracts are evaluated on the basis of the results achieved in relation to the expected results, not on criteria fixed by one of the named offices. (Art 19(2): organ evaluation follows yearly guidance of the Office of the Prime Minister; that is guidance for organ contracts only, while the stem covers both organ and individual contracts.)

questions.stem: When was the Imihigo performance contract started in local government?
questions.explanation: Imihigo started in 2006 with district performance contracts.

questions.stem: HGS (as in Girinka, Umuganda, Gacaca) stands for:
questions.explanation: Rwanda Governance Board is custodian of the Home Grown Solutions (HGS), which include Girinka, Umuganda and Gacaca.

questions.stem: By the term "vision" (Vision 2020 / Vision 2050) we mean:
options: A short term aspiration of what a country wants to achieve
A long term aspiration of what a country wants to achieve in a specific period of time
A medium period plan that includes what a country wants to achieve
questions.explanation: Vision 2050 sets out the long-term strategic direction (30 years) of the country; the medium-term plans are the NSTs, so a vision is a long-term aspiration.

questions.stem: The Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) are:
questions.explanation: The 2030 Agenda has 17 Sustainable Development Goals.

questions.stem: When were the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) adopted?
questions.explanation: The 2030 Agenda with its Sustainable Development Goals was adopted by world leaders at the UN in September 2015.

questions.stem: According to the 5th Rwanda Population and Housing Census (RPHC5), which is the most densely populated District?
questions.explanation: Kicukiro is the most densely populated District (about 2,944 inhabitants per sq km), ahead of Nyarugenge and Gasabo.

questions.stem: According to the 5th Rwanda Population and Housing Census (RPHC5), which is the least populated District?
questions.explanation: Nyaruguru has the lowest population of all Districts (about 318,900 residents).

questions.stem: According to the 5th Rwanda Population and Housing Census (RPHC5), what is the adult (15 years and above) literacy rate in 2022?
questions.explanation: About 79% (6.5 million) of the 8.2 million adults aged 15+ can read and write with understanding in any language.

questions.stem: According to the 5th Rwanda Population and Housing Census (RPHC5), youth (16-30 years) constitute ... of the Rwandan population.
questions.explanation: Youth aged 16-30 are 27.1% (3.6 million) of the population.

extras.title: Executive Secretary — Mock Exam 7
extras.summary: Practice for Executive Secretary recruitment: governance concepts and the law, plus administrative practice and service delivery.

questions.stem: By 2050, Rwanda aspires to become a:
questions.explanation: Vision 2050 targets upper-middle-income status by 2035 and high-income status by 2050.

questions.stem: DDS in district planning means:
questions.explanation: District Development Strategy (DDS) is the five-year district plan aligned with NST2 and Vision 2050.

questions.stem: Vision 2050 aims to make Rwanda a:
questions.explanation: Vision 2050 targets upper-middle-income status by 2035 and high-income status by 2050.

questions.stem: Imihigo are best described as:
questions.explanation: Imihigo are performance contracts with targets that central and local institutions set and are evaluated on each year.

questions.stem: What does NST2 stand for?
questions.explanation: NST2 is the National Strategy for Transformation 2 (2024-2029), the successor to NST1.

questions.stem: Which of these is a pillar of NST1?
questions.explanation: NST1 (2017-2024) had three pillars: Economic Transformation, Social Transformation and Transformational Governance.

questions.stem: Which is NOT a pillar of Vision 2050?
questions.explanation: Vision 2050's five pillars are Human Development, Competitiveness and Integration, Agriculture for Wealth Creation, Urbanisation and Agglomeration, and Accountable and Capable State Institutions; Mining for Export is not one.

questions.stem: Agenda 2063 of the AU is:
questions.explanation: Agenda 2063 is the AU's blueprint and master plan for transforming Africa.

questions.stem: By "vision" we mean:
options: a short-term plan for one year
a long-term aspiration of what a country wants to achieve
questions.explanation: A vision is a long-term aspiration of what a country wants to achieve, as in Vision 2050.

questions.stem: Imihigo are:
questions.explanation: Imihigo are performance contracts that leaders and institutions sign and are evaluated on.

questions.stem: SDG 2 aims to achieve:
questions.explanation: Sustainable Development Goal 2 is "Zero Hunger": end hunger, achieve food security and improved nutrition and promote sustainable agriculture.

questions.stem: SEDO stands for:
questions.explanation: SEDO is the Cell-level civil-service post of Social (Socio-) Economic Development Officer, advertised under that title by districts through MIFOTRA recruitment.

questions.stem: The African Union replaced the:
questions.explanation: The African Union was launched in 2002 as the successor to the Organisation of African Unity (1963-1999).

questions.stem: Rwanda's official languages are:
questions.explanation: Under Article 8 of the Constitution, Kinyarwanda is the national language and Kinyarwanda, French and English are official languages (Kiswahili was added in 2017).

questions.stem: Where is the EAC headquarters located?
questions.explanation: The East African Community headquarters is in Arusha, Tanzania.

questions.stem: Decentralisation aims at:
options: empowering citizens to take part in decision making
questions.explanation: Rwanda's decentralisation policy aims to enhance citizens' participation in initiating, making, implementing and monitoring decisions that affect them by transferring power and resources to local level.

questions.stem: According to RPHC 2022 (Fifth Population and Housing Census), the population of Rwanda is:
questions.explanation: The Fifth Population and Housing Census (August 2022) enumerated 13,246,394 residents. The ticked number has two digits transposed.

questions.stem: By 2050, Rwanda aspires to achieve a GDP per capita of:
questions.explanation: Vision 2050 targets a GDP per capita of over USD 12,476 by 2050 (high-income status). USD 4,036 is the 2035 target for upper-middle-income status.

questions.stem: The following are Imihigo programme ambitious aims, except:
options: Instill a culture of regular performance evaluation
Ensure stakeholder ownership of the development agenda
questions.explanation: Imihigo aims include speeding up implementation, stakeholder ownership of the development agenda, accountability and transparency, results-oriented performance, competitiveness, and instilling a culture of regular performance evaluation. Equitable distribution of resources is not among the stated aims.

questions.stem: According to the fifth Rwanda Population and Housing Census, which is the most densely populated District in Rwanda?
questions.explanation: RPHC5 reports Kicukiro as the most densely populated district (2,944 inhabitants per km2), ahead of Nyarugenge (2,830) and Gasabo (2,056).

questions.stem: By definition integrity is:
options: the obligation and authority to take the necessary actions to ensure success.
a disposition to be humble; a lack of false pride
the act of consistency of actions, values, methods, measures, principles, expectations and outcome
The spirit of not putting one's self first but being willing to give one's time and resources for the benefit of others
questions.explanation: Integrity is consistency of actions, values and principles, being honest with strong moral principles. The other options define responsibility, humility and selflessness.

questions.stem: Which one of the following is not a strategy for mainstreaming cross-cutting issues?
options: Disaster management, environment and climate change
questions.explanation: NST1 names capacity development, disaster management, environment and climate change, and regional integration among its cross-cutting areas to be mainstreamed. "Sequencing of interventions" is not one of them.

questions.stem: The Vision 2050 aspirations focus on which of the following broad priorities?
options: Rwanda's progress has been grounded in favorable transformational factors
Increase Citizens' Participation and Engagement in Development
questions.explanation: NST1 states that Vision 2050 aspirations focus on five broad priorities: high quality and standards of life, modern infrastructure and livelihoods, transformation for prosperity, values for Vision 2050, and international cooperation and positioning. Citizen participation and justice are NST1 governance priorities, not these five.

questions.stem: How many Districts with legal personality do we have in Rwanda?
questions.explanation: Rwanda has 30 districts, but the three districts of the City of Kigali (Nyarugenge, Gasabo, Kicukiro) have no legal personality under the City of Kigali law, so 27 districts have legal personality.

questions.stem: Which one of the following is not a value linked to unity?
options: Sharing of the first fruits of a harvest
questions.explanation: The values linked to unity are Rwandanness, covenant, conviviality, sharing of the first fruits of a harvest, solidarity, use of Kinyarwanda, love, satisfaction and tolerance. Self-confidence belongs to the values linked to dignity.

questions.stem: Fill in the missing: The Vision 2050 was requested by ...........
questions.explanation: Vision 2050 was requested by the 13th National Umushyikirano Council in 2015, after which broad stakeholder consultations were held.

questions.stem: Which one of the following is not a pillar of the national decentralization policy?
questions.explanation: The five pillars of the 2021 National Decentralization Policy are sectoral decentralization and service delivery, fiscal and financial decentralization, capacity development for decentralized entities, local economic development, and governance imperatives for national transformation. Community mobilization is only a priority area under the governance pillar.

questions.stem: As at 2026, who is the head (Chancellor) of the Chancellery for Heroes, National Orders and Decorations of Honour (CHENO), according to its official website?
options: H.E Paul Kagame the President of the Republic of Rwanda
questions.explanation: CHENO's website names François Ngarambe as Chancellor (appointed August 2023); the Chancellor leads the Chancellery and is its legal representative.

questions.stem: The pillars of Vision 2050 are:
options: Economic transformation, rural development and accountable governance

Capacity Development, HIV/AIDS and Non-Communicable Diseases, Disability and Social Inclusion, Environment and Climate Change, Regional Integration and International Positioning, Gender and Family Promotion, Disaster Management
Human Development, Competitiveness and Integration, Agriculture for Wealth Creation, Urbanization and Accountable and Capable Institutions
questions.explanation: Vision 2050 has five pillars: Human Development; Competitiveness and Integration; Agriculture for Wealth Creation; Urbanization and Agglomeration; and Accountable and Capable State Institutions. The long list in the second option is NST1 cross-cutting areas.

questions.stem: As per the fifth Rwanda Population and Housing Census, which is the least populated District in Rwanda?
questions.explanation: RPHC5 gives the lowest district population as 318,900 residents in Nyaruguru (with Nyabihu close behind). Kayonza, Rulindo and Gisagara are all larger, so none of the three named districts is correct.

questions.stem: Which one of the following is a pillar of Vision 2050?
questions.explanation: Vision 2050's pillars are Human Development, Competitiveness and Integration, Agriculture for Wealth Creation, Urbanization and Agglomeration, and Accountable and Capable State Institutions. Solidarity and Dignity (Agaciro) is a shared value, and Economic Transformation is an NST1 pillar.

questions.stem: What is human security as noted in General Assembly resolution 66/290?
options: an approach to assist Member States in identifying and addressing widespread and cross-cutting challenges to the survival, livelihood and dignity of their people
a strategy to assist Member States in identifying and addressing widespread and cross-cutting challenges to the survival, livelihood and dignity of their people
A mechanism fixed to assist Member States in identifying and addressing widespread and cross-cutting challenges to the survival, livelihood and dignity of their people
questions.explanation: Resolution 66/290 says human security is 'an approach' to assist Member States; it does not call it a strategy or a mechanism.

questions.stem: Which one of the following is NOT a criterion used by RGB to qualify an innovation as a Home Grown Solution?
options: An innovation that has proved to be a solution to a particular problem
An innovation that addresses a challenge in a new and different way, often through simpler and more effective approaches
An innovation or initiative rooted in the Rwandan cultural heritage and values
A practice imported from another country and applied unchanged, without adaptation to Rwanda
questions.explanation: RGB lists five criteria for a Home Grown Solution, including all four options shown (the post-genocide political philosophy criterion is one of them), so the item has no correct option as written.

questions.stem: Every year, the ...... shall determine the priority areas under which joint imihigo should be formulated.
options: National Institute of Statistics of Rwanda
questions.explanation: Law No 18/2017 Art. 9: at the annual planning stage the Office of the Prime Minister specifies the list of priority activities requiring joint planning (joint imihigo).

questions.stem: The Imihigo program is based on main objectives. How many are there?
questions.explanation: The Government of Rwanda presentation on Imihigo lists seven objectives: speed up implementation, stakeholder ownership, accountability and transparency, results orientation, innovation and competitiveness, zeal and determination, and a culture of results.

questions.stem: The NST1 has considered ... cross-cutting areas to attain inclusive and sustainable development.
questions.explanation: NST1 lists seven cross-cutting areas: capacity development, HIV/AIDS and NCDs, disability and social inclusion, gender and family promotion, regional integration, disaster management, environment and climate change.

questions.stem: How many lakes in Rwanda are shared with neighbouring countries?
questions.explanation: Three lakes straddle borders: Lake Kivu (with DR Congo), and Lake Rweru and Lake Cyohoha South (with Burundi). Lake Ihema and Cyohoha North lie wholly in Rwanda.

questions.stem: The Cabinet of Rwanda consists of:
options: the Ministers and Ministers of State
the Prime Minister, Ministers, Ministers of State and other members nominated by the President
the Prime Minister, Ministers, Ministers of State
questions.explanation: The Constitution says the Cabinet comprises the Prime Minister, Ministers, Ministers of State and other members determined by the President.

questions.stem: The law governing results-based performance management in branches of Government is:
questions.explanation: The law is Law No 18/2017 of 28/04/2017 governing Results-Based Performance Management in branches of Government.

questions.stem: After the 1994 genocide, the government of National Unity was established ..........:
questions.explanation: The Government of National Unity was sworn in on 19 July 1994, the date Rwanda marks each year as the start of national unity and reconstruction.

questions.stem: Which one of the following is not part of the ambitious aims of the Imihigo programme?
options: Ensure stakeholder ownership of the development agenda
Instill a culture of regular performance evaluation
questions.explanation: The stated aims of Imihigo include speeding up implementation, stakeholder ownership of the development agenda, accountability and transparency, and results-oriented performance. Equitable distribution of resources is not one of them.

questions.stem: Which of the following is one of the five pillars of Vision 2050?
options: Human Resource Development and a Knowledge-based Economy
Good Governance and a Capable State
questions.explanation: The five pillars of Vision 2050 are Human Development, Competitiveness and Integration, Agriculture for Wealth Creation, Urbanization and Agglomeration, and Accountable and Capable State Institutions. 'Good Governance and a Capable State' and the other two options are Vision 2020 pillar wordings.

questions.stem: In the implementation of decentralization policy since its adoption in 2001, the following major challenge hindered the effective decentralization processes:
questions.explanation: The policy's list of major challenges includes sectoral decentralization that is yet to foster strategic linkages. Constant development partner commitment and continuous leadership commitment are lessons learnt (strengths), and capacity development is a pillar, whereas the challenge is capacity constraints.

questions.stem: Which one of the following is among the main duties of the socio-economic development officer?
options: To identify socio-economic development needs at the Cell level and accordingly take decision on response measures
To facilitate gathering data related to the employment status within the cell
To prepare and sign documents at Cell level
To elaborate him/her self the programs of community works
questions.explanation: The Cell Socio-Economic Development Officer advertisement lists: identify needs and advise on response measures (not take decisions), prepare documents for the Executive Secretary to sign (not sign them), elaborate community-works programmes under the Executive Secretary's supervision, and facilitate gathering data on the employment status within the Cell.

questions.stem: A homegrown solution consisting in pledging to accomplish a certain number of tasks for which someone is held accountable is called:
questions.explanation: Imihigo is Rwanda's home-grown approach of signing performance contracts, in which institutions and leaders pledge targets for the year and are held accountable. Ubudehe is collective action and categorisation, not a performance pledge.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT a pillar of NST1 (2017-2024)?
questions.explanation: NST1 (2017-2024) had three pillars: Economic Transformation, Social Transformation and Transformational Governance. "Socio-economic transformation" is not a pillar, so as written (A, B and C are all pillars) the item has no single correct option.

questions.stem: To be classified as a National Hero in Rwanda, a person shall meet ..... criteria:
questions.explanation: CHENO lists nine characteristics a person must meet to be classified as a National Hero: integrity, patriotism, sacrifice, vision, bravery, being an example, truthfulness, magnanimity and humanity.

questions.stem: When were the SDGs set up?
questions.explanation: The 2030 Agenda with the 17 Sustainable Development Goals was adopted by the UN in September 2015.

questions.stem: Fill in the blanks: As outlined in Vision 2050, by 2050 Rwanda aspires to achieve a per capita income of ...... and a life expectancy of ......
questions.explanation: Vision 2050 targets GDP per capita of over USD 12,476 and life expectancy of 73 years by 2050.

questions.stem: The Economic and Human Capital Development Officer has the duty to collect and consolidate data on specific social, health and education programs and prepare the reports. What are the main parts of any formal written report?
options: Title or Cover page - Table of contents - Introduction - Body - Recommendations
Title or Cover page - Introduction - Executive summary - Body - Recommendations - Conclusion
Title or Cover page - Table of contents - Executive summary - Introduction - Body - Conclusion - Recommendations
Title or Cover page - Executive summary - Main content - Conclusion - Recommendations
questions.explanation: A formal report has a title page, table of contents, executive summary, introduction, body, conclusion and recommendations, with the executive summary before the introduction.

extras.title: Executive Secretary — Mock Exam 8
extras.summary: Practice for Executive Secretary recruitment: governance concepts and the law, plus administrative practice and service delivery.

questions.stem: At the district level, the strategic plan guiding all activities is the DDS. It means, in full words:
questions.explanation: DDS stands for District Development Strategy, the five-year district plan that is aligned with NST1 and turned into annual action plans and Imihigo.

questions.stem: How many cross-cutting areas does the NST1 have?
questions.explanation: NST1 has seven cross-cutting areas: capacity development, HIV/AIDS and NCDs, disability and social inclusion, gender and family promotion, regional integration and international positioning, disaster management, and environment and climate change.

questions.stem: The SDGs were adopted by all United Nations member states in:
questions.explanation: The 2030 Agenda with the 17 SDGs was adopted by all UN member states at the UN summit of 25-27 September 2015.

questions.stem: How many community works supervising organs are there at national level?
questions.explanation: At national, provincial and Kigali City levels there are two organs: the Steering Committee and the Technical Committee.

questions.stem: In which condition does the competent authority dismiss a public servant without requesting the disciplinary committee to meet?
options: If a public servant has deserted his or her job for a period equal to or greater than ten (10) days and has not provided written explanations within the time limit provided for by law
If a public servant has deserted his or her job for a period equal to or greater than fifteen (15) days and has not provided written explanations within the time limit provided for by law
If a public servant has deserted his or her job for a period equal to or greater than thirty (30) days and has not provided written explanations within the time limit provided for by law
questions.explanation: Article 34 of the Presidential Order on professional ethics says the competent authority dismisses, without asking the disciplinary committee to meet, a public servant who has deserted work for seven (7) days or more and has given no written explanations in time. 10, 15 and 30 days are all wrong.

questions.stem: The proceedings against a public servant over a disciplinary fault punishable by a sanction of the second category are concluded within:
options: One (1) month counted from the date on which he or she was requested to provide explanations
Three (3) months counted from the date on which he or she was requested to provide explanations
Two (2) months counted from the date on which he or she was requested to provide explanations
questions.explanation: Proceedings for a second-category fault must be concluded within three months from the date the servant was requested to provide explanations (first category: 30 consecutive days).

questions.stem: A new governor is appointed in the province where your sector is located. As Executive Secretary you are asked to inform him about the attributions, organization and functioning of community works supervising committees. How many times do these committees meet at provincial level?
questions.explanation: Committees at provincial and Kigali City levels meet four times a year and whenever necessary (national: twice a year; other entities: monthly).

questions.stem: The attributions, organisation and functioning of community works supervising committees and their relations with other organs are determined by which Prime Minister's Order?
questions.explanation: It is Prime Minister's Order N 58/03 of 24/08/2009 (Official Gazette N 46 of 16/11/2009).

questions.stem: A sector Executive Secretary is supposed to have enough information about the law on fighting against corruption in Rwanda. What is that law?
questions.explanation: The law on fighting against corruption is Law N 54/2018 of 13/08/2018.

questions.stem: Under Presidential Order N° 072/01 of 31/10/2023, how often does the Advisory Council to fight against corruption and injustice at sector level hold its regular meetings (in addition to meetings whenever necessary)?
questions.explanation: The Advisory Council at Sector level meets quarterly (four times a year) and whenever necessary, so none of 2, 3 or 6 is right.

questions.stem: How many members does the community works Steering Committee have at national level?
questions.explanation: The national Steering Committee has eleven members, namely the ministers listed in the order (local government, defence, infrastructure, agriculture, internal security, public service, education, finance, youth, gender, natural resources).

questions.stem: How many members does the community works Technical Committee have at provincial level?
questions.explanation: The Technical Committee of a Province or Kigali City has six members: officers in charge of specific programmes, planning, environment, good governance, the Women's Council coordinator and a National Youth Council representative.

questions.stem: How many members does the community works Technical Committee have at district level?
questions.explanation: The district Technical Committee has ten listed members (vice mayor economic affairs, executive secretary, police commander, officers for education, environment and social affairs, women and youth council representatives, private sector, NGOs).

questions.stem: How many members does the community works Technical Committee have at sector level?
questions.explanation: The sector Technical Committee has six listed categories: the executive secretary, the cell executive secretaries, the agriculture officer, the women and youth council coordinators and the Intore representatives.

questions.stem: In which conditions does the competent authority dismiss a public servant without requesting the disciplinary committee to meet: if he or she has deserted his or her job for a period equal to or greater than ...
questions.explanation: Article 34 of the Presidential Order on professional ethics sets desertion for seven (7) days or more (with no written explanation in time) as the ground for dismissal without convening the disciplinary committee, so ten, fifteen and thirty days are all wrong.

questions.stem: How many community works supervising organs are there at provincial level?
questions.explanation: The Province and Kigali City each have two organs: the Steering Committee and the Technical Committee.

questions.stem: Rwanda is one of the countries in the world that have focused on the fight against corruption through its institutions. A public servant such as the Executive Secretary of a sector is supposed to know the law on fighting corruption and the Presidential Order determining the advisory council to fight against corruption and injustice. What is the law?
questions.explanation: The law on fighting against corruption is Law N° 54/2018 of 13/08/2018.

questions.stem: According to Law No 45/2011 governing contracts, a contract is:
options: A promise or a set of promises the performance of which the law recognizes as an obligation and the breach of which the law provides a remedy
Only a written agreement signed by two parties
Only an oral agreement between two parties
An agreement that is never enforceable by law
questions.explanation: Law No 45/2011 defines a contract as a promise or a set of promises whose performance the law recognises as an obligation and whose breach the law provides a remedy for. It does not require writing or signature.

questions.stem: How is the Constitution of the Republic of Rwanda officially referred to?
options: The Constitution of the Republic of Rwanda of 2015
The Constitution of the Republic of Rwanda as revised in 2015
The Constitution of the Republic of Rwanda of 2003, revised in 2015
The Constitution of the Republic of Rwanda of 2003, replaced in 2015
questions.explanation: The current Constitution is the one adopted in 2003 and revised in 2015 (Official Gazette Special of 24/12/2015); it was amended, not replaced.

questions.stem: Why should Sector Strategic Plans and District Development Strategies take into consideration HIV/AIDS and non-communicable diseases?
options: Because both are among the cross-cutting areas approved in NST1
Because they are the only diseases affecting development
questions.explanation: HIV/AIDS and non-communicable diseases are one of the cross-cutting areas of the National Strategy for Transformation, which must be mainstreamed in Sector Strategic Plans and District Development Strategies.

questions.stem: Which of the following correctly describes the duties of the Director of Planning, Monitoring and Evaluation (M&E) at District level?
options: Providing technical support for strategies implementing national policies and District Council decisions, monitoring strategic plans, action plans and Imihigo, and ensuring stakeholder participation in planning and M&E
Recruiting and dismissing all District staff and approving the District budget
Approving the District Imihigo on behalf of the District Council
Auditing the District financial statements and reporting directly to the Auditor General
questions.explanation: The District Director of Planning, Monitoring and Evaluation provides technical support for strategies localising national policies and implementing Council decisions, monitors the strategic plan, action plan and Imihigo, and ensures stakeholder participation in planning and M&E.

questions.stem: What is the relationship between Results-Based Management (RBM) and Imihigo in Rwanda?
options: Imihigo originated from RBM and was translated into Kinyarwanda
RBM is applied through Imihigo, where specific targets are defined to be achieved within a specific period
Imihigo is only a practice used by local government
questions.explanation: Imihigo is Rwanda's home-grown performance-contract tool through which results-based management is applied: targets are set and evaluated each fiscal year, by ministries, boards and districts alike.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a decentralized administrative entity with legal personality?
options: Kicukiro District in the City of Kigali
questions.explanation: Under Law 22/2019 Article 3 the City of Kigali has legal personality but the Districts, Sectors, Cells and Villages of the City of Kigali are decentralised entities WITHOUT legal personality (so Kicukiro District is out). Sectors (Kacyiru) have no legal personality (Law 065/2021 Art 5). A Province is not a decentralised administrative entity at all (not in the list of Article 2 of Law 87/2013). So none of the options qualifies.

questions.stem: Which of the following lists the three pillars of NST1 (2017-2024)?
options: Economic Transformation, Social Transformation and Transformational Governance
Economic Transformation, Social Transformation and Environmental Sustainability
Economic Growth, Human Development and Regional Integration
questions.explanation: NST1 (2017-2024) rests on three pillars: Economic Transformation, Social Transformation and Transformational Governance.

questions.stem: According to Rwanda's laws governing public finance, which authorities are responsible for determining the general regulations on financial management for decentralized administrative entities with legal personality?
options: An order jointly issued by the Minister in charge of Local Government and the Minister in charge of Finance.
An order issued by the Minister in charge of Finance alone.
An order issued by the Minister in charge of Local Government alone.
A decision adopted by the District Council.
questions.explanation: Marks said a joint order, but the law gives this power to an Order of the Minister in charge of Finance alone (the current PFM organic law likewise provides for Ministerial Orders of the Minister in charge of public finance).

questions.stem: How many cross-cutting areas are included in NST1?
questions.explanation: NST1 has seven cross-cutting areas: capacity development, HIV/AIDS and NCDs, disability and social inclusion, gender and family promotion, regional integration, environment and climate change, and disaster management.

questions.stem: Which law currently governs persons and family matters, including civil status registration, in Rwanda?
options: Law No. 32/2016 of 28/08/2016 governing persons and family.
Law No. 001/2020 of 02/02/2020 amending Law No. 32/2016.
Law No. 71/2024 of 26/06/2024 governing persons and family.
Law No. 42/1988 instituting the preliminary title and Book One of the Civil Code.
questions.explanation: Law No 71/2024 of 26/06/2024 governing persons and family repealed Law 32/2016 (as modified) and Law 27/2016 and now governs civil status registration.

questions.stem: What does SWOT analysis stand for?
questions.explanation: SWOT stands for Strengths, Weaknesses, Opportunities and Threats.

questions.stem: Which of the following best describes Results-Based Management (RBM)?
options: A management approach in which an organisation applies its processes and resources to achieve agreed, clearly defined results that can be measured
A budgeting method that shares funds equally among departments regardless of results
A system for recording staff attendance and working hours
A procurement method for selecting the cheapest supplier
questions.explanation: All three statements are accepted descriptions of RBM: a management strategy/approach focused on performance, in which processes and resources are applied to achieve agreed, measurable results.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT one of the NST1 cross-cutting areas?
questions.explanation: Security Maintenance is not a cross-cutting area; the NST1 areas are capacity development, regional integration, gender and family promotion, HIV/AIDS and NCDs, disability and social inclusion, environment and climate change, and disaster management.

questions.stem: What does NIDA stand for?
questions.explanation: NIDA is the National Identification Agency, established by Law No 43/2011 of 31/10/2011.

questions.stem: According to the law governing Districts, the District Executive Secretariat comprises:
options: The District Executive Secretary and his/her Administrative Assistant
The District Executive Secretary and Sector Executive Secretaries
The District Executive Secretary and other staff appointed in accordance with relevant laws
All permanent District staff on the payroll
questions.explanation: The District Executive Secretariat comprises the District Executive Secretary and other staff appointed in accordance with relevant laws.

questions.stem: What is the implication of the publication of Law No. 065/2021 of 09/10/2021 governing Districts?
options: Law No. 87/2013 of 11/09/2013 was replaced in its entirety
Both laws can be consulted by the Sector Executive Secretary
The Sector Executive Secretary should refer only to the new District law
questions.explanation: Article 68 of Law 065/2021 repeals Law 87/2013 EXCEPT Article 84 (Security Committee) and Article 136 (District Coordinating Committee), so A (replaced in its entirety) is false; the Sector Executive Secretary's duties are now in Presidential Order 001/01 of 06/02/2023 on the Sector, Cell and Village, so C (refer only to the new District law) is false; and B (both laws can be consulted) is not a correct statement of the implication because the surviving Articles do not govern the Sector. "None is correct" is the keyed answer.

questions.stem: According to the planning and budgeting calendar, why does MINECOFIN issue a planning and budgeting call circular to Chief Budget Managers?
options: To guide them in the planning and budgeting process for the concerned fiscal year
To approve their budgets on behalf of Parliament
To carry out monitoring and evaluation of their performance
questions.explanation: The first planning and budget call circular guides budget agencies in the planning process for the fiscal year and MTEF; ceilings come later through the PBOP and second circular, and M&E is not its purpose.

questions.stem: Who is responsible for recruiting Sector staff?
questions.explanation: Sector Executive Secretariat staff are employees of the District, and the District Executive Committee has the power to recruit staff (the District Council approves the Executive Secretary and Auditor).

questions.stem: What is the hierarchy of laws in Rwanda?
options: International laws, Constitution, Organic Laws, Instructions
Constitution, International Laws, Organic Laws, Instructions
International laws, Constitution, Instructions, Organic Laws
questions.explanation: Article 95 gives the hierarchy: Constitution, organic law, international treaties and agreements ratified by Rwanda, ordinary law, orders. None of the three listed orderings matches.

questions.stem: How many civil status registers are there?
questions.explanation: Law 71/2024 lists seven civil status registers: birth, death, marriage, guardianship, recognition of children born out of wedlock, adoption and divorce.

questions.stem: Respect for the hierarchy of laws is fundamental to the rule of law. Which of the following sets of instruments does the hierarchy of laws rank against each other?
options: The Constitution, organic laws and orders (such as Ministerial Orders), among others
Court judgments, customary practices and opinions of Ministers
Party manifestos, Cabinet speeches and press statements
Imihigo contracts, annual reports and meeting minutes
questions.explanation: The hierarchy of laws ranks the Constitution, organic laws, international treaties, ordinary laws and orders (including Ministerial Orders), so all listed instruments are covered.

questions.stem: Which of the following cannot be treated as a cash equivalent or liquid cash item?
questions.explanation: Coins, money orders and cheques are cash or near-cash items; an investment is held for investment purposes and is not treated as cash or a cash equivalent.

questions.stem: How many local government councils were responsible for approving annual plans and budgets for the 2022/2023 financial year, considering the City of Kigali's special administrative arrangement?
questions.explanation: Rwanda has 27 districts with their own councils plus the City of Kigali council; the three Kigali districts (Gasabo, Kicukiro, Nyarugenge) are not counted because they have no legal personality, so 27 + 1 = 28 councils approve budgets.

questions.stem: According to the law governing decentralised administrative entities, when does the financial year begin and end?
options: It begins on 15 July and ends on 15 June of the following year
It begins on 1 July and ends on 30 June of the following year
It begins on 1 July and ends on 30 June of the same year
It begins on 1 July and ends on 30 July of the following year
questions.explanation: The decentralisation law states that the financial year begins on 1 July and ends on 30 June of the following year.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT an advantage of maintaining a Cash Book?
options: It improves accuracy in recording financial transactions
It helps detect errors and differences in cash balances
It removes the need to keep supporting documents for transactions
questions.explanation: A cash book records all cash and bank receipts and payments, which makes bank reconciliation possible, improves recording accuracy and exposes errors or differences between the book and bank balances, so all three statements are advantages.

questions.stem: In the context of Vision 2020 and Vision 2050, the term "vision" means:
options: A long-term aspiration of what a country wants to achieve
questions.explanation: Vision 2020 and Vision 2050 are long-term national aspirations, implemented through medium-term strategies such as NST1 and NST2.

questions.stem: At Cell level, what are the responsibilities of the Cell?
options: Provide basic services, collect numerical data and encourage participation in sustainable development
Implement development programmes and promote good governance/social welfare
Gather welfare data, maintain security, inform residents about government programmes and carry out delegated decisions
questions.explanation: The Cell's responsibilities are to provide basic services, collect numerical data, and encourage the population to contribute to and participate in sustainable development activities.

questions.stem: How many organs manage the Cell?
questions.explanation: The Cell has three management organs: the Cell Council, the Executive Secretariat and the Consultative Committee on Development of the Cell.

questions.stem: What is the main purpose of Rwanda's National Strategy for Transformation 2 (NST2)?
options: To replace Vision 2050 with a short-term development plan
To guide Rwanda's national transformation priorities for 2024 to 2029
To focus exclusively on agricultural development
To address only the challenges experienced during NST1
questions.explanation: NST2 is the five-year government programme for 2024-2029 that implements Vision 2050 priorities.

questions.stem: Which period did Rwanda's first National Strategy for Transformation (NST1) cover?
questions.explanation: NST1 covered 2017 to 2024.

questions.stem: What average annual GDP growth rate does NST2 target over its implementation period?
questions.explanation: NST2 targets an annual average real GDP growth of 9.3% over 2024-2029.

questions.stem: How many jobs does NST2 aim to create over five years?
questions.explanation: NST2 sets a target of creating 1.25 million productive and decent jobs over five years (250,000 a year).

questions.stem: Why is Vision 2050 important to NST2?
options: Vision 2050 provides the long-term direction that NST2 helps implement.
Vision 2050 focuses only on the annual national budget.
Vision 2050 applies only to the private sector.
questions.explanation: NST2 is the medium-term strategy that takes the country closer to Vision 2050, which gives the long-term direction.

extras.title: Executive Secretary — Mock Exam 9
extras.summary: Practice for Executive Secretary recruitment: governance concepts and the law, plus administrative practice and service delivery.

questions.stem: Which approach provides the strongest basis for evaluating whether NST2 is improving citizens' welfare?
options: Counting the number of policy documents published
Measuring only the amount of money allocated to projects
Counting meetings held by local leaders
Examining indicators such as employment, income, access to services, nutrition, and economic productivity
questions.explanation: Welfare is best judged with outcome indicators such as employment, income, access to services and nutrition, as in the NST2 results framework, not activity counts.

questions.stem: A district wants to prepare an integrated local development plan aligned with NST2. Which proposal best reflects the strategy's interconnected priorities?
options: Develop roads, support agro-processing and local businesses, strengthen skills and job creation, expand productive-use infrastructure, and protect the environment.
Invest exclusively in urban construction while neglecting rural livelihoods and environmental risks.
Focus only on increasing agricultural production without considering transport, markets, or employment.
Concentrate on digital services without addressing infrastructure, skills, or economic opportunities.
questions.explanation: NST2 priorities are interconnected: roads, agro-processing and MSMEs, skills and jobs, productive-use infrastructure and environmental protection.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT qualified as a non-professional bailiff under Law 12/2013?
options: Coordinator of an Access to Justice Bureau
questions.explanation: Under Article 50 of Law 12/2013 only the Deputy Coordinators of Access to Justice Bureaus are non-professional bailiffs, not the Coordinators; prison directors and other persons authorised by law are qualified.

questions.stem: Which is the highest organ of the Cell responsible for making decisions on Cell responsibilities in accordance with the law and instructions from higher levels?
questions.explanation: Under Presidential Order 001/01 of 2023, the Cell Council is the highest organ of the Cell and takes decisions on matters within the Cell's responsibilities that do not contradict laws or higher-level instructions.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT a strategy for implementing the National Disaster Management Policy?
options: Preparing Strategic Orientation Papers and guidelines
Informing citizens, preventing disasters and responding based on reliable evidence
questions.explanation: The National Disaster Management Policy strategies include strengthening coordination, setting up Strategic Orientation Papers and focusing on disaster risk reduction; "informing citizens and responding based on reliable evidence" is not one of them.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT a pillar of NST1?
questions.explanation: NST1 has three pillars: Economic Transformation, Social Transformation and Transformational Governance. Three of the four options are pillars, so the stem as captured has no single answer; "Socio-economic transformation" is not a pillar.

questions.stem: In which year was Umuganda officially launched as a government-organised programme?
questions.explanation: Umuganda was officially launched on 2 February 1974 under the Second Republic; it was later reintroduced by Law 53/2007.

questions.stem: How often does the Village Executive Committee meet?
questions.explanation: The Village Executive Committee meets twice a month (about every fifteen days) and whenever necessary.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT a good quality of a customer-service provider?
questions.explanation: Impatience is the only option that is not a good quality in a customer-service provider; empathy, problem-solving and communication are.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT a source or expression of national sovereignty?
options: Government authority is based on the Rwandan people, who exercise it through referenda, elections or their representatives
All power comes from the Rwandan people and is exercised in accordance with the Constitution
A Rwandan Government made up of Rwandans and serving Rwandans
No individual or group of people may claim the authority to exercise national sovereignty
questions.explanation: Article 1 of the Constitution says all power derives from Rwandans, national sovereignty is exercised by referendum, elections or representatives, and no individual or group may arrogate it. "A Government of Rwandans serving Rwandans" is the principle of the Republic in Article 4, not an expression of sovereignty.

questions.stem: How are home-grown solutions defined?
options: Unique Rwandan practices developed by Rwandans, based on domestic opportunities, values and history, to accelerate development
Innovations that solve problems in new and simple ways
Innovations or activities based on Rwandan culture and values
Innovations that have demonstrated their ability to solve a particular problem
questions.explanation: Rwanda Governance Board defines Home Grown Solutions as Rwanda's own solutions developed by Rwandans, based on local opportunities, cultural values and history, to fast-track development.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a specific priority under the Human Development Pillar of Vision 2050?
options: A diversified economy based on the industries of the future
A skilled and competent workforce capable of increasing productivity
questions.explanation: Vision 2050 lists 'a transformed workforce for higher productivity' among the Human Development pillar priorities; the diversified economy and high-end tourism sit under Competitiveness and Integration, and mobility under Urbanization.

questions.stem: At which National Dialogue Council (Umushyikirano) meeting, and in which year, was Vision 2050 proposed?
options: The 13th National Dialogue Council meeting in 2018
The 15th National Dialogue Council meeting in 2018
The 13th National Dialogue Council meeting in 2015
The 15th National Dialogue Council meeting in 2015
questions.explanation: Vision 2050 was requested by the 13th National Umushyikirano Council in 2015.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT an objective of the Imihigo performance-contract programme?
options: Enabling stakeholders to participate in development planning
Ensuring that resources are distributed equitably
Building a culture of regular performance evaluation
questions.explanation: Imihigo aims include stakeholder participation, results-oriented (performance-based) management and a culture of regular performance evaluation; equitable distribution of resources is not among them.

questions.stem: In which year was the Imihigo performance-contract programme introduced?
questions.explanation: Imihigo performance contracts were introduced in 2006 as part of Rwanda's decentralization drive.

questions.stem: Under Law No 18/2017 governing results-based performance management, "medium term" means a period longer than one year but not exceeding:
questions.explanation: Article 3 of Law No 18/2017 defines medium term as more than one year but not more than five years, while long term is a period exceeding five years.

questions.stem: Who monitors the implementation of joint Imihigo under Law No 18/2017?
options: The Ministry in charge of local government
The Office of the Prime Minister
The Ministry in charge of planning
questions.explanation: Article 17 of Law No 18/2017 gives the monitoring of joint Imihigo to the Office of the Prime Minister, because no single organ can deliver them alone.

questions.stem: Under Law No 18/2017, which institution collects the performance-contract implementation reports from all State organs and submits them to the Office of the Prime Minister?
options: The Ministry in charge of local government
The Ministry in charge of public service
The National Institute of Statistics of Rwanda
The Ministry in charge of planning
questions.explanation: Article 18 says supervising organs send their reports to the Ministry in charge of planning, which collects reports from all State organs and passes them to the Office of the Prime Minister.

questions.stem: In the Judiciary, the monitoring of the implementation of performance contracts is the responsibility of:
options: The High Council of the Judiciary
questions.explanation: Article 15 of Law No 18/2017 assigns this task to the High Council of the Judiciary, and in Parliament to the Bureau of each Chamber.

questions.stem: Under Law No 18/2017, how is responsibility for achieving the intended result shared among the organs involved in a joint Imihigo?
options: Equally among all the organs involved
Only by the Office of the Prime Minister
Mainly by the organ in charge of coordination
In proportion to the budget each organ received
questions.explanation: Article 9 states that all organs in a joint Imihigo have equal responsibility for the result, even though a Prime Minister's Order names one organ to coordinate the activities.

questions.stem: Under Law No 18/2017, who determines by order the indicators that State organs use to monitor the individual performance contracts of their staff?
options: The head of each State organ
The Minister in charge of planning
The Minister in charge of public service
questions.explanation: Article 16 says each State organ monitors staff Imihigo using indicators fixed by an Order of the Minister in charge of public service (MIFOTRA).

questions.stem: Choose the false response: under Law No 18/2017, the quarterly and annual monitoring carried out by every State organ must indicate:
options: The number of staff recruited during the year
The expenditures made to achieve the result
The progress attained against each expected result
