questions.explanation: Article 15 lists progress against each expected result, expenditures made and challenges faced; staff recruitment is not part of the required monitoring content.

questions.stem: Under Law No 18/2017, a "performance contract of the organ" is concluded between:
options: The head of the organ and its supervising authority
The Prime Minister and the President of the Republic
The head of the organ and its individual staff
questions.explanation: Article 13 provides that the organ's performance contract is concluded between its head and its supervising authority; an individual contract is between a public servant and his or her immediate supervisor.

questions.stem: In the 2024/2025 Imihigo evaluation of districts, MINALOC's scores on human security issues (shelter, sanitation and child malnutrition) account for what share of the final score?
questions.explanation: The NISR report adds MINALOC's human-security score at 20% of the final district score, so the NISR-measured part is 80%.

questions.stem: In the 2024/2025 Imihigo evaluation, citizen participation and satisfaction are assessed by RGB and contribute what percentage to the Imihigo evaluation score?
questions.explanation: Section 3.4 of the report gives RGB-assessed citizen participation and satisfaction a 10% weight in the Imihigo score.

questions.stem: A District includes the construction of a market as an output Imihigo. At the final evaluation the market is 95% complete but not yet usable. How does the NISR methodology score this Imihigo?
options: 95%, in proportion to the physical progress made
0%, because it was not fully completed as planned
80%, based on the share of budget spent
50%, as partial credit for the effort made
questions.explanation: Output Imihigo (classrooms, hospitals, markets) benefit people only when complete, so they score 100% if completed on time and 0% if not.

questions.stem: A District sets an outcome Imihigo of connecting 10,000 households to electricity. At the evaluation, 6,000 households are connected. How is this Imihigo scored?
options: On the progress achieved at assessment time (60%)
0%, because the target was not fully achieved
questions.explanation: Outcome Imihigo (terraces, electricity connectivity, health insurance) can be used progressively, so they are scored on the proportion of progress achieved, here 60%.

questions.stem: Since which fiscal year has the National Institute of Statistics of Rwanda (NISR) been mandated to evaluate Imihigo?
questions.explanation: NISR took over the evaluation of Imihigo from the 2017/2018 cycle to add independence and a rigorous evidence base.

questions.stem: Which district recorded the highest score in the 2024/2025 Imihigo evaluation of districts?
questions.explanation: Ngoma District topped the 2024/2025 ranking with 77.2%, followed by Gisagara, while Nyabihu was last with 54.4%.

questions.stem: Which joint Imihigo sector had the lowest performance in the 2024/2025 evaluation?
questions.explanation: Urbanization scored 51.96%, mainly because output-based targets were not met, while service delivery scored highest at 93.70%.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT one of the seven joint Imihigo sectors used in the 2024/2025 evaluation?
questions.explanation: The seven joint sectors are agriculture, energy, job creation, export, urbanization and rural settlement, social protection and service delivery; education is not one of them.

questions.stem: Using the 2024/2025 Imihigo district scores (Ngoma 77.2, Gisagara 76.6, Nyagatare 74.3, Gakenke 74.2), by how many points did the top-ranked district exceed the fourth-ranked district?
questions.explanation: The ranking table shows Ngoma at 77.2 and Gakenke at 74.2, so the gap is 77.2 minus 74.2, which is 3.0 points.

questions.stem: In the NISR Imihigo Evaluation Report 2017/2018, which district was the highest performer?
questions.explanation: Rwamagana scored 84.5% in 2017/18 and Nyanza was lowest at 53%; the 2016/17 leaders had been Rwamagana, Musanze, Huye and Gakenke.

questions.stem: Since which fiscal year was the concept of joint Imihigo introduced, leading to the joint signing of higher-level Imihigo by Ministers, District Mayors and the private sector?
questions.explanation: The 2016/2017 evaluation report records that joint Imihigo started with FY 2015-2016 so that partners share both failure and success.

questions.stem: The National Decentralization Policy adopted in 2000 was revised in which year, before the 2021 policy was issued?
questions.explanation: The 2021 policy explains that the 2000 policy was revised in 2012 and that the 2021 version reorients decentralization toward socio-economic transformation.

questions.stem: How many guiding principles for decentralization are set out in the 2021 National Decentralization Policy?
questions.explanation: Section 4.4 lists eight principles, from subsidiarity (1) to gender equality and inclusive governance (8).

questions.stem: Under the 2021 National Decentralization Policy, which administrative entity is to be strengthened as the centre of service delivery and data collection for development?
questions.explanation: The policy gives the Village citizen mobilization, the Cell service delivery and data collection, the Sector coordination of volunteerism, and the District overall planning.

questions.stem: In the 2021 National Decentralization Policy, the Governance and Decentralization Sector Working Group is led by the Ministry in charge of local governance. Who is nominated as its Co-chair?
options: The Rwanda Association of Local Government Authorities
questions.explanation: Section 6.1 keeps the G&DSWG as the primary technical forum, led by the local government ministry with a development partner as Co-chair.

questions.stem: To implement government policies and programmes at local level, the Government earmarked what shares of the development budget and of the recurrent budget respectively?
questions.explanation: The policy cites the earmark of 10% of the development budget and 3% of the recurrent budget as proof of continuous leadership commitment.

questions.stem: According to the 2021 National Decentralization Policy, the Common Development Fund (CDF), now the Local Administrative Entities Development Agency (LODA), was established in:
questions.explanation: Section 3.2 mentions the establishment of the Common Development Fund in 2003, which later became LODA.

questions.stem: According to the 2021 National Decentralization Policy, intergovernmental transfers for decentralized entities in 2019/20 totalled FRW 595 billion. How much of this came from block grants?
questions.explanation: The FRW 595 billion consisted of 82 billion own revenues, 361.7 billion earmarked transfers, 59.2 billion block grants and 92.1 billion from other agencies.

questions.stem: Which forum gives high-level ministerial consultation on key policies before their submission to Cabinet and monitors Presidential pledges, post-Cabinet actions and Umushyikirano resolutions, according to the 2021 National Decentralization Policy?
options: The Governance and Decentralization Sector Working Group
questions.explanation: The Governance Cluster is the ministerial-level forum, while the G&DSWG is the primary technical coordination forum.

questions.stem: Fill in the missing: The mission of the 2021 National Decentralization Policy is "To build a highly effective and accountable ...... driven by citizen centered governance for local social economic transformation".
questions.explanation: Section 4.2 states the mission as building a highly effective and accountable Local Government.

questions.stem: What does PPCP stand for in the National Decentralization Policy?
questions.explanation: The acronym list of the 2021 policy defines PPCP as Public Private Community Partnership, which is linked to local economic development.

questions.stem: The 2021 National Decentralization Policy proposes to revamp the RMI to address the capacity needs of Local Government. What does RMI stand for?
questions.explanation: Pillar 3 on capacity development proposes to revamp the Rwanda Management Institute (RMI) so that it can sustainably address Local Government capacity.

questions.stem: What does OSR stand for in the National Decentralization Policy, when it refers to Local Government revenue?
questions.explanation: The acronym list of the 2021 policy gives OSR as Own Source Revenue, the revenue local governments generate themselves.

questions.stem: According to the 2001-2017 impact assessment of the decentralisation policy, what share of citizens say services are cheaper under decentralisation?
questions.explanation: Citizens say services are more accessible (81%), faster (75%), cheaper (73%) and more reliable (76%).

questions.stem: The 2017 impact assessment of decentralisation reports that 131,030 local leaders were elected in 2016, of whom 52,516 were women. About what share of the elected leaders were women?
questions.explanation: The share is 52,516 divided by 131,030, which is about 40%.

questions.stem: The Community Development Policy (revised in April 2008) was first adopted by the Cabinet in:
questions.explanation: Section 1.1 says the policy was adopted in March 2001, together with the Fiscal Decentralization Policy, to reinforce the national decentralization policy.

questions.stem: Which entity does the Community Development Policy identify as the core formal community and the focus of the policy?
questions.explanation: The policy treats the Umudugudu as the core formal community; Imidugudu then aggregate into the Cell, Sector, District and Nation.

extras.title: Executive Secretary — Mock Exam 10
extras.summary: Practice for Executive Secretary recruitment: governance concepts and the law, plus administrative practice and service delivery.

questions.stem: Fill in the missing: The mission of the Community Development Policy is to ensure effective and sustainable participation of the community in its own development, to achieve poverty reduction and self-reliance based on ......
options: the sustainable exploitation of available resources
questions.explanation: The mission links poverty reduction and self-reliance to the sustainable exploitation of available (local) resources.

questions.stem: According to the Community Development Policy, the JADF coordination mechanism focuses on all of the following EXCEPT:
options: Monitoring the implementation of the Poverty Reduction Programmes
Coordinating the District action plans and determining implementation strategies
Collecting local taxes on behalf of the districts
Participating in the community based planning process
questions.explanation: Section 3.4.2.3 lists planning, coordination of District action plans, monitoring of poverty reduction programmes and conflict resolution between projects; tax collection is not a JADF task.

questions.stem: The Joint Action Development Forum (JADF) was first adopted by the Government of Rwanda through a Cabinet decision of:
questions.explanation: The RGB report says JADF was first adopted by Cabinet decision of 11 April 2007 and is now governed by the Prime Minister's instructions of 03/07/2015.

questions.stem: How many Executive Committee meetings must a District JADF hold each year under the Prime Minister's instructions?
questions.explanation: The Executive Committee meets every quarter (four a year) while the General Assembly meets at least twice a year.

questions.stem: Fill in the missing: The three thematic commissions set up by the District JADF General Assembly are Economic, Social and ......
questions.explanation: The three commissions are Economic, Social and Governance, aligned with the NST1 pillars and the district council commissions.

questions.stem: Under the Prime Minister's instructions, every District JADF must organise an open day event, where JADF stakeholders exhibit their products and services to the public, at least:
questions.explanation: The instructions require at least one open day a year to promote accountability, transparency and better service delivery.

questions.stem: The 2024 RGB assessment covered 15 districts. Only five of them held the required ten JADF General Assembly meetings over five years. What percentage of the sampled districts is this?
questions.explanation: Five out of fifteen districts is 33.3%; the other percentages in the report refer to open days (46.6%) and approved action plans (53.3%).

questions.stem: The Executive Committee of a District JADF is made up of the following members EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: The report lists the Chairperson, Vice Chairperson, Treasurer, District JADF Secretary and the chairpersons of the thematic commissions.

questions.stem: Since which fiscal year has the contribution of Umuganda been integrated into the national budget?
questions.explanation: The RGB impact assessment notes that, from 2013-2014, the value of Umuganda has been integrated in the national budget.

questions.stem: According to MINALOC's annual report cited in the RGB Impact Assessment of Umuganda, what was the average countrywide participation level in Umuganda in fiscal year 2015-2016?
questions.explanation: The average was 91.3%; the City of Kigali was lowest at 82.2% and the Northern Province highest at about 94%.

questions.stem: In the 2015-2016 Umuganda participation data, which province recorded the highest level of participation?
questions.explanation: The Northern Province reached 94.03%, ahead of the Southern (93%), Eastern (90%) and Western (89%) provinces; the City of Kigali had the lowest (82.2%).

questions.stem: According to the RGB impact assessment of Umuganda (2007-2016), Umuganda contributed nearly what share of the total cost of classrooms built under the 9&12 Years Basic Education programme?
questions.explanation: The foreword states that community works contributed nearly 62% of the total cost of the classrooms.

questions.stem: The estimated cost of the Governance and Decentralization Sector Strategic Plan 2018/19-2023/24 is about:
questions.explanation: The plan costs Rwf 302,888,000,000 in total, an annual average of about Rwf 50.5 billion.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT one of the eight sector priorities of the Governance and Decentralization Sector Strategic Plan 2018/19-2023/24?
options: Values and Home Grown Solutions for transformational governance
questions.explanation: The eight priorities cover participation, accountability, service delivery, fiscal decentralization, local economic development, sectoral decentralization, capacity development, and values and HGS.

questions.stem: The Governance and Decentralization Sector Strategic Plan calls for public accountability days in local government administrative entities at least:
questions.explanation: Under the transparency and accountability priority, local entities should hold public accountability days at least twice a year.

questions.stem: Which of the following was NOT one of the four Home Grown Initiatives assessed in the 2014 RGB impact assessment?
questions.explanation: The study assessed Ubudehe, Imihigo, Umuganda and Girinka; Gacaca, Abunzi, Itorero and others are home grown initiatives that were not assessed.

questions.stem: Which institution was instructed by the 8th National Dialogue (Umushyikirano) of December 2010 to assess the social and economic impact of Home Grown Initiatives?
options: National Institute of Statistics of Rwanda
questions.explanation: The 8th National Dialogue of 20-21 December 2010 asked RGB to assess the impact of HGIs and document their best practices.

questions.stem: On which date did the President of the Republic launch Itorero ry'Igihugu?
questions.explanation: The NURC study records that the President of the Republic launched Itorero ry'Igihugu on 16 November 2007.

questions.stem: In the structure of Itorero ry'Igihugu, who is responsible for monitoring the implementation of values and advising those who deviate from them?
questions.explanation: At each level of Itorero there are keepers of values (abarinzi b'indangagaciro) who monitor values, advise those who deviate and choose who should be rewarded.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a value that promotes good service delivery, according to the NURC study on Rwandan cultural values?
questions.explanation: Good customer care is a service-delivery value; solidarity belongs to unity, humility to nobility and bravery to patriotism.

questions.stem: Under NST2, which institution coordinates the elaboration of NST2 and related strategies in collaboration with OPM, MINALOC, Sector Working Groups and districts?
questions.explanation: Table 4 of NST2 gives the Ministry of Finance and Economic Planning (MINECOFIN) the role of coordinating the elaboration of NST2, national planning, resource mobilisation and the NST2 monitoring systems.

questions.stem: Which institution develops the metadata of the indicators in the NST2 M&E matrix, working closely with the relevant sector working groups, and makes it publicly accessible on its website?
questions.explanation: NST2 section 8.1 (vii) says the metadata of NST2 indicators, which defines how each indicator is measured, is developed by NISR with the sector working groups and is publicly accessible through the NISR website.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT one of the cross-cutting areas (CCAs) that NST2 takes into consideration?
questions.explanation: NST2 section 6 lists seven cross-cutting areas: environment and climate change, disability and social inclusion, disaster risk reduction and management, HIV/AIDS and NCDs, gender and family promotion, regional integration and capacity development. Digital transformation is treated in the economic pillar, not as a cross-cutting area.

questions.stem: Which NST2 monitoring tool is the basis for annual reporting and for tracking the performance of NST2 at the national level?
questions.explanation: NST2 section 8.1 (iv) states that the NST2 M&E matrix is the basis for annual reporting and tracking of NST2 performance nationally; the SSP and CoK/DDS matrices are cascaded from it.

questions.stem: In the hierarchy of results of the NST2 Theory of Change, which result level is the highest?
questions.explanation: The NST2 Theory of Change places the goal at the top, followed by priority areas, outcomes and strategic interventions (NST2 section 8.1 (i)).

questions.stem: Through which mechanisms is the CoK/District Development Strategy (DDS) M&E matrix monitored annually at the City or district level under NST2?
options: The National Leadership Retreat and Cabinet reviews
JADF and administrative reports submitted to the District Council
Joint sector reviews held at Sector Working Group level
Evaluations coordinated by MINECOFIN and the Development Partners Coordination Group
questions.explanation: NST2 section 8.1 (vi): the CoK/DDS matrix is monitored annually through the JADF and administrative reports to the District Council, while the SSP matrix is monitored at Sector Working Group level through joint sector reviews.

questions.stem: A District has finalised its District Development Strategy (DDS) aligned to NST2. As a local officer, which organ do you know approves the DDS and oversees its implementation?
questions.explanation: Table 4 of NST2 says the City of Kigali and District Councils approve the CoK/DDS aligned to NST2 and provide oversight of its implementation; MINALOC only coordinates its elaboration and JADF facilitates joint planning.

questions.stem: Strategic interventions identified in the NST2 Theories of Change are cascaded to institutional strategic plans and implemented through all of the following EXCEPT:
options: The annual planning and budgeting process
The National Land Use and Development Master Plan (2020-2050)
questions.explanation: NST2 section 8.1 says interventions are implemented through the MTEF, the annual planning and budgeting process and Imihigo; the land use master plan is not listed as an implementation channel.

questions.stem: As an Economic and Human Capital Development Officer, you are asked to what level NST2 plans to scale up Vocational Training Centres (VTCs) through workplace learning approaches. What is the correct answer?
questions.explanation: NST2 section 4.1 says VTCs with workplace learning will be scaled up in every cell, while Technical Secondary School centres of excellence are to be set up in all districts.

questions.stem: NST2 aims to increase the proportion of learners enrolled in technical and vocational training schools to what share of the total learners enrolled in upper secondary?
questions.explanation: NST2 section 4.1 sets the TVET target at 60% of learners in upper secondary, up from a baseline of 43% in the M&E matrix.

questions.stem: NST2 states that, to improve the quality of healthcare, the number of active registered health workers will be:
questions.explanation: NST2 section 4.2 (and Goal 25 of Annex 2, "Quadruple skilled health workforce") plans to quadruple the number of active registered health workers.

questions.stem: According to NST2, during the NST1 period (2017-2024) life expectancy rose from 66.6 years to:
questions.explanation: NST2 section 1.1 reports that life expectancy rose from 66.6 to 69.9 years under NST1.

questions.stem: NST2 reports that the number of public services available online expanded over the NST1 period from 155 to:
questions.explanation: NST2 section 1.1 (transformational governance) notes that online services grew from 155 to over 680.

questions.stem: NST2 reports that citizen satisfaction with the quality of service delivery had reached what level in 2023?
questions.explanation: NST2 section 1.2 gives 78% citizen satisfaction in 2023 and the M&E matrix targets a level above 90% by 2028/29.

questions.stem: NST2 aims to raise the proportion of poor and vulnerable people covered by social protection systems from 11% to what level by 2028/29?
questions.explanation: Annex 1 of NST2 (indicator 28) sets a mid-term target of 16% for 2026/27 and an end-period target of 20% for 2028/29.

questions.stem: Under NST2, which cadre provides coaching, referrals and behaviour change support to empower households taking part in graduation from poverty?
questions.explanation: NST2 Annex 2, priority area PA-36, provides for coaching, referrals and behaviour change support through para-social workers for graduation participants.

questions.stem: Under NST2, legal aid for vulnerable people is to be expanded through a legal aid week that is held:
questions.explanation: NST2 Annex 2 (PA-44) expands legal aid through a "semestrial" legal aid week, meaning one held every six months.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT a headline indicator for the NST2 Social Transformation pillar?
options: Improve the quality and market relevance of education
Reduce case backlogs in the justice system by half
Reduce the stunting rate for children under five years from 33% to 15%
Increase graduation out of poverty and enhanced coverage of social safety nets
questions.explanation: The Social Transformation headline indicators in NST2 cover education quality, stunting, WASH access and graduation from poverty. Reducing case backlogs by half is a headline target of the Transformational Governance pillar.

questions.stem: NST2 expects public entities to adhere to IPSAS and PFM regulations. What does IPSAS stand for?
options: International Procurement and Supply Accounting Standards
questions.explanation: NST2 section 5.3 refers to International Public Sector Accounting Standards (IPSAS), with a phased implementation of accrual standards.

questions.stem: NST2 plans to improve justice service delivery by enhancing the functioning and use of the IECMS. What does IECMS stand for?
options: Integrated Evidence and Crime Management System
questions.explanation: NST2 section 5.1 names the Integrated Electronic Case Management System (IECMS) among the technologies used to improve justice service delivery.

questions.stem: Vision 2050 notes that NISR projects Rwanda's population to reach about 17.6 million by 2035 and about how many people by 2050?
questions.explanation: Vision 2050 (Human Development pillar) says the population will rise by more than 50% to 17.6 million by 2035 and double to about 22.1 million by 2050.

questions.stem: Fill in the missing: Vision 2050 aims to reduce the fertility rate from 4.1 births per woman (DHS 2019/2020) to high income country standards of ........... births per woman in 2050.
questions.explanation: Vision 2050 targets a fertility rate of 2.3 births per woman in 2050, down from 4.1 in the 2019/20 DHS.

questions.stem: Vision 2050 says Rwanda reduced the poverty rate from 78% after 1994 to what level in 2017?
questions.explanation: Vision 2050 (overarching goals) records a fall of the poverty rate from 78% after 1994 to 38% in 2017, with the aim of eliminating poverty altogether.

questions.stem: Fill in the missing: According to MINALOC, the value of Umuganda in money terms was estimated at 4 billion Rwandan francs in 2007 and increased up to ........... in 2016.
questions.explanation: Vision 2050 notes that Umuganda supports the national budget: its value rose from 4 billion Rwandan francs in 2007 to 19 billion in 2016 (MINALOC).

questions.stem: Which two home-grown justice mechanisms does Vision 2050 say contribute to reducing backlogs from the ordinary courts and to reducing the cost of access to justice?
options: Gacaca and Access to Justice Bureaus (MAJ)
Abunzi and Access to Justice Bureaus (MAJ)
questions.explanation: Vision 2050 says Abunzi and the Access to Justice Bureaus reduce backlogs and the cost of justice, whereas Gacaca is credited with bringing justice after the genocide against the Tutsi.

questions.stem: Vision 2050 aims to enhance local revenue mobilisation so that urban and rural local governments can cater for what share of their development projects?
questions.explanation: Vision 2050 sets a target that local revenue can finance 85% of local development projects, reducing reliance on central government transfers.

questions.stem: Fill in the missing: Under Vision 2050, child stunting (under 5 years) will be reduced from 33% (2020) to ........... in 2035 and 3% in 2050.
questions.explanation: Vision 2050 sets stunting targets of 5.5% in 2035 and 3% in 2050; NST2 targets below 15% by 2029 as a step toward them.

questions.stem: Vision 2050 notes that citizens who identify themselves as Rwandans first, and not by ethnic identity, stand at what share (CRC, 2016)?
questions.explanation: Vision 2050 gives 95.3% (CRC, 2016) for citizens identifying as Rwandans first; 94.55% (RRB, 2015) is the figure for social cohesion and mutual trust.

questions.stem: Vision 2050 warns that with an average GDP growth rate of only around 7%, Rwanda would become a high-income country only by:
questions.explanation: Vision 2050 uses this example to show that "business as usual" is not sufficient: around 7% growth would delay high-income status to 2075.

questions.stem: How many priority areas does the Social Transformation pillar of NST1 have?
questions.explanation: NST1 Social Transformation has 5 priority areas (graduation from poverty, malnutrition, health, education and a modern Rwandan household); Economic Transformation has 7 and Transformational Governance has 6.

extras.title: Economic Development Officer — Mock Exam 6
extras.summary: Practice for SEDO / Economic Development Officer recruitment: governance concepts and local economic development, plus field practice and service delivery.

questions.stem: Which programme is NOT intended to promote youth employment?
options: Programmes to eliminate all forms of child labour
Establishing programmes for small income-generating projects
questions.explanation: Programmes against child labour protect children and enforce labour standards; they are not youth-employment promotion measures, unlike entrepreneurship, start-up/income-generating support and skills training.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT a major challenge to job creation?
options: Lack of workers with the technical skills required by the labour market
The existence of an adequate national framework for coordinating and monitoring employment-promotion programmes
A mindset that undervalues traditional agriculture and livestock farming
Low investment caused by low domestic savings
questions.explanation: The Revised National Employment Policy lists an inadequate coordination institutional framework as a challenge, so "the existence of an adequate national framework" is the opposite of a challenge and is the NOT item.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT a pillar of NST1?
questions.explanation: NST1 has three pillars: Economic Transformation, Social Transformation and Transformational Governance. Three of the four options are pillars, so the stem as captured has no single answer; "Socio-economic transformation" is not a pillar.

questions.stem: Which institution trains beneficiaries who lack sufficient cattle-rearing knowledge, in collaboration with districts?
options: Rwanda Agriculture and Animal Resources Development Board (RAB)
questions.explanation: The Rwanda Agriculture and Animal Resources Development Board (RAB), established by Law 14/2017, trains Girinka beneficiaries who lack cattle-rearing knowledge in collaboration with districts. The other options are not real institution names.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT a good quality of a customer-service provider?
questions.explanation: Impatience is the only option that is not a good quality in a customer-service provider; empathy, problem-solving and communication are.

questions.stem: How are home-grown solutions defined?
options: Unique Rwandan practices developed by Rwandans, based on domestic opportunities, values and history, to accelerate development
Innovations that solve problems in new and simple ways
Innovations or activities based on Rwandan culture and values
Innovations that have demonstrated their ability to solve a particular problem
questions.explanation: Rwanda Governance Board defines Home Grown Solutions as Rwanda's own solutions developed by Rwandans, based on local opportunities, cultural values and history, to fast-track development.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a specific priority under the Human Development Pillar of Vision 2050?
options: A diversified economy based on the industries of the future
A skilled and competent workforce capable of increasing productivity
questions.explanation: Vision 2050 lists 'a transformed workforce for higher productivity' among the Human Development pillar priorities; the diversified economy and high-end tourism sit under Competitiveness and Integration, and mobility under Urbanization.

questions.stem: At which National Dialogue Council (Umushyikirano) meeting, and in which year, was Vision 2050 proposed?
options: The 13th National Dialogue Council meeting in 2018
The 15th National Dialogue Council meeting in 2018
The 13th National Dialogue Council meeting in 2015
The 15th National Dialogue Council meeting in 2015
questions.explanation: Vision 2050 was requested by the 13th National Umushyikirano Council in 2015.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT an objective of the Imihigo performance-contract programme?
options: Enabling stakeholders to participate in development planning
Ensuring that resources are distributed equitably
Building a culture of regular performance evaluation
questions.explanation: Imihigo aims include stakeholder participation, results-oriented (performance-based) management and a culture of regular performance evaluation; equitable distribution of resources is not among them.

questions.stem: In which year was the Imihigo performance-contract programme introduced?
questions.explanation: Imihigo performance contracts were introduced in 2006 as part of Rwanda's decentralization drive.

questions.stem: Under Law No 18/2017 governing results-based performance management, "medium term" means a period longer than one year but not exceeding:
questions.explanation: Article 3 of Law No 18/2017 defines medium term as more than one year but not more than five years, while long term is a period exceeding five years.

questions.stem: Who monitors the implementation of joint Imihigo under Law No 18/2017?
options: The Ministry in charge of local government
The Office of the Prime Minister
The Ministry in charge of planning
questions.explanation: Article 17 of Law No 18/2017 gives the monitoring of joint Imihigo to the Office of the Prime Minister, because no single organ can deliver them alone.

questions.stem: Under Law No 18/2017, which institution collects the performance-contract implementation reports from all State organs and submits them to the Office of the Prime Minister?
options: The Ministry in charge of local government
The Ministry in charge of public service
The National Institute of Statistics of Rwanda
The Ministry in charge of planning
questions.explanation: Article 18 says supervising organs send their reports to the Ministry in charge of planning, which collects reports from all State organs and passes them to the Office of the Prime Minister.

questions.stem: In the Judiciary, the monitoring of the implementation of performance contracts is the responsibility of:
options: The High Council of the Judiciary
questions.explanation: Article 15 of Law No 18/2017 assigns this task to the High Council of the Judiciary, and in Parliament to the Bureau of each Chamber.

questions.stem: Under Law No 18/2017, how is responsibility for achieving the intended result shared among the organs involved in a joint Imihigo?
options: Equally among all the organs involved
Only by the Office of the Prime Minister
Mainly by the organ in charge of coordination
In proportion to the budget each organ received
questions.explanation: Article 9 states that all organs in a joint Imihigo have equal responsibility for the result, even though a Prime Minister's Order names one organ to coordinate the activities.

questions.stem: Under Law No 18/2017, who determines by order the indicators that State organs use to monitor the individual performance contracts of their staff?
options: The head of each State organ
The Minister in charge of planning
The Minister in charge of public service
questions.explanation: Article 16 says each State organ monitors staff Imihigo using indicators fixed by an Order of the Minister in charge of public service (MIFOTRA).

questions.stem: Choose the false response: under Law No 18/2017, the quarterly and annual monitoring carried out by every State organ must indicate:
options: The number of staff recruited during the year
The expenditures made to achieve the result
The progress attained against each expected result
questions.explanation: Article 15 lists progress against each expected result, expenditures made and challenges faced; staff recruitment is not part of the required monitoring content.

questions.stem: Under Law No 18/2017, a "performance contract of the organ" is concluded between:
options: The head of the organ and its supervising authority
The Prime Minister and the President of the Republic
The head of the organ and its individual staff
questions.explanation: Article 13 provides that the organ's performance contract is concluded between its head and its supervising authority; an individual contract is between a public servant and his or her immediate supervisor.

questions.stem: In the 2024/2025 Imihigo evaluation of districts, MINALOC's scores on human security issues (shelter, sanitation and child malnutrition) account for what share of the final score?
questions.explanation: The NISR report adds MINALOC's human-security score at 20% of the final district score, so the NISR-measured part is 80%.

questions.stem: In the 2024/2025 Imihigo evaluation, citizen participation and satisfaction are assessed by RGB and contribute what percentage to the Imihigo evaluation score?
questions.explanation: Section 3.4 of the report gives RGB-assessed citizen participation and satisfaction a 10% weight in the Imihigo score.

questions.stem: A District includes the construction of a market as an output Imihigo. At the final evaluation the market is 95% complete but not yet usable. How does the NISR methodology score this Imihigo?
options: 95%, in proportion to the physical progress made
0%, because it was not fully completed as planned
80%, based on the share of budget spent
50%, as partial credit for the effort made
questions.explanation: Output Imihigo (classrooms, hospitals, markets) benefit people only when complete, so they score 100% if completed on time and 0% if not.

questions.stem: A District sets an outcome Imihigo of connecting 10,000 households to electricity. At the evaluation, 6,000 households are connected. How is this Imihigo scored?
options: On the progress achieved at assessment time (60%)
0%, because the target was not fully achieved
questions.explanation: Outcome Imihigo (terraces, electricity connectivity, health insurance) can be used progressively, so they are scored on the proportion of progress achieved, here 60%.

questions.stem: Since which fiscal year has the National Institute of Statistics of Rwanda (NISR) been mandated to evaluate Imihigo?
questions.explanation: NISR took over the evaluation of Imihigo from the 2017/2018 cycle to add independence and a rigorous evidence base.

questions.stem: Which district recorded the highest score in the 2024/2025 Imihigo evaluation of districts?
questions.explanation: Ngoma District topped the 2024/2025 ranking with 77.2%, followed by Gisagara, while Nyabihu was last with 54.4%.

questions.stem: Which joint Imihigo sector had the lowest performance in the 2024/2025 evaluation?
questions.explanation: Urbanization scored 51.96%, mainly because output-based targets were not met, while service delivery scored highest at 93.70%.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT one of the seven joint Imihigo sectors used in the 2024/2025 evaluation?
questions.explanation: The seven joint sectors are agriculture, energy, job creation, export, urbanization and rural settlement, social protection and service delivery; education is not one of them.

questions.stem: Using the 2024/2025 Imihigo district scores (Ngoma 77.2, Gisagara 76.6, Nyagatare 74.3, Gakenke 74.2), by how many points did the top-ranked district exceed the fourth-ranked district?
questions.explanation: The ranking table shows Ngoma at 77.2 and Gakenke at 74.2, so the gap is 77.2 minus 74.2, which is 3.0 points.

questions.stem: In the NISR Imihigo Evaluation Report 2017/2018, which district was the highest performer?
questions.explanation: Rwamagana scored 84.5% in 2017/18 and Nyanza was lowest at 53%; the 2016/17 leaders had been Rwamagana, Musanze, Huye and Gakenke.

questions.stem: Since which fiscal year was the concept of joint Imihigo introduced, leading to the joint signing of higher-level Imihigo by Ministers, District Mayors and the private sector?
questions.explanation: The 2016/2017 evaluation report records that joint Imihigo started with FY 2015-2016 so that partners share both failure and success.

questions.stem: The National Decentralization Policy adopted in 2000 was revised in which year, before the 2021 policy was issued?
questions.explanation: The 2021 policy explains that the 2000 policy was revised in 2012 and that the 2021 version reorients decentralization toward socio-economic transformation.

questions.stem: How many guiding principles for decentralization are set out in the 2021 National Decentralization Policy?
questions.explanation: Section 4.4 lists eight principles, from subsidiarity (1) to gender equality and inclusive governance (8).

questions.stem: In the 2021 National Decentralization Policy, the Governance and Decentralization Sector Working Group is led by the Ministry in charge of local governance. Who is nominated as its Co-chair?
options: The Rwanda Association of Local Government Authorities
questions.explanation: Section 6.1 keeps the G&DSWG as the primary technical forum, led by the local government ministry with a development partner as Co-chair.

questions.stem: To implement government policies and programmes at local level, the Government earmarked what shares of the development budget and of the recurrent budget respectively?
questions.explanation: The policy cites the earmark of 10% of the development budget and 3% of the recurrent budget as proof of continuous leadership commitment.

questions.stem: According to the 2021 National Decentralization Policy, the Common Development Fund (CDF), now the Local Administrative Entities Development Agency (LODA), was established in:
questions.explanation: Section 3.2 mentions the establishment of the Common Development Fund in 2003, which later became LODA.

questions.stem: According to the 2021 National Decentralization Policy, intergovernmental transfers for decentralized entities in 2019/20 totalled FRW 595 billion. How much of this came from block grants?
questions.explanation: The FRW 595 billion consisted of 82 billion own revenues, 361.7 billion earmarked transfers, 59.2 billion block grants and 92.1 billion from other agencies.

questions.stem: Which forum gives high-level ministerial consultation on key policies before their submission to Cabinet and monitors Presidential pledges, post-Cabinet actions and Umushyikirano resolutions, according to the 2021 National Decentralization Policy?
options: The Governance and Decentralization Sector Working Group
questions.explanation: The Governance Cluster is the ministerial-level forum, while the G&DSWG is the primary technical coordination forum.

questions.stem: Fill in the missing: The mission of the 2021 National Decentralization Policy is "To build a highly effective and accountable ...... driven by citizen centered governance for local social economic transformation".
questions.explanation: Section 4.2 states the mission as building a highly effective and accountable Local Government.

questions.stem: What does PPCP stand for in the National Decentralization Policy?
questions.explanation: The acronym list of the 2021 policy defines PPCP as Public Private Community Partnership, which is linked to local economic development.

questions.stem: The 2021 National Decentralization Policy proposes to revamp the RMI to address the capacity needs of Local Government. What does RMI stand for?
questions.explanation: Pillar 3 on capacity development proposes to revamp the Rwanda Management Institute (RMI) so that it can sustainably address Local Government capacity.

questions.stem: What does OSR stand for in the National Decentralization Policy, when it refers to Local Government revenue?
questions.explanation: The acronym list of the 2021 policy gives OSR as Own Source Revenue, the revenue local governments generate themselves.

questions.stem: According to the 2001-2017 impact assessment of the decentralisation policy, what share of citizens say services are cheaper under decentralisation?
questions.explanation: Citizens say services are more accessible (81%), faster (75%), cheaper (73%) and more reliable (76%).

questions.stem: The 2017 impact assessment of decentralisation reports that 131,030 local leaders were elected in 2016, of whom 52,516 were women. About what share of the elected leaders were women?
questions.explanation: The share is 52,516 divided by 131,030, which is about 40%.

questions.stem: The Community Development Policy (revised in April 2008) was first adopted by the Cabinet in:
questions.explanation: Section 1.1 says the policy was adopted in March 2001, together with the Fiscal Decentralization Policy, to reinforce the national decentralization policy.

questions.stem: Fill in the missing: The mission of the Community Development Policy is to ensure effective and sustainable participation of the community in its own development, to achieve poverty reduction and self-reliance based on ......
options: the sustainable exploitation of available resources
questions.explanation: The mission links poverty reduction and self-reliance to the sustainable exploitation of available (local) resources.

questions.stem: According to the Community Development Policy, the JADF coordination mechanism focuses on all of the following EXCEPT:
options: Monitoring the implementation of the Poverty Reduction Programmes
Coordinating the District action plans and determining implementation strategies
Collecting local taxes on behalf of the districts
Participating in the community based planning process
questions.explanation: Section 3.4.2.3 lists planning, coordination of District action plans, monitoring of poverty reduction programmes and conflict resolution between projects; tax collection is not a JADF task.

questions.stem: The Joint Action Development Forum (JADF) was first adopted by the Government of Rwanda through a Cabinet decision of:
questions.explanation: The RGB report says JADF was first adopted by Cabinet decision of 11 April 2007 and is now governed by the Prime Minister's instructions of 03/07/2015.

questions.stem: How many Executive Committee meetings must a District JADF hold each year under the Prime Minister's instructions?
questions.explanation: The Executive Committee meets every quarter (four a year) while the General Assembly meets at least twice a year.

questions.stem: Fill in the missing: The three thematic commissions set up by the District JADF General Assembly are Economic, Social and ......
questions.explanation: The three commissions are Economic, Social and Governance, aligned with the NST1 pillars and the district council commissions.

questions.stem: Under the Prime Minister's instructions, every District JADF must organise an open day event, where JADF stakeholders exhibit their products and services to the public, at least:
questions.explanation: The instructions require at least one open day a year to promote accountability, transparency and better service delivery.

questions.stem: The 2024 RGB assessment covered 15 districts. Only five of them held the required ten JADF General Assembly meetings over five years. What percentage of the sampled districts is this?
questions.explanation: Five out of fifteen districts is 33.3%; the other percentages in the report refer to open days (46.6%) and approved action plans (53.3%).

extras.title: Economic Development Officer — Mock Exam 7
extras.summary: Practice for SEDO / Economic Development Officer recruitment: governance concepts and local economic development, plus field practice and service delivery.

questions.stem: The Executive Committee of a District JADF is made up of the following members EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: The report lists the Chairperson, Vice Chairperson, Treasurer, District JADF Secretary and the chairpersons of the thematic commissions.

questions.stem: Since which fiscal year has the contribution of Umuganda been integrated into the national budget?
questions.explanation: The RGB impact assessment notes that, from 2013-2014, the value of Umuganda has been integrated in the national budget.

questions.stem: According to MINALOC's annual report cited in the RGB Impact Assessment of Umuganda, what was the average countrywide participation level in Umuganda in fiscal year 2015-2016?
questions.explanation: The average was 91.3%; the City of Kigali was lowest at 82.2% and the Northern Province highest at about 94%.

questions.stem: In the 2015-2016 Umuganda participation data, which province recorded the highest level of participation?
questions.explanation: The Northern Province reached 94.03%, ahead of the Southern (93%), Eastern (90%) and Western (89%) provinces; the City of Kigali had the lowest (82.2%).

questions.stem: According to the RGB impact assessment of Umuganda (2007-2016), Umuganda contributed nearly what share of the total cost of classrooms built under the 9&12 Years Basic Education programme?
questions.explanation: The foreword states that community works contributed nearly 62% of the total cost of the classrooms.

questions.stem: The estimated cost of the Governance and Decentralization Sector Strategic Plan 2018/19-2023/24 is about:
questions.explanation: The plan costs Rwf 302,888,000,000 in total, an annual average of about Rwf 50.5 billion.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT one of the eight sector priorities of the Governance and Decentralization Sector Strategic Plan 2018/19-2023/24?
options: Values and Home Grown Solutions for transformational governance
questions.explanation: The eight priorities cover participation, accountability, service delivery, fiscal decentralization, local economic development, sectoral decentralization, capacity development, and values and HGS.

questions.stem: The Governance and Decentralization Sector Strategic Plan calls for public accountability days in local government administrative entities at least:
questions.explanation: Under the transparency and accountability priority, local entities should hold public accountability days at least twice a year.

questions.stem: Which of the following was NOT one of the four Home Grown Initiatives assessed in the 2014 RGB impact assessment?
questions.explanation: The study assessed Ubudehe, Imihigo, Umuganda and Girinka; Gacaca, Abunzi, Itorero and others are home grown initiatives that were not assessed.

questions.stem: Which institution was instructed by the 8th National Dialogue (Umushyikirano) of December 2010 to assess the social and economic impact of Home Grown Initiatives?
options: National Institute of Statistics of Rwanda
questions.explanation: The 8th National Dialogue of 20-21 December 2010 asked RGB to assess the impact of HGIs and document their best practices.

questions.stem: On which date did the President of the Republic launch Itorero ry'Igihugu?
questions.explanation: The NURC study records that the President of the Republic launched Itorero ry'Igihugu on 16 November 2007.

questions.stem: In the structure of Itorero ry'Igihugu, who is responsible for monitoring the implementation of values and advising those who deviate from them?
questions.explanation: At each level of Itorero there are keepers of values (abarinzi b'indangagaciro) who monitor values, advise those who deviate and choose who should be rewarded.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a value that promotes good service delivery, according to the NURC study on Rwandan cultural values?
questions.explanation: Good customer care is a service-delivery value; solidarity belongs to unity, humility to nobility and bravery to patriotism.

questions.stem: Under NST2, which institution coordinates the elaboration of NST2 and related strategies in collaboration with OPM, MINALOC, Sector Working Groups and districts?
questions.explanation: Table 4 of NST2 gives the Ministry of Finance and Economic Planning (MINECOFIN) the role of coordinating the elaboration of NST2, national planning, resource mobilisation and the NST2 monitoring systems.

questions.stem: Which institution develops the metadata of the indicators in the NST2 M&E matrix, working closely with the relevant sector working groups, and makes it publicly accessible on its website?
questions.explanation: NST2 section 8.1 (vii) says the metadata of NST2 indicators, which defines how each indicator is measured, is developed by NISR with the sector working groups and is publicly accessible through the NISR website.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT one of the cross-cutting areas (CCAs) that NST2 takes into consideration?
questions.explanation: NST2 section 6 lists seven cross-cutting areas: environment and climate change, disability and social inclusion, disaster risk reduction and management, HIV/AIDS and NCDs, gender and family promotion, regional integration and capacity development. Digital transformation is treated in the economic pillar, not as a cross-cutting area.

questions.stem: Which NST2 monitoring tool is the basis for annual reporting and for tracking the performance of NST2 at the national level?
questions.explanation: NST2 section 8.1 (iv) states that the NST2 M&E matrix is the basis for annual reporting and tracking of NST2 performance nationally; the SSP and CoK/DDS matrices are cascaded from it.

questions.stem: In the hierarchy of results of the NST2 Theory of Change, which result level is the highest?
questions.explanation: The NST2 Theory of Change places the goal at the top, followed by priority areas, outcomes and strategic interventions (NST2 section 8.1 (i)).

questions.stem: Through which mechanisms is the CoK/District Development Strategy (DDS) M&E matrix monitored annually at the City or district level under NST2?
options: The National Leadership Retreat and Cabinet reviews
JADF and administrative reports submitted to the District Council
Joint sector reviews held at Sector Working Group level
Evaluations coordinated by MINECOFIN and the Development Partners Coordination Group
questions.explanation: NST2 section 8.1 (vi): the CoK/DDS matrix is monitored annually through the JADF and administrative reports to the District Council, while the SSP matrix is monitored at Sector Working Group level through joint sector reviews.

questions.stem: A District has finalised its District Development Strategy (DDS) aligned to NST2. As a local officer, which organ do you know approves the DDS and oversees its implementation?
questions.explanation: Table 4 of NST2 says the City of Kigali and District Councils approve the CoK/DDS aligned to NST2 and provide oversight of its implementation; MINALOC only coordinates its elaboration and JADF facilitates joint planning.

questions.stem: Strategic interventions identified in the NST2 Theories of Change are cascaded to institutional strategic plans and implemented through all of the following EXCEPT:
options: The annual planning and budgeting process
The National Land Use and Development Master Plan (2020-2050)
questions.explanation: NST2 section 8.1 says interventions are implemented through the MTEF, the annual planning and budgeting process and Imihigo; the land use master plan is not listed as an implementation channel.

questions.stem: As an Economic and Human Capital Development Officer, you are asked to what level NST2 plans to scale up Vocational Training Centres (VTCs) through workplace learning approaches. What is the correct answer?
questions.explanation: NST2 section 4.1 says VTCs with workplace learning will be scaled up in every cell, while Technical Secondary School centres of excellence are to be set up in all districts.

questions.stem: NST2 aims to increase the proportion of learners enrolled in technical and vocational training schools to what share of the total learners enrolled in upper secondary?
questions.explanation: NST2 section 4.1 sets the TVET target at 60% of learners in upper secondary, up from a baseline of 43% in the M&E matrix.

questions.stem: NST2 states that, to improve the quality of healthcare, the number of active registered health workers will be:
questions.explanation: NST2 section 4.2 (and Goal 25 of Annex 2, "Quadruple skilled health workforce") plans to quadruple the number of active registered health workers.

questions.stem: According to NST2, during the NST1 period (2017-2024) life expectancy rose from 66.6 years to:
questions.explanation: NST2 section 1.1 reports that life expectancy rose from 66.6 to 69.9 years under NST1.

questions.stem: NST2 reports that the number of public services available online expanded over the NST1 period from 155 to:
questions.explanation: NST2 section 1.1 (transformational governance) notes that online services grew from 155 to over 680.

questions.stem: NST2 reports that citizen satisfaction with the quality of service delivery had reached what level in 2023?
questions.explanation: NST2 section 1.2 gives 78% citizen satisfaction in 2023 and the M&E matrix targets a level above 90% by 2028/29.

questions.stem: NST2 aims to raise the proportion of poor and vulnerable people covered by social protection systems from 11% to what level by 2028/29?
questions.explanation: Annex 1 of NST2 (indicator 28) sets a mid-term target of 16% for 2026/27 and an end-period target of 20% for 2028/29.

questions.stem: Under NST2, which cadre provides coaching, referrals and behaviour change support to empower households taking part in graduation from poverty?
questions.explanation: NST2 Annex 2, priority area PA-36, provides for coaching, referrals and behaviour change support through para-social workers for graduation participants.

questions.stem: Under NST2, legal aid for vulnerable people is to be expanded through a legal aid week that is held:
questions.explanation: NST2 Annex 2 (PA-44) expands legal aid through a "semestrial" legal aid week, meaning one held every six months.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT a headline indicator for the NST2 Social Transformation pillar?
options: Improve the quality and market relevance of education
Reduce case backlogs in the justice system by half
Reduce the stunting rate for children under five years from 33% to 15%
Increase graduation out of poverty and enhanced coverage of social safety nets
questions.explanation: The Social Transformation headline indicators in NST2 cover education quality, stunting, WASH access and graduation from poverty. Reducing case backlogs by half is a headline target of the Transformational Governance pillar.

questions.stem: NST2 expects public entities to adhere to IPSAS and PFM regulations. What does IPSAS stand for?
options: International Procurement and Supply Accounting Standards
questions.explanation: NST2 section 5.3 refers to International Public Sector Accounting Standards (IPSAS), with a phased implementation of accrual standards.

questions.stem: NST2 plans to improve justice service delivery by enhancing the functioning and use of the IECMS. What does IECMS stand for?
options: Integrated Evidence and Crime Management System
questions.explanation: NST2 section 5.1 names the Integrated Electronic Case Management System (IECMS) among the technologies used to improve justice service delivery.

questions.stem: Vision 2050 notes that NISR projects Rwanda's population to reach about 17.6 million by 2035 and about how many people by 2050?
questions.explanation: Vision 2050 (Human Development pillar) says the population will rise by more than 50% to 17.6 million by 2035 and double to about 22.1 million by 2050.

questions.stem: Fill in the missing: Vision 2050 aims to reduce the fertility rate from 4.1 births per woman (DHS 2019/2020) to high income country standards of ........... births per woman in 2050.
questions.explanation: Vision 2050 targets a fertility rate of 2.3 births per woman in 2050, down from 4.1 in the 2019/20 DHS.

questions.stem: Vision 2050 says Rwanda reduced the poverty rate from 78% after 1994 to what level in 2017?
questions.explanation: Vision 2050 (overarching goals) records a fall of the poverty rate from 78% after 1994 to 38% in 2017, with the aim of eliminating poverty altogether.

questions.stem: Fill in the missing: According to MINALOC, the value of Umuganda in money terms was estimated at 4 billion Rwandan francs in 2007 and increased up to ........... in 2016.
questions.explanation: Vision 2050 notes that Umuganda supports the national budget: its value rose from 4 billion Rwandan francs in 2007 to 19 billion in 2016 (MINALOC).

questions.stem: Which two home-grown justice mechanisms does Vision 2050 say contribute to reducing backlogs from the ordinary courts and to reducing the cost of access to justice?
options: Gacaca and Access to Justice Bureaus (MAJ)
Abunzi and Access to Justice Bureaus (MAJ)
questions.explanation: Vision 2050 says Abunzi and the Access to Justice Bureaus reduce backlogs and the cost of justice, whereas Gacaca is credited with bringing justice after the genocide against the Tutsi.

questions.stem: Vision 2050 aims to enhance local revenue mobilisation so that urban and rural local governments can cater for what share of their development projects?
questions.explanation: Vision 2050 sets a target that local revenue can finance 85% of local development projects, reducing reliance on central government transfers.

questions.stem: Fill in the missing: Under Vision 2050, child stunting (under 5 years) will be reduced from 33% (2020) to ........... in 2035 and 3% in 2050.
questions.explanation: Vision 2050 sets stunting targets of 5.5% in 2035 and 3% in 2050; NST2 targets below 15% by 2029 as a step toward them.

questions.stem: Vision 2050 notes that citizens who identify themselves as Rwandans first, and not by ethnic identity, stand at what share (CRC, 2016)?
questions.explanation: Vision 2050 gives 95.3% (CRC, 2016) for citizens identifying as Rwandans first; 94.55% (RRB, 2015) is the figure for social cohesion and mutual trust.

questions.stem: Vision 2050 warns that with an average GDP growth rate of only around 7%, Rwanda would become a high-income country only by:
questions.explanation: Vision 2050 uses this example to show that "business as usual" is not sufficient: around 7% growth would delay high-income status to 2075.

questions.stem: How many priority areas does the Social Transformation pillar of NST1 have?
questions.explanation: NST1 Social Transformation has 5 priority areas (graduation from poverty, malnutrition, health, education and a modern Rwandan household); Economic Transformation has 7 and Transformational Governance has 6.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT a priority area of the NST1 Transformational Governance pillar?
options: Ensure safety and security of citizens and property
Increase citizens' participation, engagement and partnerships in development
Promoting resilience and enhancing graduation from poverty and extreme poverty
questions.explanation: Graduation from poverty is Priority Area 1 of the Social Transformation pillar, whereas the six Transformational Governance priority areas include justice, security and citizen participation.

questions.stem: NST1 targeted an increase in the proportion of cases resolved at Abunzi level from 86% to what level by 2024?
questions.explanation: Paragraph 95 of NST1 targets 94% of cases resolved at Abunzi level by 2024, up from 86% in 2015/16.

questions.stem: To reduce school dropout, NST1 planned to introduce which community workers at Cell level?
questions.explanation: NST1 paragraph 68 proposes Education community workers (Abajyanama b'Uburezi) at Cell level, alongside a student ID system and School General Assembly Committees, to fight dropout.

questions.stem: Which law of 2013 provides for the organisation of statistical activities in Rwanda and was one of the legal bases of the 2022 census?
questions.explanation: Section 1.2 of the RPHC5 report cites Law No 53bis/2013 (which establishes NISR) and Law No 45/2013 of 16/06/2013 on the organization of statistical activities.

questions.stem: In which years were the five modern censuses held in Rwanda, up to the fifth census?
questions.explanation: RPHC5 section 1.1 lists the five modern censuses as 1978, 1991, 2002, 2012 and 2022.

questions.stem: The 2012 Population and Housing Census indicated a total population of:
questions.explanation: RPHC5 section 1.1 recalls that the 2012 census counted 10,515,973 people, against 13,246,394 in 2022.

questions.stem: According to RPHC5, which Province has the highest total fertility rate (TFR) in Rwanda?
questions.explanation: RPHC5 shows the City of Kigali with the lowest TFR (3.0) and the Eastern Province with the highest (4.0 children per woman).

extras.title: Economic Development Officer — Mock Exam 8
extras.summary: Practice for SEDO / Economic Development Officer recruitment: governance concepts and local economic development, plus field practice and service delivery.

questions.stem: According to RPHC5, about what percentage of children's births were registered?
questions.explanation: The RPHC5 executive summary reports that about 94% of children's births were registered (urban 93.8%, rural 94.4%) with no variation by sex.

questions.stem: RPHC5 defines the elderly as people aged 60 and above. What share of the resident population do they represent?
questions.explanation: Section 4.4 of RPHC5 counts 862,929 people aged 60 and above, which is 6.5% of residents; people aged 65 and above are 4.2%.

questions.stem: According to RPHC5, what share of private households in Rwanda reside in planned rural settlements (Umudugudu)?
questions.explanation: RPHC5 reports 65% of private households in planned rural settlements (up from about 49% in 2012), 15% in dispersed housing and 9% in spontaneous or squatter settlements.

questions.stem: Contrary to the other provinces, most private households in the City of Kigali are:
questions.explanation: RPHC5 shows that 61% of households in Kigali are tenants and 34% are owners, whereas about 72% of households nationally own their dwelling.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT counted as an improved source of drinking water in RPHC5?
questions.explanation: The RPHC5 footnote lists improved sources as piped water, public taps, tube well or borehole, protected spring or well, rain and mineral water; unprotected springs and wells are unsafe sources.

questions.stem: RPHC5 counted 374,319 residents in Nyarugenge, 879,505 in Gasabo and 491,731 in Kicukiro. What was the total population of the City of Kigali?
questions.explanation: Adding 374,319 + 879,505 + 491,731 gives 1,745,555, the figure in Table 1 of RPHC5 for the City of Kigali.

questions.stem: According to the Vital Statistics Report 2022, until 2006 the lowest office for civil registration in Rwanda was the:
questions.explanation: The report explains that registration was done at District level until the 2006 decentralisation phase, when it was extended to the Sector, adding the Sector Executive Secretary as a civil registrar.

questions.stem: The National Centralized and Integrated CRVS system (NCI-CRVS) was officially launched on:
questions.explanation: Section 2.3.2.1 of the Vital Statistics Report 2022 gives 10 August 2020 as the official launch of NCI-CRVS; the CRVS web-based application dates from 1 January 2015.

questions.stem: By 2022, births, deaths, marriages, divorces, annulment of marriage, recognition of a child and adoption were registered through NCI-CRVS. Which event's module was still being completed?
questions.explanation: The report says 7 of 9 modules were operational; the remaining two, legitimization and guardianship, were almost completed.

questions.stem: As a Cell Executive Secretary supporting civil registration, you want to benchmark performance against the CRVS strategic plan of 2017. What were its fixed targets for birth and death registration completeness?
questions.explanation: Section 3.3 of the Vital Statistics Report 2022 states the CRVS strategic plan (2017) targets of 95% completeness for births and 90% for deaths.

questions.stem: According to the Vital Statistics Report 2022, birth registration completeness stood at what level in 2022?
questions.explanation: Section 3.4.1 gives 92.9% completeness in 2022, up from 87% in 2019 (84.2% in 2021); the strategic plan target was 95%.

questions.stem: According to the Vital Statistics Report 2022, which matrimonial regime was chosen by 98.2% of the marriages registered in 2022?
questions.explanation: Table 17 of the report shows 34,890 marriages under community of property (98.2%), 530 under limited community of property (0.3%) and 93 under separation of property.

questions.stem: The EICV7 extreme poverty line of RWF 356,432 per adult per year is the annual cost of food equivalent to how many kilocalories per day per adult?
questions.explanation: The EICV7 booklet defines the food (extreme) poverty line as the cost of 2,400 kcal per day per adult at January 2024 prices, RWF 356,432 a year.

questions.stem: EICV7 gives a poverty rate of 39.8% in 2017 (new series) and 27.4% in 2024. By how many percentage points did the poverty rate decrease?
questions.explanation: The difference 39.8 - 27.4 is 12.4 percentage points, which the EICV7 booklet gives as the decrease in 2024 compared to 2017. The 5.9-point fall relates to extreme poverty.

questions.stem: According to EICV7 (2023/24), how many of the 30 districts had a poverty rate below 30%?
questions.explanation: The EICV7 booklet reports 16 of 30 districts below a 30% poverty rate in 2024, against only 8 districts in 2017.

questions.stem: According to the EICV7 booklet, which province has the lowest inequality (Gini coefficient)?
questions.explanation: The booklet states that the City of Kigali has the highest inequality and the Northern Province the lowest; the national Gini coefficient is 0.37.

questions.stem: In the EICV7 booklet, quintiles split the population into five equal groups based on:
options: The distance to the nearest health centre
How much each adult spends in a year
The land area each household cultivates
questions.explanation: The EICV7 booklet defines quintiles by annual adult spending, from the lowest-spending group (Q1) to the highest (Q5).

questions.stem: Which period does the fifth Strategic Plan for Agriculture Transformation (PSTA 5) cover?
questions.explanation: PSTA 5 is the agriculture sector plan for 2024/25 to 2028/29, which implements the second National Strategy for Transformation (NST2). See the Executive Summary of PSTA 5.

questions.stem: What is the total estimated cost of implementing PSTA 5?
questions.explanation: PSTA 5 is costed at RWF 6,406.5 billion, of which the private sector is expected to provide a large share. The other figures in the options are sub-totals (private share, local currency, Priority Area I).

questions.stem: What share of the PSTA 5 budget is allocated to Priority Area I, Modernization of Agriculture and Animal Resources Production for Climate Resilient Agri-food Systems?
questions.explanation: Priority Area I takes the biggest share of the PSTA 5 budget at 58.6%, while Priority Area II gets 17.5% and Priority Area III gets 23.9%.

questions.stem: In 2023, agriculture accounted for about what share of Rwanda's GDP, according to PSTA 5?
questions.explanation: PSTA 5 states that in 2023 agriculture accounted for 27% of GDP and about 34% of exports (Introduction).

questions.stem: According to PSTA 5, about what share of Rwanda's farmers are women?
questions.explanation: PSTA 5 (Section 2, Sector performance) reports that about 58% of farmers are women and 95% of farmers live in rural areas.

questions.stem: PSTA 5 projects that the stunting rate, which stood at 32.4%, will be reduced to:
questions.explanation: The PSTA 5 Executive Summary projects stunting falling from 32.4% to below 15% by the end of the strategy in 2028/29.

questions.stem: Under PSTA 5, AgriHubs are market-driven agricultural production sites operating on large land parcels of at least:
questions.explanation: PSTA 5 (Key innovations, Section 4.5) describes AgriHubs as large parcels of at least 500 hectares, often irrigated and run mainly by large-scale farmers or investors.

questions.stem: Food Basket Sites (FoBaSi) under PSTA 5 are built on consolidated land sites of not less than:
questions.explanation: FoBaSi are consolidated sites of at least 5 hectares under one management and are mainly run by smallholder farmer organisations (PSTA 5, Section 4.5).

questions.stem: According to PSTA 5, how many hectares had been developed for irrigation by 2023?
questions.explanation: PSTA 5 (Section 2.2.1) reports 71,585 ha under irrigation by 2023. The 110,905 ha and 138,579 ha figures are radical terrace areas, not irrigation.

questions.stem: Under Output 1.1.5 of PSTA 5, how many large-scale irrigation schemes with existing feasibility studies are to be activated, and over how many hectares?
questions.explanation: PSTA 5 aims to activate 20 schemes covering 45,000 ha that already have feasibility studies, and to initiate 19 new schemes across the country.

questions.stem: At least what share of Small-Scale Irrigation Technologies (SSIT) shall be given to women farmers under PSTA 5?
questions.explanation: PSTA 5 sets a floor of 30% of SSIT for women farmers to reduce the gender gap in access (16% of male-headed versus 10% of female-headed households).

questions.stem: According to PSTA 5, only what share of farmers receive formal finance for their operations?
questions.explanation: PSTA 5 (Section 3.1) reports that only 17% of farmers get formal finance, while another 60% rely on informal lenders or family.

questions.stem: To create a critical mass and allow risk spreading, PSTA 5 proposes to make agriculture insurance compulsory for which farmers?
options: All large-scale crop and livestock farmers
questions.explanation: Under Output 3.2.2 of PSTA 5, insurance would be compulsory for all large-scale crop and livestock farmers, with the Government subsidising output coverage products.

questions.stem: PSTA 5 supports compliance with the newly adopted zero-grazing policy in which province?
questions.explanation: PSTA 5 (Output 1.2.1) gives support for compliance with the newly adopted zero-grazing policy in the Eastern Province as an example of tailoring AnimalHub interventions to local contexts.

questions.stem: Under PSTA 5, skill development plans aim to increase the success rate of artificial insemination (AI) in cattle to:
questions.explanation: PSTA 5 (Output 1.2.2) notes a low AI success rate of 40% and aims to raise it to 60% through LN2 plants near AnimalHubs and training of AI technicians.

questions.stem: The National Land Use and Development Masterplan 2020-2050, as cited in PSTA 5, reserves how many hectares for agriculture by 2050?
questions.explanation: PSTA 5 (Output 1.1.1) says the Masterplan reserves 1,243,300 ha for agriculture by 2050, with investment concentrated on the 841,400 ha judged highly suitable.

questions.stem: When the Farmer Field School (FFS) approach was first introduced in Rwanda in 2008, it was meant mainly to promote:
questions.explanation: FFS began in 2008 as a tool for integrated pest management and later widened to general crop management. It was integrated into Twigire Muhinzi in 2016.

questions.stem: Under Twigire Muhinzi, an FFS facilitator cooperative signs a three-party, performance-based contract with which parties?
questions.explanation: FFS facilitators are organised in district cooperatives that sign a performance-based contract with RAB and the district; payment is linked to performance.

questions.stem: Within the Twigire Muhinzi extension system, which level is responsible for daily coordination of the programme?
questions.explanation: RAB provides technical support to Twigire Muhinzi, but daily coordination is the responsibility of districts, in line with decentralised agricultural services.

questions.stem: In the second season of a new FFS group, how often does the FFS facilitator join the group at its learning plot?
questions.explanation: In season one the facilitator works with the group at least weekly; in season two, once every two weeks; from season three, only upon request.

questions.stem: According to an impact study cited in PSTA 5, the yields of Farmer Field School (FFS) participants grew by close to:
questions.explanation: PSTA 5 (Output 3.1.2) cites an impact study in which FFS participants' yields grew by close to 38%, while farmers trained by farmer promoters had 11% higher yields. (The 75% figure in the same passage is the milk-yield gain of livestock FFS participants.)

questions.stem: According to the Nutrition Sensitive Agriculture Mainstreaming Guideline, Season C, practised mainly in lowland marshland areas, starts in:
questions.explanation: The guideline describes Season C as running from July to September, with harvest in September, mainly in marshland areas during the drier season.

questions.stem: In the NSA Mainstreaming Guideline, the feasibility assessment used to identify Nutrient Dense Foods (NDF) is based on how many criteria?
questions.explanation: The third step of NDF identification uses four criteria: nutrient content density, technical, social and economic feasibility (Section 3.2).

questions.stem: The NSA Mainstreaming Guideline recalls a recommendation to set a target of over what share of tree-and-shrub cover on all farmland by 2030?
questions.explanation: In the kitchen garden section, the guideline recalls the national agroforestry strategy's recommendation of over 10% tree-and-shrub cover on all farmland by 2030.

questions.stem: According to CFSVA 2018 cited in the NSA Mainstreaming Guideline, about what share of children achieved the minimum acceptable diet (MAD)?
questions.explanation: The Introduction of the guideline reports that only about 17 percent of children achieved the minimum acceptable diet, based on dietary diversity and meal frequency.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT among the systemic enablers prioritised under Priority Area III of PSTA 5?
questions.explanation: Priority Area III covers innovation and technology transfer, agriculture financing and de-risking, digitalization, and planning and coordination. Export promotion belongs to Priority Area II.

questions.stem: Choose the false response: PSTA 5 will advocate which of the following sustainable practices in mechanization?
questions.explanation: Output 1.1.8 promotes direct sowing, minimal tillage, land levelling and crop residue retention. Burning residues is the opposite of retention.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT one of the four pillars of food security used in the NSA Mainstreaming Guideline?
questions.explanation: The four pillars of food security are availability, access, utilization and stability (Section 2.1). Profitability is not a pillar.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT a type of human capital generated through the FFS approach under Twigire Muhinzi?
questions.explanation: The FAO/IFPRI case study lists technical, social and functional skills and empowerment as the human capital generated by FFS. Political skills are not listed.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT named as an indigenous vegetable in the NSA Mainstreaming Guideline?
questions.explanation: The guideline lists amaranths, African eggplant, spider plant, pumpkin and nightshade as indigenous. Cabbage is listed among the exotic vegetables.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT named in PSTA 5 among the nutrition-sensitive social protection programmes to be maintained and scaled up?
options: One Cup of Milk per Child Program
questions.explanation: Output 2.3.1 names Childhood Development Programs, VUP and One Cup of Milk per Child. NAIS is an agriculture risk-management scheme, not a nutrition safety net.

questions.stem: Fill in the missing: The key strategic entry point for unlocking the Agri-food system in the PSTA 5 theory of change is to connect farmers to ................
questions.explanation: PSTA 5 (Section 4.4) argues that linking farmers to remunerative markets raises incomes, which funds investment in inputs, technologies and resilience.

questions.stem: How does the NSA Mainstreaming Guideline define Nutrition Sensitive Agriculture (NSA)?
options: A food-based approach to agricultural development that puts nutritionally rich foods, dietary diversity and food fortification at the heart of overcoming malnutrition
A subsidy scheme that lowers fertiliser prices for the poorest farmers
A crop-based approach that puts cash crops and export earnings ahead of household diets
A health programme that distributes micronutrient supplements to children under five
