questions.explanation: Section 2.1 of the guideline defines NSA as a food-based approach to agricultural development centred on nutritious foods, dietary diversity and fortification.

extras.title: Economic Development Officer — Mock Exam 9
extras.summary: Practice for SEDO / Economic Development Officer recruitment: governance concepts and local economic development, plus field practice and service delivery.

questions.stem: What are Farm Service Centres (FSCs) under PSTA 5?
options: Government warehouses that store the national strategic grain reserve
Local hubs providing farmers with quality inputs, capacity building, finance, technology and market linkages
Cooperative banks that provide loans to farmers
Research stations that develop new seed varieties
questions.explanation: Output 1.1.6 describes FSCs as hubs giving farmers a full range of services, intended to fix delays in timely delivery of quality inputs and to create local jobs.

questions.stem: What does the Kinyarwanda name Twigire Muhinzi, given to Rwanda's national agricultural extension system, mean?
questions.explanation: Twigire Muhinzi, adopted in 2014, means self-reliance in farming. Seeing is believing is the farmer promoter motto and The plant is the teacher is the FFS motto.

questions.stem: Fill in the missing: Under PSTA 5, the Government of Rwanda will continue the path toward becoming a market ................ rather than a market actor.
questions.explanation: Outcome 3.4 of PSTA 5 says the Government will become a market facilitator rather than a market actor, shifting from tactical implementation to strategic facilitation.

questions.stem: In PSTA 5, what does CAES stand for?
questions.explanation: CAES is the Customized Agriculture Extension System, developed to complement Twigire Muhinzi and make extension more sustainable and market-responsive.

questions.stem: In PSTA 5, what does CAHWs stand for?
questions.explanation: CAHWs are Community Animal Health Workers, trained to give basic animal health services. PSTA 5 plans to expand and rebrand them as Twigire Mworozi.

questions.stem: In the NSA Mainstreaming Guideline, what does DPEM stand for?
options: District Programme for Early Child Meals
Development Plan for Education and Meals
District Plan for the Eradication of Malnutrition
questions.explanation: DPEM is the District Plan for the Eradication of Malnutrition, under which Irerero pre-school feeding and community kitchens operate.

questions.stem: Under the NSA Mainstreaming Guideline, fruits and vegetables in Rwanda are managed by which institution, together with essential oils, coffee and tea?
questions.explanation: The guideline says horticulture is managed under the National Agriculture Export Board (NAEB) together with essential oils, coffee and tea.

questions.stem: PSTA 5 aims to raise the share of food-secure households from 79.4% to 88%. By how many percentage points will the share rise?
questions.explanation: 88% minus 79.4% equals 8.6 percentage points. These are the PSTA 5 baseline and end-of-strategy targets for food-secure households.

questions.stem: Livestock FFS participants raised their milk yield from 4.5 to 7.9 litres per day. Which percentage increase does this represent, to the nearest 5%?
questions.explanation: 7.9 divided by 4.5 is about 1.76, an increase of about 75%, which matches the figure reported in PSTA 5 (Output 3.1.2).

questions.stem: In the 2023 RAB study cited in PSTA 5, which value chain recorded the highest post-harvest losses?
questions.explanation: The RAB study found losses of 33.5% for tomato, 25.2% for Irish potatoes, 24.8% for cassava, 13.8% for maize, 12.4% for rice and 11.3% for beans (Output 2.2.2).

questions.stem: As an Economic Development Officer advising smallholders in a drought-prone sector who need quick results, which irrigation option does PSTA 5 prioritise because of its faster implementation and broader farmer reach?
options: Large dams built by the district
questions.explanation: Output 1.1.5 notes that large-scale schemes typically take five years, so small-scale irrigation is prioritised for faster implementation and broader reach, with solar-driven equipment piloted.

questions.stem: As an Economic Development Officer, you notice that farmers in an irrigation scheme grow only staples because profitability drives crop choice. According to the NSA Mainstreaming Guideline, how can production of nutrient dense foods (NDF) be promoted in the scheme?
options: Ban staple crops in the scheme
Wait until farmers ask for NDF on their own
Combine it with market creation for NDF, such as nutrition campaigns, nutrition education, subsidies and school feeding
Convert the scheme to export-only cash crops
questions.explanation: Section 4.3 of the guideline says NDF production in irrigation schemes must be combined with market creation for NDF, because farmers only grow NDF for sale if a market outlet exists.

questions.stem: Under Rwanda's personal income tax rules, a micro-enterprise is a business activity whose turnover per tax period is equal to or less than:
questions.explanation: The RRA taxation booklet (Nov 2025), section 4.1.1, says micro-enterprises have a turnover of Frw 12,000,000 or less and pay a flat amount of tax; above that up to Frw 20,000,000 is a small enterprise.

questions.stem: A small trader in your Sector has an annual turnover of Frw 15,000,000 and stays in the flat-rate tax regime. How much lumpsum personal income tax does the trader owe for the year?
questions.explanation: A turnover between Frw 12,000,001 and Frw 20,000,000 is a small enterprise taxed at a lumpsum of 3% of annual turnover (RRA booklet, section 4.1.2), so 3% x 15,000,000 = Frw 450,000.

questions.stem: According to the 2025 RRA taxation booklet, at what rate is the taxable business profit of a company (corporate income tax) taxed?
questions.explanation: Section 4.2 of the RRA booklet states that taxable business profit is taxed at 28%; only newly listed companies get reduced rates of 20% or 25% for five years.

questions.stem: A taxpayer who has already paid the first annual income tax must pay the quarterly prepayments not later than which dates?
questions.explanation: Section 4.1 (and section 5) of the RRA booklet gives the quarterly prepayment deadlines as 30 June, 30 September and 31 December of the year of taxable business activities.

questions.stem: What percentage of the invoice sum, excluding VAT, is retained as withholding tax when successful bidders of public tenders are paid?
questions.explanation: Section 6.1 of the RRA booklet sets withholding tax on public tenders at 3% of the invoice sum excluding VAT; the 5% rate applies to commercial imports and 15% to dividends, interest and royalties.

questions.stem: In Rwandan tax law, a casual labourer is an employee who does work needing no special skills and who is employed for an aggregate period not exceeding ..... during a twelve-month period.
questions.explanation: Section 6.2 of the RRA booklet defines a casual labourer by an aggregate employment of not more than thirty days in twelve months; such income is taxed at a special 15% rate above Frw 60,000 per month.

questions.stem: What is the standard rate of value added tax (VAT) on taxable goods and services supplied in Rwanda or imported, other than zero-rated supplies?
questions.explanation: Section 7 of the RRA booklet (Law 049/2023 as amended in 2025) states VAT is 0% on zero-rated goods or services and 18% on all other goods and services supplied in Rwanda or imported.

questions.stem: A person carrying out taxable activities must register for value added tax when his or her turnover in the previous fiscal year exceeds:
questions.explanation: Section 7.1 of the RRA booklet requires VAT registration within seven days when annual turnover exceeds Frw 20,000,000 (or Frw 5,000,000 in the previous quarter). Frw 200,000,000 is the threshold for monthly VAT declaration.

questions.stem: Under the taxes levied by decentralized entities, immovable property tax on a building and its plot used for commercial purposes is charged at:
questions.explanation: Section 12.1 of the RRA booklet gives 0.5% for residential use, 0.3% for commercial use and 0.1% for industrial use and for micro and small businesses.

questions.stem: The tax on the sale of immovable property is levied after deducting an amount that is not subject to tax. How much is this amount?
questions.explanation: Section 12.4 of the RRA booklet says the tax on sale of immovable property (2% or 2.5% depending on the seller) is levied after deduction of Frw 5,000,000 which is not taxed.

questions.stem: A VAT-registered person sells goods without issuing an electronic invoice. The administrative fine is equal to how many times the value of the evaded VAT?
questions.explanation: Section 13.5.1 of the RRA booklet sets the fine at ten times the evaded VAT, doubling to twenty times if repeated within two years. Two times applies to persons not registered for VAT.

questions.stem: A person convicted of the offence of tax evasion in Rwanda is liable to imprisonment for a term of:
questions.explanation: Section 13.6.1 of the RRA booklet states that tax evasion, for example by using forged documents or hiding taxable goods, is punished by imprisonment of not less than two and not more than five years.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT an accessory sanction that may be imposed on a person who commits a fault or an offence under tax law?
options: Closure of business activities for a period not exceeding thirty days
Being barred from bidding for public tenders
Confiscation of the offender's residential house
questions.explanation: Section 13.7 of the RRA booklet lists closure for up to 30 days, exclusion from public tenders, withdrawal of the business register and publication in the media; confiscating a residence is not listed.

questions.stem: A trader starts a taxable business activity in a District in July. For the trading licence tax, what does the trader pay for that year?
options: The tax for the whole year
The tax for the months after July only
The tax for the remaining months of the year, including July
questions.explanation: Section 12.2 of the RRA booklet says that when taxable trading activities start after January, the tax is for the remaining months of the year, including the month in which the activities started.

questions.stem: Choose the false response: Which of the following is NOT a category of taxable minerals under the tax on minerals?
questions.explanation: Section 9.1 of the RRA booklet (Law 56/2024) lists six taxable mineral categories: gemstones, rare earth elements, energy minerals, platinum group metals, base metals and gold. Timber and forest products are not minerals and are not a category.

questions.stem: Choose the false response: Which of the following is NOT a right of a taxpayer in Rwanda?
options: To be heard on a draft rectification note
To set the tax rate that applies to his or her business
To lodge an appeal with the Commissioner General
questions.explanation: Section 3.1 of the RRA booklet lists the taxpayer's rights, including being heard on a draft rectification note, appealing to the Commissioner General and requesting amicable settlement; tax rates are set by law.

questions.stem: In tax administration, what does TIN stand for?
questions.explanation: Section 3.2.1 of the RRA booklet says the Registrar General assigns a taxpayer identification number (TIN), which is used for payment of any tax and written on tax declarations.

questions.stem: The tourism tax on accommodation is charged at what percentage of the amount paid or payable for accommodation, exclusive of VAT?
questions.explanation: Section 8 of the RRA booklet (Law 015/2025) sets the tourism tax on accommodation at 3%; the facility must register, charge the tax and remit it to the Tax Administration.

questions.stem: Within how many days following the tax period (a calendar month) must a taxpayer declare and pay excise duty?
questions.explanation: Section 11.1 of the RRA booklet says the excise tax period is the calendar month and the declaration and payment are due within five days after it, unlike VAT, which is due within 15 days.

questions.stem: In the 2025 Labour Force Survey, 4,772,704 persons were employed and 676,340 were unemployed. The labour force was therefore about:
questions.explanation: LFS 2025 defines the labour force as the sum of the employed and the unemployed: 4,772,704 + 676,340 = 5,449,044, about 5.4 million. The 8.5 million figure is the working-age population and 3.1 million is the population outside the labour force.

questions.stem: In a Sector, 1,000 persons are of working age. Of them 600 are employed and 100 are unemployed (seeking and available for work); the rest are outside the labour force. Using the Labour Force Survey definition, what is the unemployment rate?
questions.explanation: LFS 2025 defines the unemployment rate as unemployed persons divided by the total labour force. The labour force is 600 + 100 = 700, so 100 / 700 = 14.3%.

questions.stem: According to the Labour Force Survey 2025, the employment-to-population ratio in Rwanda was:
questions.explanation: LFS 2025 reports that the employment-to-population ratio rose to 55.9% in 2025 from 53.5% in 2024. The 63.8% figure is the labour force participation rate.

questions.stem: In the Labour Force Survey 2025, the unemployment rate among youth (aged 16-30 years) was:
questions.explanation: LFS 2025 found unemployment more prevalent among youth (14.7%) than adults (10.8%); the national rate was 12.4%. The 19.3% figure is the youth rate of February 2019 in the National Employment Policy.

questions.stem: In the Labour Force Survey, a person of working age is classified as employed if, during a reference period of 7 days, he or she did some work for pay or profit for at least:
questions.explanation: Following the 19th ICLS definition, section 4 of LFS 2025 counts as employed anyone who did some work, even for just one hour, for profit or pay, or who was temporarily absent from a job.

questions.stem: According to the Labour Force Survey 2025, the national strategy for transformation targets the creation of how many decent and productive jobs between 2024 and 2029?
questions.explanation: Section 4.9 of LFS 2025 states the target of 1,250,000 decent and productive jobs over five years, around 250,000 jobs a year. The 1.5 million target belonged to NST1 (2017-2024).

questions.stem: In the Labour Force Survey, long-term unemployment refers to unemployed persons who have been actively seeking employment for:
questions.explanation: Section 5.2 of LFS 2025 defines long-term unemployment as active job search of 12 months or more; 16.4% of the unemployed were long-term unemployed in 2025.

questions.stem: In 2025, what share of the population outside the labour force was engaged in subsistence agriculture?
questions.explanation: Section 6.1 of LFS 2025 shows 48.7% of persons outside the labour force were in subsistence agriculture, 23% were exclusively students and 28.2% were others. The 36.2% figure is the share of the working-age population outside the labour force.

questions.stem: Choose the false response: Labour underutilization in the Labour Force Survey includes all of the following EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: Section 5.3 of LFS 2025 says labour underutilization includes unemployment, time-related underemployment and the potential labour force; informal-sector employment is a separate topic.

questions.stem: In labour statistics, what does ICLS stand for?
questions.explanation: The Labour Force Survey follows standards adopted by the 19th International Conference of Labour Statisticians (ICLS) in 2013 on work, employment and labour underutilization.

questions.stem: In the Rwanda Labour Force Survey, what does ICSE stand for?
options: International Council for Statistics on Employment
Integrated Classification of Sectors of Employment
International Classification of Status in Employment
International Code of Skills and Education
questions.explanation: Chapter 4 of LFS 2025 explains that status in employment was reported using the International Classification of Status in Employment (ICSE-93) until the updated ICSE-18 was adopted in February 2025.

questions.stem: In the youth chapter of the Labour Force Survey, what does NEET stand for?
options: Not Eligible for Employment, Education or Training
Not in Employment, Education or Training
questions.explanation: Section 7.2 of LFS 2025 analyses Youth Not in Employment, Education or Training (NEET), an indicator of young people neither working nor studying nor training.

questions.stem: The Revised National Employment Policy (2019) states that the Government of Rwanda first developed and adopted a National Employment Policy in:
questions.explanation: Chapter 1 of the Revised National Employment Policy 2019 says the first National Employment Policy was developed and adopted in 2007, in line with ILO Convention No. 122 of 1964.

questions.stem: In the Revised National Employment Policy, the output elasticity of employment was 1.8 for which sub-sector?
questions.explanation: Section 5.3 of the policy gives output elasticities of 1.8 for manufacturing, 1.7 for construction and 0.94 for transport and communication, so manufacturing and construction generate the most jobs.

questions.stem: Choose the false response: The National Employment Programme (NEP) adopted in January 2014 is based on four pillars. Which one is NOT among them?
questions.explanation: Section 5.5.5 of the Revised National Employment Policy lists skills development, entrepreneurship and business development, labour market interventions, and coordination with monitoring and evaluation as the four NEP pillars.

questions.stem: Fill in the missing: According to the Revised National Employment Policy (2019), time-related underemployment refers to the situation when the working time of persons in employment is insufficient (less than ..... a week) in relation to alternative employment situations in which they are willing and available to engage.
questions.explanation: Section 5.5.2 of the Revised National Employment Policy defines time-related underemployment as working time of less than 35 hours a week while the person is willing and available to work more.

questions.stem: Choose the false response: Which of the following is NOT a major function of public employment services (PES) according to the Revised National Employment Policy?
options: Job search assistance and matching services including counselling
Collection and analysis of labour market information
Administration of active labour market policies
Collection of income tax from employers
questions.explanation: Section 5.8 of the policy lists job search assistance and matching, labour market information, administration of active labour market policies and administration of unemployment benefits; tax collection is the role of the Tax Administration.

questions.stem: Who chairs the National Steering Committee that gives overall guidance on the implementation of the Revised National Employment Policy?
options: The Minister of Finance and Economic Planning
The Minister of Public Service and Labour
The Chief Executive Officer of the Rwanda Development Board
questions.explanation: Section 7.2 of the policy says the National Steering Committee is chaired by the Minister of Public Service and Labour and meets biannually, with the Directorate General of Labour and Employment as secretariat.

questions.stem: In EICV7 (2023/24), the extreme poverty line, based on the cost of food equivalent to 2,400 kcal per day, is about how much per adult per year (January 2024 prices)?
questions.explanation: The EICV7 booklet gives an extreme (food) poverty line of RWF 356,432 per adult per year; RWF 560,127 is the full poverty line, while RWF 105,064 was the 2014 extreme line.

extras.title: Economic Development Officer — Mock Exam 10
extras.summary: Practice for SEDO / Economic Development Officer recruitment: governance concepts and local economic development, plus field practice and service delivery.

questions.stem: According to EICV7, the extreme poverty rate in 2024 decreased by how many percentage points compared to 2017?
questions.explanation: The EICV7 booklet reports that the extreme poverty rate fell by 5.9 percentage points between 2017 and 2024, to 5.4%. The 12.4-point fall is for the overall poverty rate, now 27.4%.

questions.stem: According to the EICV7 2023/24 results, which area has the highest inequality (Gini coefficient)?
questions.explanation: The EICV7 booklet states that inequality is wider in urban areas; Kigali City has the highest inequality and the Northern Province the lowest, with a national Gini of 0.37.

questions.stem: According to the EICV7 district poverty map, in 2024 how many of the 30 districts had a poverty rate below 30%?
questions.explanation: The EICV7 booklet shows 16 of 30 districts below 30% poverty in 2024, against only 8 districts in 2017.

questions.stem: According to the EICV7 2023/24 poverty ranking by district, which District had the highest poverty rate?
questions.explanation: The EICV7 ranking places Nyamagabe first with 51.4% poverty, followed by Gisagara, Rusizi and Nyanza; the ten highest-poverty districts are in the Western and Southern provinces.

questions.stem: Under the VUP Programme Document (2022), the monthly transfer value for Expanded Public Works was increased to:
questions.explanation: Section 3.6 of the VUP Programme Document raises the Expanded Public Works transfer from Frw 10,000 to Frw 15,000 per month, paid monthly; the Child Grant rose from Frw 7,500 to Frw 10,000.

questions.stem: Under the VUP Programme Document, a classic public works household should receive a minimum cash injection of how much per year?
questions.explanation: Section 3.6 states that classic public works households have labour capacity and should get at least RWF 150,000 per year, enough to cover basic needs and support graduation.

questions.stem: To give a household identified as able to graduate a firm basis for its livelihood, the VUP Programme Document provides a one-off payment of how much, together with financial literacy and coaching?
questions.explanation: Section 5.1.1 of the VUP Programme Document provides a one-off payment of RwF 800,000 in year 1 of the two-year graduation programme, plus financial literacy and coaching.

questions.stem: Expanded Public Works targets households where the working member is ageing but does not qualify for any form of grant. Which age range does the VUP Programme Document give?
questions.explanation: Section 4.2.2 of the VUP Programme Document lists households whose working member is between 55 and 63 years and gets no grant; older persons receive the Old Age Grant instead.

questions.stem: In the VUP Programme Document, what does cPW stand for?
questions.explanation: The acronyms list of the VUP Programme Document gives cPW as Classic Public Works, the short-term employment scheme on community infrastructure; ePW stands for Expanded Public Works.

questions.stem: Under Law 62/2013 establishing LODA, State budget allocations to LODA comprise at least what share of domestic revenues, calculated on the State budget of the previous year?
questions.explanation: Article 12 of Law 62/2013 lists as the first source of LODA property State budget allocations of at least ten percent of domestic revenues, based on the previous year's State budget.

questions.stem: Law 62/2013 requires that at least what percentage of the members of the LODA Board of Directors must be female?
questions.explanation: Article 6 of Law 62/2013 says the Board members are appointed by Presidential Order on the basis of competence and expertise, and at least thirty percent of them must be women.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a mission of LODA under Law 62/2013?
options: To appoint the Executive Secretaries of Districts
To issue land titles to citizens
To establish strategies for creation of high intensive labour and assistance to those unable to perform such jobs
questions.explanation: Article 3 of Law 62/2013 lists LODA's mission, including financing local development, monitoring funds and setting up strategies for labour-intensive work with assistance for those unable to do it, the basis of VUP public works and direct support.

questions.stem: According to the NST2 macroeconomic projections (Table 1), in which year is real GDP growth projected to be highest?
questions.explanation: Table 1 of NST2 shows real GDP growth rising every year from 7.9% in 2024 to 11.5% in 2029, which averages 9.3% over the period.

questions.stem: NST2 projects the manufacturing sub-sector to grow at an average annual rate of:
questions.explanation: NST2 section 2.1(ii) says industry grows by over 10% a year, driven by manufacturing at 10.4%. The 6.5% figure is agriculture and 10.2% is services.

questions.stem: NST2 expects GDP per capita to rise from USD 1,040 in 2023 to what level by 2029?
questions.explanation: The NST2 macroeconomic framework (section 2) targets per capita income of USD 1,369 by 2029.

questions.stem: According to NST2, total investment is expected to reach what share of GDP by 2029?
questions.explanation: NST2 section 2.1(iv) puts total investment at 32.1% of GDP by 2029. The 21.5% figure is private investment alone and 25.9% is the savings rate target.

questions.stem: Fill in the missing: NST2 aims to raise the national savings rate from 12.4% of GDP in 2023 to ...... by 2029.
questions.explanation: NST2 section 2.1(iv) targets a national savings rate of 25.9% of GDP by 2029; 19.6% is only the 2026/27 mid-term value in Annex 1.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT among the driving objectives of the financial sector under NST2?
options: Strengthening Rwanda's role as an international financial services hub
Sustaining the expansion of financial inclusion
questions.explanation: Section 3.9 lists four objectives: financial inclusion, contribution to growth and welfare, an international financial hub and deeper capital markets. Nationalising banks is not one of them.

questions.stem: NST2 projects the current account deficit to fall from 11.8% of GDP in 2023 to what level in 2029?
questions.explanation: NST2 section 2.1(v) projects a 7.9% deficit in 2029; 10.7% is only the 2026/27 mid-term target and 9.5% was the 2017 level.

questions.stem: NST2 expects the tax-to-GDP ratio to rise from 15.2% in 2023/2024 to what level by 2028/2029?
questions.explanation: Under the fiscal policy in NST2 section 2.1(vi), tax collection is strengthened so that the ratio reaches 19.4% by 2028/2029.

questions.stem: Of the total NST2 financing for 2024/25-2028/29, what share is expected to be mobilised by the private sector?
questions.explanation: NST2 section 2.2 says 43% of financing comes from the private sector and the remaining 57% from public resources.

questions.stem: Economic Transformation under NST2 advances which three pillars of Vision 2050?
options: Competitiveness and Integration; Accountable and Capable State Institutions; Human Development
Human Development; Competitiveness and Integration; Urbanization and Agglomeration
Agriculture for Wealth Creation; Human Development; Accountable and Capable State Institutions
Competitiveness and Integration; Agriculture for Wealth Creation; Urbanization and Agglomeration
questions.explanation: The opening of section 3 of NST2 links the economic pillar to these three Vision 2050 pillars; Human Development is served by the Social Transformation Pillar.

questions.stem: NST2 aims to increase the productivity of priority food crops by:
questions.explanation: Section 3.1 of NST2 lists a 50% productivity increase on priority food crops as the first objective for agriculture.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT among the main food crops named in NST2 for the productivity increase?
questions.explanation: Coffee is an export crop. The food crops named in section 3.1 are maize, beans, potatoes, rice, cassava, wheat and bananas.

questions.stem: NST2 plans to increase the application of fertilizers from 70 kg per hectare to:
questions.explanation: Section 3.1 of NST2 sets the fertilizer target at 94.6 kg per hectare, together with more improved seed.

questions.stem: NST2 aims to expand irrigated land from 71,000 ha to over:
questions.explanation: Section 3.1 sets over 130,000 ha under irrigation, with CDAT as one of the major projects. The 160,000 ha figure is for radical terraces.

questions.stem: NST2 aims to increase credit to the agriculture sector from 6% to what share of total loans?
questions.explanation: Section 3.1 of NST2 targets 10% credit to agriculture through de-risking such as crop and livestock insurance; 8% is the 2026/27 mid-term value.

questions.stem: A cooperative of maize and bean farmers in your Cell loses a large part of its harvest because grain is not dried properly after harvest. Which NST2 strategic intervention directly addresses this problem?
options: Establishing new drying infrastructure such as mobile dryers, drying shelters and collection centres
Increasing the quantity of fertilizer applied per hectare
questions.explanation: Priority area PA-03 in Annex 2 of NST2 is to strengthen post-harvest handling, and drying infrastructure for maize and beans is one of its strategic interventions.

questions.stem: Which two key projects does NST2 name as instrumental in achieving its new agricultural management models such as Agri-hubs and Food Basket sites?
options: Kigali Logistics Platform and Gako Beef
Gabiro Agri-business Hub and Bugesera International Airport
Gabiro Agri-business Hub and Gako Beef
Muvumba Multipurpose Dam and Kigali Wholesale Market
questions.explanation: Section 3.1 of NST2 names the Gabiro Agri-business Hub and Gako Beef as instrumental projects.

questions.stem: What does CDAT, the major project named in NST2 for agricultural irrigation, stand for?
options: Commercialization and De-risking for Agriculture Transformation
Cooperative Development for Agriculture and Trade
questions.explanation: Section 3.1 of NST2 spells out CDAT as Commercialization and De-risking for Agriculture Transformation.

questions.stem: Under the NST2 strategic interventions for animal resources, proximity veterinary services are to be provided at which level?
questions.explanation: Annex 2 (PA-02) of NST2 says clinics will reach all districts and proximity services will be provided at sector level.

questions.stem: NST2 plans to increase the percentage of farmers reached by extension services from 35% to:
questions.explanation: Annex 2 (PA-01) of NST2 sets extension coverage at 69%, to be delivered in partnership with the private sector.

questions.stem: What does KSEZ, one of the industrial parks that NST2 plans to operationalise and expand, stand for?
questions.explanation: Section 3.2 of NST2 names KSEZ, Bugesera and Rwamagana as industrial parks and special economic zones to be expanded.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT listed in NST2 as a priority manufacturing sub-sector for attracting private investment?
questions.explanation: Section 3.2 lists nine priority manufacturing sub-sectors; shipbuilding is not among them.

questions.stem: AfCFTA, which NST2 uses to boost exports and economic diplomacy, stands for:
options: African Customs and Free Trade Agreement
questions.explanation: NST2 refers to the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA) in its sections on industry, exports and economic diplomacy.

questions.stem: What is the purpose of the E-commerce Readiness Program that NST2 plans to implement?
options: To train civil servants to manage online tax returns
To replace SACCOs with digital banks
To give a free smartphone to every household
To help SMEs use digital trade platforms for exports
questions.explanation: Section 3.2 of NST2 describes the programme as support for SMEs to leverage digital trade platforms for exports.

questions.stem: NST2 projects revenue from non-traditional exports such as horticulture to grow from USD 1.4 billion in 2023 to what level in 2029?
questions.explanation: Section 3.2 gives USD 3.2 billion for non-traditional exports; USD 2.17 billion is the mining target and USD 7.3 billion is total exports.

questions.stem: NST2 anticipates mining revenues to rise from USD 1.1 billion to what level?
questions.explanation: Section 3.2 of NST2 targets USD 2.17 billion in mining revenues, helped by exploration, professionalised artisanal mining and value addition; USD 1.6 billion is only the 2026/27 mid-term figure.

questions.stem: NST2 aims to nearly double tourism revenues from USD 620 million to:
questions.explanation: Section 3.3 of NST2 positions Rwanda as a high-value ecotourism destination with revenues of USD 1.1 billion by 2029.

questions.stem: What does MICE, the tourism segment that NST2 aims to grow, stand for?
questions.explanation: Section 3.3 of NST2 and its list of acronyms define MICE as Meetings, Incentives, Conferences, and Exhibitions.

questions.stem: NST2 prioritises increasing the share of renewable and clean energy in the power generation mix from 51% to:
questions.explanation: Section 3.4 sets a 60% renewable share by 2029; 53.8% is only the 2026/27 mid-term value in Annex 1.

questions.stem: Fill in the missing: NST2 headline indicators aim for universal access to electricity for productive use with connections countrywide in all ...... and universal access to water supply in all ......
questions.explanation: The economic pillar headline indicators target electricity in all cells and water in all villages, which makes local government planning at Cell and Village level central.

questions.stem: To improve the efficiency of water services, NST2 says which of the following will be reduced?
questions.explanation: Section 3.5 of NST2 reduces non-revenue water, while daily production capacity is more than doubled and piped water in dwellings is increased.

questions.stem: NST2 plans to develop over how many kilometres of feeder roads to facilitate local trade and ease farmers' access to markets?
questions.explanation: Section 3.6 of NST2 sets over 500 km of feeder roads for the period; over 300 km of national roads are also to be built and rehabilitated.

questions.stem: Under NST2, strategic ports on Lake Kivu are to be constructed and operationalised in which locations?
questions.explanation: Section 3.6 of NST2 names Rusizi, Karongi and Rutsiro (Nkora) for Lake Kivu ports, to be built in partnership with the private sector.

questions.stem: NST2 sets the goal of accelerating sustainable urbanization from 27.9% to what level?
questions.explanation: Annex 2 of NST2 (urbanization and rural settlements sector) sets Goal 16 at 39.2% urbanization.

questions.stem: As an Economic and Human Capital Development Officer you find several households living in a flood-prone high-risk zone. Which approach is consistent with NST2?
options: Move them to another unplanned settlement
Wait until a disaster happens before acting
Urge them to relocate to more resilient planned sites
Rebuild their houses in the same zone without drainage
questions.explanation: Section 3.7 of NST2 urges households in high-risk zones to relocate to resilient sites and rural households to settle in planned settlements.

questions.stem: NST2 plans to increase digital literacy from 53% to:
questions.explanation: Section 3.8 of NST2 targets universal digital literacy so that all Rwandans can benefit from digital transformation.

questions.stem: What does NST2 plan for Umurenge SACCOs in order to improve access to tailored financial services for local communities and small businesses?
options: Consolidate them at district and national levels into a cooperative bank
Convert them into branches of the Ejo Heza scheme
Transfer them to the Rwanda Stock Exchange
Close them and transfer their members to commercial banks
questions.explanation: Section 3.9 of NST2 supports local economic development by consolidating Umurenge SACCOs into a cooperative bank.

questions.stem: According to NST2, which institution is scoping the introduction of a Central Bank Digital Currency (CBDC)?
options: Ministry of Finance and Economic Planning (MINECOFIN)
questions.explanation: Section 3.9 of NST2 says the National Bank of Rwanda is scoping a CBDC to support a cashless economy.

extras.title: Human Capital & Social Development Officer — Mock Exam 6
extras.summary: A mixed-practice mock covering the main areas of this role: social protection, education, health, youth, governance and professional ethics.

sections.name: District plans, reporting and performance monitoring
Youth, gender, disability and inclusion programmes
Data collection, reporting and information management
Civil service values and professional conduct
Sports, innovation, talent detection and delinquency prevention

questions.section: District plans, reporting and performance monitoring
questions.stem: By "vision" we mean:
options: a short-term plan for one year
a long-term aspiration of what a country wants to achieve
questions.explanation: A vision is a long-term aspiration of what a country wants to achieve, as in Vision 2050.

questions.section: District plans, reporting and performance monitoring
questions.stem: Imihigo are:
questions.explanation: Imihigo are performance contracts that leaders and institutions sign and are evaluated on.

questions.stem: SDG 2 aims to achieve:
questions.explanation: Sustainable Development Goal 2 is "Zero Hunger": end hunger, achieve food security and improved nutrition and promote sustainable agriculture.

questions.section: Youth, gender, disability and inclusion programmes
questions.stem: SEDO stands for:
questions.explanation: SEDO is the Cell-level civil-service post of Social (Socio-) Economic Development Officer, advertised under that title by districts through MIFOTRA recruitment.

questions.stem: The African Union replaced the:
questions.explanation: The African Union was launched in 2002 as the successor to the Organisation of African Unity (1963-1999).

questions.section: District plans, reporting and performance monitoring
questions.stem: Rwanda's official languages are:
questions.explanation: Under Article 8 of the Constitution, Kinyarwanda is the national language and Kinyarwanda, French and English are official languages (Kiswahili was added in 2017).

questions.stem: Where is the EAC headquarters located?
questions.explanation: The East African Community headquarters is in Arusha, Tanzania.

questions.stem: Decentralisation aims at:
options: empowering citizens to take part in decision making
questions.explanation: Rwanda's decentralisation policy aims to enhance citizens' participation in initiating, making, implementing and monitoring decisions that affect them by transferring power and resources to local level.

questions.section: Data collection, reporting and information management
questions.stem: According to RPHC 2022 (Fifth Population and Housing Census), the population of Rwanda is:
questions.explanation: The Fifth Population and Housing Census (August 2022) enumerated 13,246,394 residents. The ticked number has two digits transposed.

questions.section: District plans, reporting and performance monitoring
questions.stem: By 2050, Rwanda aspires to achieve a GDP per capita of:
questions.explanation: Vision 2050 targets a GDP per capita of over USD 12,476 by 2050 (high-income status). USD 4,036 is the 2035 target for upper-middle-income status.

questions.section: District plans, reporting and performance monitoring
questions.stem: The following are Imihigo programme ambitious aims, except:
options: Instill a culture of regular performance evaluation
Ensure stakeholder ownership of the development agenda
questions.explanation: Imihigo aims include speeding up implementation, stakeholder ownership of the development agenda, accountability and transparency, results-oriented performance, competitiveness, and instilling a culture of regular performance evaluation. Equitable distribution of resources is not among the stated aims.

questions.section: Data collection, reporting and information management
questions.stem: According to the fifth Rwanda Population and Housing Census, which is the most densely populated District in Rwanda?
questions.explanation: RPHC5 reports Kicukiro as the most densely populated district (2,944 inhabitants per km2), ahead of Nyarugenge (2,830) and Gasabo (2,056).

questions.section: Civil service values and professional conduct
questions.stem: By definition integrity is:
options: the obligation and authority to take the necessary actions to ensure success.
a disposition to be humble; a lack of false pride
the act of consistency of actions, values, methods, measures, principles, expectations and outcome
The spirit of not putting one's self first but being willing to give one's time and resources for the benefit of others
questions.explanation: Integrity is consistency of actions, values and principles, being honest with strong moral principles. The other options define responsibility, humility and selflessness.

questions.topic: District plans, reporting and performance monitoring
questions.section: District plans, reporting and performance monitoring
questions.stem: Which one of the following is not a strategy for mainstreaming cross-cutting issues?
options: Disaster management, environment and climate change
questions.explanation: NST1 names capacity development, disaster management, environment and climate change, and regional integration among its cross-cutting areas to be mainstreamed. "Sequencing of interventions" is not one of them.

questions.section: District plans, reporting and performance monitoring
questions.stem: The Vision 2050 aspirations focus on which of the following broad priorities?
options: Rwanda's progress has been grounded in favorable transformational factors
Increase Citizens' Participation and Engagement in Development
questions.explanation: NST1 states that Vision 2050 aspirations focus on five broad priorities: high quality and standards of life, modern infrastructure and livelihoods, transformation for prosperity, values for Vision 2050, and international cooperation and positioning. Citizen participation and justice are NST1 governance priorities, not these five.

questions.stem: How many Districts with legal personality do we have in Rwanda?
questions.explanation: Rwanda has 30 districts, but the three districts of the City of Kigali (Nyarugenge, Gasabo, Kicukiro) have no legal personality under the City of Kigali law, so 27 districts have legal personality.

questions.topic: Civil service values and professional conduct
questions.section: Civil service values and professional conduct
questions.stem: Which one of the following is not a value linked to unity?
options: Sharing of the first fruits of a harvest
questions.explanation: The values linked to unity are Rwandanness, covenant, conviviality, sharing of the first fruits of a harvest, solidarity, use of Kinyarwanda, love, satisfaction and tolerance. Self-confidence belongs to the values linked to dignity.

questions.section: District plans, reporting and performance monitoring
questions.stem: Fill in the missing: The Vision 2050 was requested by ...........
questions.explanation: Vision 2050 was requested by the 13th National Umushyikirano Council in 2015, after which broad stakeholder consultations were held.

questions.stem: Which one of the following is not a pillar of the national decentralization policy?
questions.explanation: The five pillars of the 2021 National Decentralization Policy are sectoral decentralization and service delivery, fiscal and financial decentralization, capacity development for decentralized entities, local economic development, and governance imperatives for national transformation. Community mobilization is only a priority area under the governance pillar.

questions.stem: As at 2026, who is the head (Chancellor) of the Chancellery for Heroes, National Orders and Decorations of Honour (CHENO), according to its official website?
options: H.E Paul Kagame the President of the Republic of Rwanda
questions.explanation: CHENO's website names François Ngarambe as Chancellor (appointed August 2023); the Chancellor leads the Chancellery and is its legal representative.

questions.section: District plans, reporting and performance monitoring
questions.stem: The pillars of Vision 2050 are:
options: Economic transformation, rural development and accountable governance

Capacity Development, HIV/AIDS and Non-Communicable Diseases, Disability and Social Inclusion, Environment and Climate Change, Regional Integration and International Positioning, Gender and Family Promotion, Disaster Management
Human Development, Competitiveness and Integration, Agriculture for Wealth Creation, Urbanization and Accountable and Capable Institutions
questions.explanation: Vision 2050 has five pillars: Human Development; Competitiveness and Integration; Agriculture for Wealth Creation; Urbanization and Agglomeration; and Accountable and Capable State Institutions. The long list in the second option is NST1 cross-cutting areas.

questions.section: Data collection, reporting and information management
questions.stem: As per the fifth Rwanda Population and Housing Census, which is the least populated District in Rwanda?
questions.explanation: RPHC5 gives the lowest district population as 318,900 residents in Nyaruguru (with Nyabihu close behind). Kayonza, Rulindo and Gisagara are all larger, so none of the three named districts is correct.

questions.section: District plans, reporting and performance monitoring
questions.stem: Which one of the following is a pillar of Vision 2050?
questions.explanation: Vision 2050's pillars are Human Development, Competitiveness and Integration, Agriculture for Wealth Creation, Urbanization and Agglomeration, and Accountable and Capable State Institutions. Solidarity and Dignity (Agaciro) is a shared value, and Economic Transformation is an NST1 pillar.

questions.stem: What is human security as noted in General Assembly resolution 66/290?
options: an approach to assist Member States in identifying and addressing widespread and cross-cutting challenges to the survival, livelihood and dignity of their people
a strategy to assist Member States in identifying and addressing widespread and cross-cutting challenges to the survival, livelihood and dignity of their people
A mechanism fixed to assist Member States in identifying and addressing widespread and cross-cutting challenges to the survival, livelihood and dignity of their people
questions.explanation: Resolution 66/290 says human security is 'an approach' to assist Member States; it does not call it a strategy or a mechanism.

questions.section: Sports, innovation, talent detection and delinquency prevention
questions.stem: Which one of the following is NOT a criterion used by RGB to qualify an innovation as a Home Grown Solution?
options: An innovation that has proved to be a solution to a particular problem
An innovation that addresses a challenge in a new and different way, often through simpler and more effective approaches
An innovation or initiative rooted in the Rwandan cultural heritage and values
A practice imported from another country and applied unchanged, without adaptation to Rwanda
questions.explanation: RGB lists five criteria for a Home Grown Solution, including all four options shown (the post-genocide political philosophy criterion is one of them), so the item has no correct option as written.

questions.section: District plans, reporting and performance monitoring
questions.stem: Every year, the ...... shall determine the priority areas under which joint imihigo should be formulated.
options: National Institute of Statistics of Rwanda
questions.explanation: Law No 18/2017 Art. 9: at the annual planning stage the Office of the Prime Minister specifies the list of priority activities requiring joint planning (joint imihigo).

questions.section: District plans, reporting and performance monitoring
questions.stem: The Imihigo program is based on main objectives. How many are there?
questions.explanation: The Government of Rwanda presentation on Imihigo lists seven objectives: speed up implementation, stakeholder ownership, accountability and transparency, results orientation, innovation and competitiveness, zeal and determination, and a culture of results.

questions.section: District plans, reporting and performance monitoring
questions.stem: The NST1 has considered ... cross-cutting areas to attain inclusive and sustainable development.
questions.explanation: NST1 lists seven cross-cutting areas: capacity development, HIV/AIDS and NCDs, disability and social inclusion, gender and family promotion, regional integration, disaster management, environment and climate change.

questions.stem: How many lakes in Rwanda are shared with neighbouring countries?
questions.explanation: Three lakes straddle borders: Lake Kivu (with DR Congo), and Lake Rweru and Lake Cyohoha South (with Burundi). Lake Ihema and Cyohoha North lie wholly in Rwanda.

questions.stem: The Cabinet of Rwanda consists of:
options: the Ministers and Ministers of State
the Prime Minister, Ministers, Ministers of State and other members nominated by the President
the Prime Minister, Ministers, Ministers of State
questions.explanation: The Constitution says the Cabinet comprises the Prime Minister, Ministers, Ministers of State and other members determined by the President.

questions.section: District plans, reporting and performance monitoring
questions.stem: The law governing results-based performance management in branches of Government is:
questions.explanation: The law is Law No 18/2017 of 28/04/2017 governing Results-Based Performance Management in branches of Government.

questions.stem: After the 1994 genocide, the government of National Unity was established ..........:
questions.explanation: The Government of National Unity was sworn in on 19 July 1994, the date Rwanda marks each year as the start of national unity and reconstruction.

questions.section: District plans, reporting and performance monitoring
questions.stem: Which one of the following is not part of the ambitious aims of the Imihigo programme?
options: Ensure stakeholder ownership of the development agenda
Instill a culture of regular performance evaluation
questions.explanation: The stated aims of Imihigo include speeding up implementation, stakeholder ownership of the development agenda, accountability and transparency, and results-oriented performance. Equitable distribution of resources is not one of them.

questions.section: District plans, reporting and performance monitoring
questions.stem: Which of the following is one of the five pillars of Vision 2050?
options: Human Resource Development and a Knowledge-based Economy
Good Governance and a Capable State
questions.explanation: The five pillars of Vision 2050 are Human Development, Competitiveness and Integration, Agriculture for Wealth Creation, Urbanization and Agglomeration, and Accountable and Capable State Institutions. 'Good Governance and a Capable State' and the other two options are Vision 2020 pillar wordings.

questions.stem: In the implementation of decentralization policy since its adoption in 2001, the following major challenge hindered the effective decentralization processes:
questions.explanation: The policy's list of major challenges includes sectoral decentralization that is yet to foster strategic linkages. Constant development partner commitment and continuous leadership commitment are lessons learnt (strengths), and capacity development is a pillar, whereas the challenge is capacity constraints.

questions.stem: Which one of the following is among the main duties of the socio-economic development officer?
options: To identify socio-economic development needs at the Cell level and accordingly take decision on response measures
To facilitate gathering data related to the employment status within the cell
To prepare and sign documents at Cell level
To elaborate him/her self the programs of community works
questions.explanation: The Cell Socio-Economic Development Officer advertisement lists: identify needs and advise on response measures (not take decisions), prepare documents for the Executive Secretary to sign (not sign them), elaborate community-works programmes under the Executive Secretary's supervision, and facilitate gathering data on the employment status within the Cell.

questions.section: District plans, reporting and performance monitoring
questions.stem: A homegrown solution consisting in pledging to accomplish a certain number of tasks for which someone is held accountable is called:
questions.explanation: Imihigo is Rwanda's home-grown approach of signing performance contracts, in which institutions and leaders pledge targets for the year and are held accountable. Ubudehe is collective action and categorisation, not a performance pledge.

questions.topic: District plans, reporting and performance monitoring
questions.section: District plans, reporting and performance monitoring
questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT a pillar of NST1 (2017-2024)?
questions.explanation: NST1 (2017-2024) had three pillars: Economic Transformation, Social Transformation and Transformational Governance. "Socio-economic transformation" is not a pillar, so as written (A, B and C are all pillars) the item has no single correct option.

questions.stem: To be classified as a National Hero in Rwanda, a person shall meet ..... criteria:
questions.explanation: CHENO lists nine characteristics a person must meet to be classified as a National Hero: integrity, patriotism, sacrifice, vision, bravery, being an example, truthfulness, magnanimity and humanity.

questions.stem: When were the SDGs set up?
questions.explanation: The 2030 Agenda with the 17 Sustainable Development Goals was adopted by the UN in September 2015.

questions.section: District plans, reporting and performance monitoring
questions.stem: Fill in the blanks: As outlined in Vision 2050, by 2050 Rwanda aspires to achieve a per capita income of ...... and a life expectancy of ......
questions.explanation: Vision 2050 targets GDP per capita of over USD 12,476 and life expectancy of 73 years by 2050.

questions.section: Data collection, reporting and information management
questions.stem: The Economic and Human Capital Development Officer has the duty to collect and consolidate data on specific social, health and education programs and prepare the reports. What are the main parts of any formal written report?
options: Title or Cover page - Table of contents - Introduction - Body - Recommendations
Title or Cover page - Introduction - Executive summary - Body - Recommendations - Conclusion
Title or Cover page - Table of contents - Executive summary - Introduction - Body - Conclusion - Recommendations
Title or Cover page - Executive summary - Main content - Conclusion - Recommendations
questions.explanation: A formal report has a title page, table of contents, executive summary, introduction, body, conclusion and recommendations, with the executive summary before the introduction.

questions.stem: What is the Vision 2020 Umurenge Programme (VUP) primarily designed to do?
options: Serve as an integrated local development programme targeting poverty eradication, rural growth and social protection
Provide loans only to registered cooperatives
questions.explanation: VUP is an integrated local development programme aimed at accelerating poverty eradication, rural growth and social protection, targeting households with limited access to assets and income.

questions.stem: Which ministry-linked agency implements VUP, using Ubudehe as its targeting tool?
options: LODA (the Local Administrative Entities Development Agency), under MINALOC
questions.explanation: VUP is implemented through LODA, which operates under the Ministry of Local Government (MINALOC), using Ubudehe categorisation as its main targeting tool.

questions.stem: Rwanda’s Ubudehe categorisation system currently groups households into how many categories, labelled with letters?
questions.explanation: Ubudehe was revised from four numbered categories to five lettered categories, A through E, with A being the highest-income group and E a special category.

questions.stem: What is the main purpose of Ubudehe categorisation?
options: To rank schools by exam results
To socially stratify households mainly by income/wealth level, to target social programmes appropriately
To assign civil servants to districts
questions.explanation: Ubudehe is a social stratification scheme based primarily on household income/wealth, used to target social protection and other programmes to those who need them most.

questions.stem: A household’s circumstances improve substantially over two years of VUP support. What should happen next under the programme’s own logic?
options: Nothing — VUP support never changes once granted
The household should be re-assessed, and if it meets the criteria, it should "graduate" to a higher Ubudehe category and exit VUP support
The household should be removed from all district records
The household should automatically become a VUP official
questions.explanation: VUP is built around a national strategy for sustainable graduation: beneficiaries are reassessed, and improved circumstances should move them to a higher Ubudehe category and off VUP support, freeing resources for others still in need.

questions.stem: Which of these is a core component commonly associated with VUP’s approach to supporting the poorest households?
options: Direct cash transfers and public-works employment for those able to work
Free international scholarships for all participants
questions.explanation: VUP combines elements such as direct support (cash transfers) for households unable to work and public-works employment for those who are able to work, among other components.

questions.stem: What role does the Cell level typically play in VUP and Ubudehe implementation?
options: None — these programmes are run entirely from the national level with no local involvement
Front-line monitoring, data collection, community mobilisation and support for the categorisation and beneficiary-identification process
questions.explanation: Cell-level staff are typically closest to households and play a front-line role in monitoring, data collection, community mobilisation and supporting the categorisation and targeting process that feeds into district and national systems.

questions.stem: A new VUP cash-transfer cycle is about to start. What should a social development officer verify before transfers are confirmed for a given household?
options: Nothing, transfers are automatic once a household is ever registered
That the household’s current Ubudehe category and registration details are accurate and up to date
Only the household head’s name, nothing else
questions.explanation: Because targeting depends on current, accurate household data, verifying the Ubudehe category and registration details before confirming transfers helps ensure support reaches the right households.

extras.title: Human Capital & Social Development Officer — Mock Exam 7
extras.summary: A mixed-practice mock covering the main areas of this role: social protection, education, health, youth, governance and professional ethics.

sections.name: Education, gender, children and disaster management

questions.stem: How many cross-cutting areas does the NST1 have?
questions.explanation: NST1 has seven cross-cutting areas: capacity development, HIV/AIDS and NCDs, disability and social inclusion, gender and family promotion, regional integration and international positioning, disaster management, and environment and climate change.

questions.stem: The SDGs were adopted by all United Nations member states in:
questions.explanation: The 2030 Agenda with the 17 SDGs was adopted by all UN member states at the UN summit of 25-27 September 2015.

questions.stem: All of the following contribute in some measure to reducing the burden of infectious diseases circulating in the community:
options: Safe disposal of faeces (both human and animal)
questions.explanation: Hand and personal hygiene, food hygiene and safe disposal of faeces (human and animal) each reduce the spread of infectious diseases in a community, so "All are correct" is right.

questions.stem: Why should Sector Strategic Plans and District Development Strategies take into consideration HIV/AIDS and non-communicable diseases?
options: Because both are among the cross-cutting areas approved in NST1
Because they are the only diseases affecting development
questions.explanation: HIV/AIDS and non-communicable diseases are one of the cross-cutting areas of the National Strategy for Transformation, which must be mainstreamed in Sector Strategic Plans and District Development Strategies.

questions.stem: What is the relationship between Results-Based Management (RBM) and Imihigo in Rwanda?
options: Imihigo originated from RBM and was translated into Kinyarwanda
RBM is applied through Imihigo, where specific targets are defined to be achieved within a specific period
Imihigo is only a practice used by local government
questions.explanation: Imihigo is Rwanda's home-grown performance-contract tool through which results-based management is applied: targets are set and evaluated each fiscal year, by ministries, boards and districts alike.

questions.stem: Which of the following lists the three pillars of NST1 (2017-2024)?
options: Economic Transformation, Social Transformation and Transformational Governance
Economic Transformation, Social Transformation and Environmental Sustainability
Economic Growth, Human Development and Regional Integration
questions.explanation: NST1 (2017-2024) rests on three pillars: Economic Transformation, Social Transformation and Transformational Governance.

questions.stem: How many cross-cutting areas are included in NST1?
questions.explanation: NST1 has seven cross-cutting areas: capacity development, HIV/AIDS and NCDs, disability and social inclusion, gender and family promotion, regional integration, environment and climate change, and disaster management.

questions.stem: Which of the following best describes Results-Based Management (RBM)?
options: A management approach in which an organisation applies its processes and resources to achieve agreed, clearly defined results that can be measured
A budgeting method that shares funds equally among departments regardless of results
A system for recording staff attendance and working hours
A procurement method for selecting the cheapest supplier
questions.explanation: All three statements are accepted descriptions of RBM: a management strategy/approach focused on performance, in which processes and resources are applied to achieve agreed, measurable results.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT one of the NST1 cross-cutting areas?
questions.explanation: Security Maintenance is not a cross-cutting area; the NST1 areas are capacity development, regional integration, gender and family promotion, HIV/AIDS and NCDs, disability and social inclusion, environment and climate change, and disaster management.

questions.stem: In the context of Vision 2020 and Vision 2050, the term "vision" means:
options: A long-term aspiration of what a country wants to achieve
questions.explanation: Vision 2020 and Vision 2050 are long-term national aspirations, implemented through medium-term strategies such as NST1 and NST2.

questions.section: Education, gender, children and disaster management
questions.stem: When was the National Child Development Agency (NCDA) established?
questions.explanation: NCDA was established by Presidential Order No 083/01 of 28/08/2020.

questions.stem: What does ECD stand for?
questions.explanation: ECD stands for Early Childhood Development.

questions.stem: Which ministry supervises the NCDA?
questions.explanation: NCDA is supervised by the ministry in charge of children, which is MIGEPROF, and MIGEPROF lists NCDA among its affiliated institutions.

questions.stem: What is the main purpose of Rwanda's National Strategy for Transformation 2 (NST2)?
options: To replace Vision 2050 with a short-term development plan
To guide Rwanda's national transformation priorities for 2024 to 2029
To focus exclusively on agricultural development
To address only the challenges experienced during NST1
questions.explanation: NST2 is the five-year government programme for 2024-2029 that implements Vision 2050 priorities.

questions.stem: Which period did Rwanda's first National Strategy for Transformation (NST1) cover?
questions.explanation: NST1 covered 2017 to 2024.

questions.stem: What average annual GDP growth rate does NST2 target over its implementation period?
questions.explanation: NST2 targets an annual average real GDP growth of 9.3% over 2024-2029.

questions.stem: How many jobs does NST2 aim to create over five years?
questions.explanation: NST2 sets a target of creating 1.25 million productive and decent jobs over five years (250,000 a year).

questions.stem: Why is Vision 2050 important to NST2?
options: Vision 2050 provides the long-term direction that NST2 helps implement.
Vision 2050 focuses only on the annual national budget.
Vision 2050 applies only to the private sector.
questions.explanation: NST2 is the medium-term strategy that takes the country closer to Vision 2050, which gives the long-term direction.

questions.section: Education, gender, children and disaster management
questions.stem: A school wants to contribute to NST2's digital transformation agenda. Which initiative would be most appropriate?
options: Restrict students from using digital learning resources
Develop digital literacy and practical ICT skills among learners
Replace all practical learning with memorization
Limit ICT education to students pursuing advanced university degrees
questions.explanation: NST2 digital transformation aims to raise digital literacy from 53% to 100% and build ICT skills among the population including youth.

questions.stem: Which approach provides the strongest basis for evaluating whether NST2 is improving citizens' welfare?
options: Counting the number of policy documents published
Measuring only the amount of money allocated to projects
Counting meetings held by local leaders
Examining indicators such as employment, income, access to services, nutrition, and economic productivity
questions.explanation: Welfare is best judged with outcome indicators such as employment, income, access to services and nutrition, as in the NST2 results framework, not activity counts.

questions.stem: A district wants to prepare an integrated local development plan aligned with NST2. Which proposal best reflects the strategy's interconnected priorities?
options: Develop roads, support agro-processing and local businesses, strengthen skills and job creation, expand productive-use infrastructure, and protect the environment.
Invest exclusively in urban construction while neglecting rural livelihoods and environmental risks.
Focus only on increasing agricultural production without considering transport, markets, or employment.
Concentrate on digital services without addressing infrastructure, skills, or economic opportunities.
questions.explanation: NST2 priorities are interconnected: roads, agro-processing and MSMEs, skills and jobs, productive-use infrastructure and environmental protection.

questions.stem: Who trains Community Health Workers (CHWs) nationwide so they can provide quality services, monitor community health at village level and refer patients to health centres?
questions.explanation: The Ministry of Health leads the community health strategy and builds capacity (training of trainers at district and health-centre level) so that CHWs deliver services to the Ministry's standards.

questions.stem: What is the objective of the Community-Based Health Insurance (CBHI) policy?
options: Mobilising the private sector to support vulnerable people
Providing financial assistance to vulnerable people so they can pay their health-insurance contributions
Providing all citizens with quality, equitable and accessible health services
questions.explanation: The CBHI development policy states its goal as providing the population of Rwanda with universal and equitable access to quality health services.

questions.stem: Which group should receive adequate social protection programmes according to the Government's capacity?
questions.explanation: The National Social Protection Policy says social protection programmes will be adequately provided to eligible beneficiaries within the limits of Government means.

questions.stem: Which responsibility is NOT among the responsibilities of the National Unity and Reconciliation Commission?
options: Educating, mobilising and encouraging citizens to promote unity and reconciliation
Establishing and promoting mechanisms for restoring and strengthening Rwandan unity and reconciliation
Planning and coordinating national programmes aimed at promoting unity and reconciliation
Connecting citizens with public and private institutions
questions.explanation: NURC responsibilities include educating and mobilising citizens, establishing and promoting mechanisms for unity and reconciliation, and preparing and coordinating national programmes; connecting citizens with public and private institutions is not among them.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT a pillar of NST1?
questions.explanation: NST1 has three pillars: Economic Transformation, Social Transformation and Transformational Governance. Three of the four options are pillars, so the stem as captured has no single answer; "Socio-economic transformation" is not a pillar.

questions.section: Education, gender, children and disaster management
questions.stem: Which institution monitors implementation of the National Gender Policy across all sectors of national development?
options: Government institution responsible for monitoring activities
Office of the Government and Ministries
questions.explanation: The Gender Monitoring Office, established by Law 51/2007, monitors the respect of gender principles in national development and in all government, private, NGO and religious organs.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT a good quality of a customer-service provider?
questions.explanation: Impatience is the only option that is not a good quality in a customer-service provider; empathy, problem-solving and communication are.

questions.stem: What are the basic principles of the Health Insurance Policy?
options: Universal access and quality service delivery
questions.explanation: The National Health Insurance Policy lists its basic principles including equity, risk-sharing and solidarity, ownership and partnership, and universality and quality (universal affiliation and high-quality services).

questions.stem: Which of the following is a guiding principle of the Community Development Policy?
options: Monitoring the implementation of poverty-reduction programmes
Understanding how households define their own poverty
questions.explanation: The Community Development Policy guiding principles include collaboration between sectors and partners; the other options are activities, not principles.

questions.stem: What is the name of the national system used to categorise households by socio-economic status for social protection programmes?
questions.explanation: Ubudehe is the home-grown socio-economic categorisation system used to target social protection and other programmes.

questions.stem: How are home-grown solutions defined?
options: Unique Rwandan practices developed by Rwandans, based on domestic opportunities, values and history, to accelerate development
Innovations that solve problems in new and simple ways
Innovations or activities based on Rwandan culture and values
Innovations that have demonstrated their ability to solve a particular problem
questions.explanation: Rwanda Governance Board defines Home Grown Solutions as Rwanda's own solutions developed by Rwandans, based on local opportunities, cultural values and history, to fast-track development.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a specific priority under the Human Development Pillar of Vision 2050?
options: A diversified economy based on the industries of the future
A skilled and competent workforce capable of increasing productivity
questions.explanation: Vision 2050 lists 'a transformed workforce for higher productivity' among the Human Development pillar priorities; the diversified economy and high-end tourism sit under Competitiveness and Integration, and mobility under Urbanization.

questions.stem: At which National Dialogue Council (Umushyikirano) meeting, and in which year, was Vision 2050 proposed?
options: The 13th National Dialogue Council meeting in 2018
The 15th National Dialogue Council meeting in 2018
The 13th National Dialogue Council meeting in 2015
The 15th National Dialogue Council meeting in 2015
questions.explanation: Vision 2050 was requested by the 13th National Umushyikirano Council in 2015.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT an objective of the Imihigo performance-contract programme?
options: Enabling stakeholders to participate in development planning
Ensuring that resources are distributed equitably
Building a culture of regular performance evaluation
questions.explanation: Imihigo aims include stakeholder participation, results-oriented (performance-based) management and a culture of regular performance evaluation; equitable distribution of resources is not among them.

questions.stem: In which year was the Imihigo performance-contract programme introduced?
questions.explanation: Imihigo performance contracts were introduced in 2006 as part of Rwanda's decentralization drive.

questions.stem: Under Law No 18/2017 governing results-based performance management, "medium term" means a period longer than one year but not exceeding:
questions.explanation: Article 3 of Law No 18/2017 defines medium term as more than one year but not more than five years, while long term is a period exceeding five years.

questions.stem: Who monitors the implementation of joint Imihigo under Law No 18/2017?
options: The Ministry in charge of local government
The Office of the Prime Minister
The Ministry in charge of planning
questions.explanation: Article 17 of Law No 18/2017 gives the monitoring of joint Imihigo to the Office of the Prime Minister, because no single organ can deliver them alone.

questions.stem: Under Law No 18/2017, which institution collects the performance-contract implementation reports from all State organs and submits them to the Office of the Prime Minister?
options: The Ministry in charge of local government
The Ministry in charge of public service
The National Institute of Statistics of Rwanda
The Ministry in charge of planning
questions.explanation: Article 18 says supervising organs send their reports to the Ministry in charge of planning, which collects reports from all State organs and passes them to the Office of the Prime Minister.

questions.stem: In the Judiciary, the monitoring of the implementation of performance contracts is the responsibility of:
options: The High Council of the Judiciary
questions.explanation: Article 15 of Law No 18/2017 assigns this task to the High Council of the Judiciary, and in Parliament to the Bureau of each Chamber.

questions.stem: Under Law No 18/2017, how is responsibility for achieving the intended result shared among the organs involved in a joint Imihigo?
options: Equally among all the organs involved
Only by the Office of the Prime Minister
Mainly by the organ in charge of coordination
In proportion to the budget each organ received
questions.explanation: Article 9 states that all organs in a joint Imihigo have equal responsibility for the result, even though a Prime Minister's Order names one organ to coordinate the activities.

questions.stem: Under Law No 18/2017, who determines by order the indicators that State organs use to monitor the individual performance contracts of their staff?
options: The head of each State organ
The Minister in charge of planning
The Minister in charge of public service
questions.explanation: Article 16 says each State organ monitors staff Imihigo using indicators fixed by an Order of the Minister in charge of public service (MIFOTRA).

questions.stem: Choose the false response: under Law No 18/2017, the quarterly and annual monitoring carried out by every State organ must indicate:
options: The number of staff recruited during the year
The expenditures made to achieve the result
The progress attained against each expected result
questions.explanation: Article 15 lists progress against each expected result, expenditures made and challenges faced; staff recruitment is not part of the required monitoring content.

questions.stem: Under Law No 18/2017, a "performance contract of the organ" is concluded between:
options: The head of the organ and its supervising authority
The Prime Minister and the President of the Republic
The head of the organ and its individual staff
questions.explanation: Article 13 provides that the organ's performance contract is concluded between its head and its supervising authority; an individual contract is between a public servant and his or her immediate supervisor.

questions.stem: In the 2024/2025 Imihigo evaluation of districts, MINALOC's scores on human security issues (shelter, sanitation and child malnutrition) account for what share of the final score?
questions.explanation: The NISR report adds MINALOC's human-security score at 20% of the final district score, so the NISR-measured part is 80%.

questions.stem: In the 2024/2025 Imihigo evaluation, citizen participation and satisfaction are assessed by RGB and contribute what percentage to the Imihigo evaluation score?
questions.explanation: Section 3.4 of the report gives RGB-assessed citizen participation and satisfaction a 10% weight in the Imihigo score.

questions.stem: A District includes the construction of a market as an output Imihigo. At the final evaluation the market is 95% complete but not yet usable. How does the NISR methodology score this Imihigo?
options: 95%, in proportion to the physical progress made
0%, because it was not fully completed as planned
80%, based on the share of budget spent
50%, as partial credit for the effort made
questions.explanation: Output Imihigo (classrooms, hospitals, markets) benefit people only when complete, so they score 100% if completed on time and 0% if not.

questions.stem: A District sets an outcome Imihigo of connecting 10,000 households to electricity. At the evaluation, 6,000 households are connected. How is this Imihigo scored?
options: On the progress achieved at assessment time (60%)
0%, because the target was not fully achieved
questions.explanation: Outcome Imihigo (terraces, electricity connectivity, health insurance) can be used progressively, so they are scored on the proportion of progress achieved, here 60%.

questions.stem: Since which fiscal year has the National Institute of Statistics of Rwanda (NISR) been mandated to evaluate Imihigo?
questions.explanation: NISR took over the evaluation of Imihigo from the 2017/2018 cycle to add independence and a rigorous evidence base.

questions.stem: Which district recorded the highest score in the 2024/2025 Imihigo evaluation of districts?
